4- In the midst of the sufferings all men forsook Christ, and there was no helper except the Father; so every person feels that he needs God intensely in the midst of tribulation, so that he is not troubled if people part from him.
12- Many bulls have compassed me: strong bulls of Bashan have beset me round.
Bashan: a region in Gilead lying east of the Jordan River, known for the fertility of its pastures, and therefore for its valuable, strong cattle and bulls.
Beset me round: surrounded me closely.
1- Christ speaks of the wicked who surrounded Him and rose up against Him to crucify Him, and describes them as follows:

a - That their number is very great; for they were from the Jews and the Gentiles, because the priests stirred up the whole Jewish people, and the Gentiles appeared in Pilate and the soldiers under him.
b - That they are strong and overbearing toward Him, resembling the strong bulls of Bashan.

2- And these bulls signify the priests who rose up against Christ, and the elders of the Jews and their rulers, and likewise the whole people, in addition to the fact that they also signify the Gentiles who rose up against Christ and crucified Him.

3- Stray bulls, if they find a stranger, surround him, charge at him with their horns, and try to kill him; just as the Jews, who had strayed from the faith, charged at Christ, who was a stranger to their thoughts, and seized Him and delivered Him to Pilate to crucify Him.
13- They gaped upon me with their mouths, as a ravening and a roaring lion.
Roaring: giving out strong, frightening sounds.

He describes the wicked Jews and the Gentiles who surrounded Christ at His arrest, torture and crucifixion as being like the ravening lion, which gives out strong, frightening sounds in order to pounce on its prey, that is, Christ. This happened when the Jews gathered before Pilate and cried out to him to crucify Him, saying, "His blood be on us, and on our children" (Mt 27:25). The comparison of Satan to a lion is repeated, as in (1 Pet 5:8; 2 Tim 4:17).
14- I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint: my heart is like wax; it is melted in the midst of my bowels.
1- Human nature, by death, dissolves quickly, like the pouring out of water; so Christ expresses the sufferings and the death that will come upon Him and separate His soul from His body.
2- Christ was poured out like water when He prayed fervently in the garden of Gethsemane as He was approaching His sufferings, and His sweat was as great drops of blood (Lk 22:44).
3- When the soldier pierced Christ's side on the Cross, blood and water came out of Him (Jn 19:34) and was poured out on the ground; it is a literal fulfillment of this prophecy.

4- The pouring out of Christ's life on the Cross like water shows the contempt of the wicked Jews for Him, and Christ accepted the shame of the Cross and the pouring out of His life, as something very cheap, out of His love for us, to redeem us.
5- Water poured out on anything washes it and cleanses it; so by the pouring out of Christ's life on the Cross He cleansed those who believe in Him from their sins.
6- When Christ's body was pierced with three nails, the body hung with all its weight on these nails, and this led to the separation of His bones from one another.

7- The separation of Christ's bones does not only mean His death on the Cross, but also means that everyone scattered from Him, as He said to His disciples, "and shall leave me alone" (Jn 16:32), and most of His followers were dispersed, while the Apostles hid in the closed upper room for fear of the Jews (Jn 20:19). And because the Church is the body of Christ, if God's children who believe in Him are scattered and leave Him, they are like the bones in the body that are separated from one another; but at the same time God promises in the Psalm and says of the bones of the righteous that they are not broken, that is, God returns and gathers them again a second time (Ps 34:20).

8- As the sufferings came upon Christ's body on the Cross, so also His inner feelings were sorrowful (His heart melted like wax) over His disciples who abandoned Him, indeed one of them sold Him and some of them doubted. He also grieved over the Jews who persisted in evil. For He feels that all are His children. And this "bowels" of His expresses His womb, which bore all these rebellious sons. But His fatherhood continued to pray for them while He was on the Cross, saying, "Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do" (Lk 23:34).

9- Wax melts by fire and heat, and this signifies that the soul of man is melted by suffering, so that it becomes pure from all evil, and then the image of Christ appears easily in this liquid wax. Therefore the believer does not fear tribulations, because they purify him and bring him near to God, and he becomes a clear image of Christ.
15- My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws; and thou hast brought me into the dust of death. Potsherd: a broken piece of pottery.
1- A potsherd, if placed in the fire, dries out of any moisture in it. Likewise the life of Christ dried up in the furnace of the sufferings and sorrows that He bore.

2- The tongue of Christ cleaved, that is, His mouth from the inside, as an expression of His silence before the many accusations falsely brought against Him by the wicked Jews. He bore all this for our sake and did not answer, because the hearts of the wicked were hard and did not wish to hear, and also as an expression of the suffering of His intense thirst.

3- Christ went down into the dust of death in the tomb, and this is a wonderful humility and great love on His part, that He accepts death, being God, for our sake, we sinners. But death could not hold Him; rather, He rose on the third day. Therefore He said "the dust of death" and not "death", as an expression of His authority over death.

4- The emptying of the will and obedience appear in Christ's submission to the will of the Father, who laid Him in the dust, although this is contrary to His divinity; but He accepted it as a man united with His divinity for the sake of our salvation.
16- For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have inclosed me: they pierced my hands and my feet.

1- David speaks of the wicked Jews, whether the priests, or the scribes and Pharisees, or the people, and likens them to dogs that tear at Christ with their false accusations, their attempts to trap Him in a word, and then their demanding that Pilate crucify Him; by this they followed Satan.

2- By dogs he also means the Gentiles who rose up against Christ, who were the Roman soldiers, and crucified Him. The Gentiles in the eyes of the Jews are considered dogs, as Christ expressed that at the healing of the daughter of the Canaanite woman (Mt 15:26); but when these Gentiles believed they became sons, while the Jews who refused to believe in Christ lost their sonship and followed Satan, so they became like dogs.

3- The Cross is a Roman form of death devised by the Romans to torture criminals, but David the prophet, in whose time there was no use of the Cross, but only hanging on a tree, saw by the spirit of prophecy the Cross of Christ, and described accurately what would happen on it, the piercing of His hands and feet, to be hung on the Cross.

4- The Jews thought that by crucifying Christ and piercing His hands and feet they had deprived Him of the ability to move, and prevented His works and words that exposed their sins. But by these nails He died for us and made the greatest movement in the world, for He saved humanity from its death, gave it new life, and bound Satan.
17- I may tell all my bones: they look and stare upon me.

1- When Christ was scourged, His flesh was torn away and His bones became clearly visible, so it became easy to count and number them, in addition to the fact that He was crucified naked and the Jews stared at Him, so they saw His bones and counted them. And Christ bore the sufferings of scourging and nakedness, and everyone looked at Him, and counted His bones, and despised Him. And He bore all this for us.

2- If nakedness is a result of sin, as Noah was uncovered when he drank the wine (Gen 9:21) and the children of Israel were uncovered when they worshiped the golden calf (Ex 32:25), then Christ accepted to be naked for our sake, that is, He bore our sins and what accompanies them, to clothe us with the robe of His righteousness.

3- When Christ was scourged and His flesh was torn away, His bones remained, and the bones signify the strong believers, while the flesh signifies the weak believers, who fall away before torments, but the bone remains firm in its place.

4- When the Jews and the Gentiles examined the crucified Christ, they found Him being tortured although He was without sin, and because their hearts were evil they despised Him. But some of them had their minds enlightened and believed, because they saw that He was tortured while without sin, such as the right-hand thief, and the soldier who pierced Him with the spear, who is called Longinus, and the centurion who was in charge of the crucifixion.

5- All these sufferings, the piercing of His hands and feet, the counting of His bones, and people's staring at Him, show the perfection of Christ's humanity; He suffered real sufferings, which answer all the heresies that reject the humanity of Christ.
18- They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture.
1- This verse too, which David prophesied, was fulfilled literally, and the Evangelists who witnessed the crucified Christ mention it (Jn 19:23, 24).

2- The garment of Christ, that is, His tunic, was woven as one piece, so the Jews cast lots for it. And this tunic signifies the one faith delivered as a grace to God's children in His Church. And the idea of casting lots means that not everyone will receive this tunic, and this signifies that faith is given only to the chosen, who are saved, while the rest reject it and so do not receive it.

3- And because Christ's garment is the faith, which cannot be divided, all believers accepted it except the heretics, who tore it, such as Arius, who tore the garments of Christ, as Pope Peter, the Seal of the Martyrs, saw Christ in a dream with His garments torn, and He told him that Arius is the one who tore His garments.

4- The garments of Christ signify His teachings, and the soldiers divided them among themselves, and this signifies the spread of Christ's teachings, and the distinction of some believers with certain virtues, and others with other virtues.
19- But be not thou far from me, O LORD: O my strength, haste thee to help me.

1- Christ accepted all the sufferings, but He asks the Father not to be far from Him, for this is the necessary support that every believer in God wants in the midst of sufferings. And therefore he is able to bear the sufferings, and even be at peace and rejoice in God's presence.

2- When He says "O my strength" He declares that God is His only hope and confidence, to be an example for us in our tribulations that we should rely on nothing except the power of God, which is able to solve all our problems.

3- He also says "haste thee to help me", that is, raise me up quickly, and this shows the extent of the sufferings He endures, and His need of a swift resurrection, for this relieves Him of His sufferings and would be a support to His disciples who stumbled and doubted Him.

4- The swiftness of the victory, that is, the swift resurrection on the third day, is a proof of His righteousness and divinity. And this signifies the feelings of the believer who suffers tribulation and needs God to raise him quickly from his sin and lift his tribulations from him.
20- Deliver my soul from the sword; my only one from the hand of the dog.

1- In the midst of the suffering of the Cross, Christ asks the Father to deliver His soul from the sword, and what is meant is the sufferings. This confirms His humanity and His bearing real, hard sufferings. The mention of the sword here is like what Simeon the elder said to the Virgin, that a sword would pass through her own soul, meaning the sufferings (Lk 2:35).

2- By the sword is also meant the divine wrath deserved for the sins of men, which Christ bore on the Cross. And this soul of His is distinguished from the rest of human souls in that it is without sin.
3- By "His only one" Christ also means the Church, so the Father delivers her from the wars of Satan.
21- Save me from the lion's mouth, and from the horns of the wild oxen hear me.
1- Christ also asks on the Cross to be saved from the lion's mouth, meaning Satan, as the Apostle Peter spoke of him (1 Pet 5:8).
2- By wild oxen he means the wicked who take the appearance of the meek, like the tame ox, but in truth are savage and gore with their horns.

Do not be troubled by the wicked rising up against you, but cry out to God who is near you and able to rescue you from their hands. And if He allows you a tribulation, He is beside you, supporting you and giving you peace, and even joy as well.

entries.section: (2) The thanksgiving of Christ the Savior

paragraphs.text: 22- I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee.

1- Christ is the only Son who is in the bosom of the Father, who knows all things, and He alone is able to declare to us what belongs to the Father (Jn 1:18). And He declares to His brethren the name of God and proclaims to them the nearness of the Kingdom of Heaven, because He is the firstborn among many brethren (Rom 8:29). By His brethren are meant His disciples, His followers, and all mankind.

2- The congregation is the Church that Christ founded with His blood. And by His Body and Blood on the altar He offers the greatest praise of love, and the believers in Him share with Him in the hymn of thanksgiving, that is, the sacrament of the Eucharist, which is the Divine Liturgy.

entries.section: (2) The thanksgiving of Christ the Savior

paragraphs.text: 23- Ye that fear the LORD, praise him; all ye the seed of Jacob, glorify him; and fear him, all ye the seed of Israel.

1- Christ asks those who fear the Lord to praise Him, and by those who fear Him is meant everyone among the Gentiles who fears God, for they used to call the devout Gentiles "those who fear the Lord", such as Cornelius (Acts 10:22).

2- He calls the people of God, whom God blessed, as Isaac blessed Jacob, and says to them "ye the seed of Jacob", and asks them to glorify Him, because they know Him and know that He is the only God who deserves all honor and glorification.

3- Christ asks the seed of Israel, who saw God and wrestled with Him and whose name He changed from Jacob to Israel, to fear God and revere Him, since Israel saw God and His majesty, and therefore the fear of Him came to be in his heart.

entries.section: (2) The thanksgiving of Christ the Savior

paragraphs.text: 24- For he hath not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted; neither hath he hid his face from him; but when he cried unto him, he heard.
1- The man fallen into sin, who became poor and in need of God's help, when he cried to Him in lowliness, God had compassion on him, became incarnate, redeemed him, and gave him new life.
2- The poor man is the humble person on whom God has compassion, so He rescues him and lifts him up, as our mother the Virgin declared that He "exalted the humble" (Lk 1:52).

3- Christ our God emptied Himself, taking the form of a servant, and being made in the likeness of men (Phil 2:7), so the title of the poor man applies to Him; all this He did for our salvation. Then His heavenly Father looked upon Him, and after He died and completed our redemption, He rose by the power of His divinity from the dead.
4- The cry of the poor is very precious to God, so He does not hide His face from them but hastens to their help.

5- God distinguishes the humble by showing His face to them, so they enjoy the sight of Him more than the rest of mankind. And seeing the face of God is better than everything in existence, and it is true life. Blessed are the humble, for they enjoy God's reign over their hearts in this age, in preparation for His eternal reign in heaven.

entries.section: (2) The thanksgiving of Christ the Savior

paragraphs.text: 25- My praise shall be of thee in the great congregation: I will pay my vows before them that fear him.

1- Christ the Son says to the Father that just as the Father is praised and glorified, so also the praise and glorification of the Son will be proclaimed after He completes salvation on the Cross, and His resurrection and ascension. And this praise will be in the midst of the great congregation, which is the Church; that is, Christians in their churches praise their Christ, the Savior and Redeemer, after they have believed that He is God, who died for their salvation.

2- Christ pays His vows by offering Himself on the Cross, because He promised the redemption and salvation of His people, and He fulfilled this and paid it on the Cross, and that was before all who feared Him and believed in Him.

3- The effects of the sacrifice of the Cross extend, and we see the carrying out of God's promise to pay His vows on the altar every day, by offering His Body and Blood before those who fear Him, who are the priests of the New Testament, the deacons, and all who believe in Him and fear Him in the Divine Liturgy.

4- The Apostles and all the servants of the New Testament went out to preach the paying of God's vows, that is, His promise of salvation to the whole world, before those who fear Him and have believed in Him, whether from the Gentiles or the Jews, so that they may enter His Church and enjoy His salvation.

entries.section: (2) The thanksgiving of Christ the Savior

paragraphs.text: 26- The meek shall eat and be satisfied: they shall praise the LORD that seek him: your heart shall live for ever.

1- The meek are the humble and those who enjoy inner calm, and what is meant by them is the believers of the New Testament, who are those who cried to God, declaring their need in (v. 24), so He gave them salvation by faith in Him, and gave them also His Body and Blood in His Church, and satisfied them also with His word.

2- The meek are also the poor in spirit, who are the sinners who repented and returned to God, so He gave them His Body and Blood, and satisfied them with His love. And this made them despise the lusts of the world and reject them.

3- These meek, when a relationship is formed between them and God, ask His forgiveness and all their needs from Him, then advance in their spiritual life, so they praise Him and their hearts cling to Him, without any request of their own, but out of love for Him, and then continue in this praise, which always draws them to God, until their whole life turns into continual praise of Him, and through it they taste the Kingdom while still on earth.

4- When the meek eat the Body and Blood of the Lord and praise Him and thank Him and are diligent in partaking of the Holy Mysteries, they abide in Christ and live for ever, that is, they enjoy the delight of life in Christ on earth, and then unspeakable glories in the Kingdom of Heaven.

5- In summary, this verse speaks about the sacrament of Communion; whoever practices it is satisfied by it, and there is implanted in him a constant hunger and thirst for righteousness, so he is diligent in Communion and in everything that binds him to Christ. Then he seeks God in all his needs and renounces the world and does not depend on it. After that his heart is lifted up to the praise of God, and he continues in praise until his whole life becomes a hymn. And finally he receives eternal life in the Kingdom of Heaven.

If God's gifts toward you are continual, then the least you can do is thank Him for them every day, and when you thank Him you will feel the value of these gifts, so your praise and your contemplation of His love will increase, and you will love praise, and become a partner of the heavenly ones in enjoying fellowship with Him.
27- All the ends of the world shall remember and turn unto the LORD: and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before thee.

1- David the prophet speaks by the spirit of prophecy about the New Testament, when the Gentiles believe in Christ and return to Him in repentance, to live with Him. The Gentiles will come to faith from every place in the world.

2- When the believers who come from the Gentiles partake of Communion they rejoice and remember the crucified Christ who saves them, so He changes their lives and they imitate Him, and they come to have an inclination to self-giving and generosity.

3- These converts from the Gentiles remember the name of the Lord, so their trust becomes in Him and they delight in fellowship with Him, because they remember Him every day and at all times, and so enjoy His presence.

4- When these believers remember the name of God and live for Him, their conscience becomes good, that is, they recover the voice of God within them, so He speaks to them of God and establishes them in Him.

5- After this they declare their submission to God and worship Him, so they seek His will and give up their own will, that is, they renounce the world and rejoice in obeying God's commandments, for they find their life in them.
28- For the kingdom is the LORD'S: and he is the governor among the nations.

1- When the peoples of the Gentiles abandoned the worship of idols and all that is connected with it, and submitted to God, He reigns over their hearts, and by His authority over them He gives them to enjoy His fatherhood and care.

2- The natural state is that God reigns over the hearts of men, and sin caused man to lose this blessing, but by repentance and faith man regains God's reign over him. And God will help the Gentiles to repent; for no man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Spirit (1 Cor 12:3).

3- By God's reign over hearts, and His authority, He gives man a strong will able to control his senses, thoughts and feelings, which increases his enjoyment of God's reign over him, so he enjoys fellowship with Him.
29- All they that be fat upon earth shall eat and worship: all they that go down to the dust shall bow before him: and he that hath not kept alive his own soul.

1- The poor in spirit, that is, the repentant humble, who cried out to God and He answered them, and who believed and delighted in His Body and Blood, became fat, that is, spiritually filled with the Holy Spirit, who helped them to submit to God and worship Him.

2- Not only the poor, the needy and those far off will eat of the Body and Blood of the Lord, but also the rich and the great who believe in God, and likewise the saints and those advanced spiritually; all eat and worship and enjoy higher degrees in the emptying of the will and in being satisfied with God.

3- But the wicked who are bound to earthly things and who reject God, and therefore do not enjoy the working of the Body and Blood of the Lord in them, go down and bow and are buried in the dust of the grave, because they refused to keep their souls alive by the Holy Mysteries.

4- The second part of the verse can also be interpreted by applying it to the humble who submit to God, so they worship Him down to the dust in many prostrations (metanoias), and so enjoy fellowship with God, and there joins them everyone who did not keep his soul alive with the pleasures and lusts of the world, that is, who renounced the world.
30- A seed shall serve him; it shall tell of the Lord to the generation to come. 31- They shall come and declare concerning his Lord unto a people that shall be born, that he hath done

1- He adds in this verse that the seed of the Gentile converts will serve God, that is, they will have a strong Church full of youth and vitality, as happened in Egypt, and they will be called children of God, that is, His offspring.

2- Preaching will continue everywhere in the world, telling of God to the generation to come, that is, in the successive generations of the New Testament, so that many may believe and join the Church. And he says in (v. 31) "They shall come" and not "they came", that is, the preaching of Christ will be in the New Testament. And the priests of the New Testament and its servants speak of the righteousness of Christ, which saves sinners from their sins and justifies them.
3- He tells us in (v. 31) of a people that shall be born, that is, a great number that will be born from the baptismal font and become a Church enjoying God's work in her.

4- If the Jews rejected Christ and crucified Him, the Gentiles have believed in Him, but some Jews also believed, and many Jews will believe in Christ in the end, and they will bear a new people for God.
5- If this Psalm began with the sufferings of Christ for us on the Cross, it ends with joy when the name of God the Holy One is proclaimed and many in the whole world believe in Christ.

God wants everyone to be saved, so He calls all to believe in Him. And you, do you call people by your life and conduct to live with God? Your love for all those around you, especially those who wrong you, shows the love of your Christ, so they believe in Him.
God the Shepherd "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want)" ... v. 1) Introduction:
1- Its writer: David the prophet.
2- When was it written?
When David was a shepherd; it is one of the first Psalms that David wrote.
3- When is it said?
At the coronation of kings; it was said on the way between the Temple and the spring of water, so that the king and all the people would remember the following:
a - That the king is of the offspring of David, the writer of this Psalm, who is a type of Christ.
b - That the true shepherd is God, and the instrument He uses is the king.
The newly baptized used to recite this Psalm after receiving the sacraments of Baptism and the Holy Myron, and before their Communion on the night of the Feast of the Resurrection.

4- This Psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayer of the Third Hour, and it points to the work of the Holy Spirit in man, for it is He who supplies his needs, leads him, befriends him, and hosts him. Therefore some of the Fathers call it the Psalm of the Paraclete, because the waters of rest signify the waters of Baptism, and the table signifies the sacrament of the Eucharist.

5- This Psalm is connected with the preceding Psalm, which speaks about Christ the Redeemer on the Cross; whoever believes in Christ the Redeemer receives the blessings of salvation that the Holy Spirit provides in this Psalm.
1- The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
1- David feels that God has shepherded his life since his existence in the world and continues to shepherd him; He is the constant Shepherd of his life, and not only in a particular time.

2- Christ described Himself as the good Shepherd, so the words of the Psalm apply to Christ as the Shepherd of our souls, and at the same time Christ became a Lamb by His Incarnation, to be the firstborn among many brethren, so that He speaks with us, saying that the Lord is shepherd; and every believer sees the fatherhood of God in His being the Shepherd of his life.
3- People in the East were accustomed to call good kings shepherds, because they care for their peoples and show fatherhood toward them.

4- The shepherd provides for his flock all its needs, so that it lacks nothing; so too David found no title to express God's care and His sufficiency for the needs of His children except the title of Shepherd.

5- The more a person trusts in God and empties his own will, the more he feels God's sufficiency for him, and even in tribulations he sees them as for his good, and sees God's nearness to him, so he is not troubled and is assured that He will arrange all his needs for him.
2- He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me to the waters of rest.
He maketh me to lie down: He makes me sit; for the sheep fold their legs and settle on the ground to rest.
He leadeth me: He brings me to the watering places that I may drink.
1- The flock eats of the green pastures and rests in them, secure because of the food available in them, and these green pastures are:
a - The Eucharist, which satisfies God's children, and as they are always bound to it, they remain in continual fullness.
b - The word of God, which nourishes souls.
c - Christ, in whom the soul settles and finds its fullness.
d - The Church, which satisfies her children with her teachings, her rites, her hymns and her praises.

2- After the flock has eaten it needs to drink; therefore the shepherd leads it to the waters of rest, for the sheep cannot go to the water except under the shepherd's leadership. Likewise it is easier for sheep to drink from still water than from running water, so the water of rest is better for the sheep. And the waters of rest are:
a - The work of the Holy Spirit in the soul.
b - The sacrament of Baptism.
c - The work of grace, which is given freely to man for his need.

d - The waters of rest are the waters of the Holy Spirit, of which whoever drinks will never thirst, as Christ said to the Samaritan woman (Jn 4:13, 14), because everyone who drinks of the waters of the world will thirst again.
3- Water washes away dirt, and likewise the waters of the Holy Spirit cleanse man from every sin.
4- Water extinguishes fire and cools heat; so too the waters of the Holy Spirit extinguish the fire of lusts.
5- Water irrigates the earth so that it gives fruit; likewise the waters of the Holy Spirit give the fruits of the virtues.
Look to God your Shepherd, who is able to supply all your needs, so that you are not troubled by any tribulation, even if all the people around you are troubled.
3- He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name's sake.

1- I am liable to be distracted from my Shepherd and to go astray in paths far from Him. But His love does not leave me, so He brings me back from my straying and I walk with the rest of the flock, that is, I return to His Church and His worship and the enjoyment of fellowship with Him. He is not angry with me and does not leave me because of my evils, but His love forgives me and brings me back to life with Him.

2- If I am enjoying the green pastures in which I lie down, but in my ignorance I walk in the way of lusts, that is, the barren wilderness full of thorns, I am wounded by the thorns of sin; but my God guides me in the paths of righteousness, which are holiness, goodness, the virtues and doing good.

3- Christ is the way, the truth and the life, so the paths of righteousness are Christ; that is, He guides me to Himself, because all my straying is a choice of the lusts of the world instead of Christ, and guidance is the return to His beloved Person.
4- Christ, who guides me to Himself, does this not because of my worthiness but by His love, for the glorification of His holy name.
4- Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.

1- The valley of the shadow of death is trials and tribulations. It is not the valley of death but its shadow; that is, a person feels that he is almost dying, that is, the tribulation is very severe, but the sense of God's being with me reassures my heart, so I do not fear any troubles.

2- The shadow of death signifies bodily death, while by true death is meant spiritual death, that is, eternal perdition. Therefore the meaning of the verse is that during our life in the world until its end in death we fear no evil, because God is with us; indeed bodily death leads to a release into eternal life.

3- The sense that God is with me not only reassures my heart but comforts it and makes it patient in sufferings, and more than this, as I feel God's love I rejoice and taste the Kingdom while I am on earth.
4- God's presence with me makes me fear Him, and then I keep away from every sin and do not fear it, nor people, nor problems and the changes of life.
5- The rod and the staff signify the Cross, since both are made of wood, and the shepherd uses them in his hand to shepherd his flock and take care of it.
6- The rod protects the flock by gathering the straying and striking the wolves and all the enemies of the flock, so it is protection from Satan and all his tricks and violence.

7- The shepherd leans on the staff, and it signifies divine support in the spiritual life, so that even if a person is weak, by leaning on the staff he continues his way toward the Kingdom and acquires the virtues.

8- The shepherd uses the rod and the staff to lead his flock, that is, by looking to the Cross we reject all evil, and offer our lives in self-giving love and find our salvation. In short, we find in the Cross all that we desire, and in the end it gives us comfort and joy.

9- The thickness of the rod of discipline varies according to the sheep's endurance; it is slender to suit the weak sheep, and thick for the stubborn and arrogant. In addition, the rod can turn into a staff and the staff into a rod according to need. The weak needs support, while the careless and stubborn needs discipline until he repents.
10- The staff is useful in old age; so too in spiritual old age and lukewarmness God supports with His grace.

11- The staff is useful if a person walks in darkness, for it guides him to the road and protects him from dangers. So too when consolations disappear and God hides Himself, even for a little while, we lean on the sacraments of the Church and the means of grace, and they guide us to the way of the Kingdom.

12- The rod is for discipline and the staff for support and help, but both are in the hand of God the Father, the tender Shepherd of our souls, who uses them for our salvation; they comfort us, that is, they give inner peace, and then the Kingdom of Heaven.

God loves you and is ready to lead your life, so surrender yourself to Him, because His will is your salvation, whether He allows you a tribulation or gives you support; but in the end you are in a faithful hand that brings you to the Kingdom.
(3) My host (vv. 5, 6:)
5- Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of them that trouble me: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup is full.
Full: watered, or filled.

1- The table is the altar of the New Testament, where the Body and Blood of the Lord are offered, and it satisfies the souls of believers. And God offers it to His children and sets it before them every day, that they may be satisfied with His love.

2- The table is also my bodily needs, which God arranges for me as long as I am occupied with seeking the Kingdom, so I am not troubled about any need, because God shepherds me and satisfies me materially and spiritually.

3- God's arrangement of my spiritual and material needs is in front of those who trouble me, that is, my enemies the demons, so I do not fear them, because God is with me, and He declares His support for me at a table over which Satan has no authority. And he cannot take away my peace and my sufficiency, because they are from God.

4- The table is one, which is the altar of the New Testament, which Solomon's Temple and the Tabernacle of Meeting signified. And the Body and Blood of the Lord are offered on this table in every place to everyone who believes in Him.

5- The anointing of the head with oil is a clear reference to the sacrament of the Holy Myron and the descent of the Holy Spirit, which begins with the anointing of the head, which is very important because it contains the mind, and then extends to anoint the rest of the members.

6- Priests, prophets and kings were anointed with oil by its being poured on their heads, and it is a reference to the sacrament of the priesthood in the New Testament, where the Holy Spirit anoints them, to lead the Church and perform the Holy Sacraments.

7- It was the custom in ancient times to place oil and perfume on the table, so that the guest would be anointed with them. And the anointing of the head signifies joy, for the one who fasts, as Christ commanded, anoints his head, to hide his asceticism and express his spiritual joy. And the host used to pour oil on the heads of the guests, as Christ mentioned in the house of Simon the Pharisee when He met the sinful woman. So anointing the head with oil represents honor, and offering love to others so that their souls rejoice.

8- Anointing with ointment or oil was used in ancient times to treat and soothe wounds, and God wants to heal our pains and remove our sins from us; He heals the diseases of our souls and bodies by His Holy Spirit, as happens in the sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick.

9- The cup is the cup of Christ's blood on the table of the New Testament, which waters the souls of believers completely, so that they do not need the waters of the world, that is, they rise above earthly things and are not troubled by their changes.

10- In ancient times shepherds used to fill large cups made of stone, into which they put water from the springs, so that the sheep might drink from the cups, and they kept pouring water into the cups so that it would be cold; and this signifies the renewal of the work of the Holy Spirit in souls, for He gives them coolness, peace and gifts renewed every day.

11- The cup signifies the cup of wine that gladdens whoever drinks it, and this signifies the work of the Holy Spirit, who makes the soul drunk with the love of God, so it rejoices and forgets the material things around it, that is, it rises above material things and is occupied with divine love.
6- Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.

1- If a person walks in the way of God, as the verses of this Psalm mention, then in the end God grants him goodness and mercy all the days of his life, that is, He forgives him his sins, finds excuses for him, and blesses him with many good things.

2- Goodness and mercy are perfected in the Person of Christ; that is, whoever lives with Christ, Christ rejoices in him and seeks him and fills his heart. Christ follows him, overtakes him, and dwells in him throughout his life, because this person declared his love and submission to God.

3- Christ grants the one who loves Him and responds to Him to dwell and settle in His house throughout the days of his life; for although this person has a private dwelling and a job, the time he spends in the house of the Lord is the delight of his life, and his heart clings to the Church and her teachings and settles in her, so that he is satisfied and enlightened, and becomes a light to the world in every place he goes to. In ancient times they used to pray the prayer of the Prime in the church and then go to their work, and when they returned from their work they prayed the prayer of the Vespers in the church; that is, they began the day with the blessing of the Church and ended it by standing before God and being satisfied with His love, to return joyfully to their homes.

The Church is the house of God your heavenly Father, who rejoices to see you in His house and blesses you. So cling to the Church and all that is in her as much as you can, and you will receive unspeakable grace and blessing. God the King of Glory. Of David. A Psalm: "The earth is the LORD'S, and the fulness thereof" (v. 1). Introduction:
1- Its writer: David the prophet.
2- When was it said?
David the prophet said it when he brought up the ark of the covenant of God from the house of Obededom to Jerusalem (2 Sam 6:12-17).
3- David wrote it by the spirit of prophecy about the founding of Solomon's Temple, to be said when the ark is brought up to it.
4- It is said on returning from any victory in war with the enemies.

5- There is a relationship between Psalms 22, 23 and 24. The first speaks about Christ the Savior, the second about Christ the Shepherd, and the third about Christ the Glorified. These three Psalms also represent the hymn of Golgotha, then the hymn of the redeemed Church, and after this the hymn of heaven.

6- This Psalm is messianic, speaking about Christ ascending to heaven in order to raise us up with Him; therefore this Psalm is said in the rite of the New Testament Church on the Feasts of the Resurrection and the Ascension.

7- The title of this Psalm in the Septuagint is "for the first day of the week", because this Psalm used to be recited on the day after the Sabbath, that is, Sunday, which is the first day of the week. And this represents in the New Testament the day of the Resurrection, on which Christ rose, triumphant over death.

8- The manner of reciting this Psalm in the Old Testament was that those entering the Temple say (vv. 1, 2) all together with one voice, to proclaim the power of God, the Creator of the whole universe. After this the leader of the group entering the Temple says the third verse, asking about the conditions of the one who enters the house of God. After this the gatekeeper answers from inside the house of the Lord, declaring the conditions of the one who enters the house of the Lord, which are the two verses (vv. 4, 5). After this the leader of the group outside the house of the Lord says the sixth verse, declaring the blessings of the one who enters the house of the Lord, then continues and asks the guards to open the gates for the King of Glory, and recites the seventh verse.
The guard inside the house asks who the King of Glory is, in the eighth verse. The leader of the group from outside replies, declaring His attributes in the ninth verse.
The gatekeeper returns from inside and asks the same question, that is, who the King of Glory is, in the first part of the tenth verse.
The Church in the New Testament took up this rite, and recites part of it on the Feast of the Resurrection and calls it the play of the Resurrection, reciting verses (7-10).

9- This Psalm is found in the Third Hour in the Agpeya, in which we celebrate the descent of the Holy Spirit, because the seas and the rivers in (v. 2) signify Baptism, and the Psalm also shows the work of the Holy Spirit in those entering the house of the Lord.
The earth is the LORD'S, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.

1- He declares that God is the Creator of the earth and all the creatures on it, and therefore He has authority over all mankind. It is natural that they should worship Him. But whoever turns away from Him and worships idols is a strange person in his thinking, because there is no creator but God; how then can a person leave his Creator?

2- This verse comforts the Jews who were captive far from Jerusalem and Judea: the whole earth belongs to God, and not only Jerusalem and its surroundings; therefore the captives can lift up their prayers to God from the captivity.
3- This verse is a prophecy about the Church of the New Testament, where people from all the regions of the earth and from various places believe in Christ.

4- Every person imprisoned in a jail, or exiled, or facing any tribulation or injustice, is comforted that his God owns the whole earth, so he is encouraged and prays, confident in the power of his God, who rescues him, protects him and satisfies him, as happened with Jeremiah while he was in prison, when God called him to stand and pray and be comforted (Jer 33:3).
For he hath founded it upon the seas, and established it upon the rivers.

1- God founded the earth upon the seas and the rivers, which signify trials. He founded it strong, such that trials cannot prevail against it as long as it holds fast to Him. And He does not let trials be beyond a person's strength, and He makes with them the way of escape.

2- The seas and rivers also signify the Holy Spirit and the Holy Sacraments, especially the sacrament of Baptism; and God founded His Church on the Holy Sacraments and the work of the Holy Spirit, and gave those who believe in Him the ability to live in His house, whose characteristics will appear in the following verses.

3- Rivers water and moisten the earth and make it able to grow crops, and help creatures to live by drinking from them. That is, God takes care of the needs of men, His children, and puts in the seas and rivers the fish from which man benefits.

4- God founded the earth upon the seas, and it is a miraculous work that it should be firm upon the moving seas and rivers; and therefore God's children are assured that they are firm in Him, however the affairs of life around them may change.

5- The rivers signify the disciples, the Apostles and the priests, the servants of the New Testament, who convey the work of the Holy Spirit to the believers, so that their souls are watered and satisfied and live with God powerfully.

Be at ease throughout your life, because you are in a faithful hand, the hand of God, the Almighty and Creator of all, and do not be troubled by tribulations, because they are by His permission for the growth of your life and your being approved before Him. Hold fast to your faith and your prayers, and you will pass successfully through all tribulations.

entries.section: (2) The conditions for entering the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: Who shall ascend into the hill of the LORD? and who shall stand in his holy place?
1- The hill of the Lord is the one on which God's Temple was built in Jerusalem, and what is meant is: who deserves to offer worship acceptable before God? And the holy place is the Temple.

2- The holy place is the Church of the New Testament, and the hill is Christ, the head of the body. And what is meant is: what are the necessary qualities of the one who ascends the hill and stands in the holy place?

3- The one who has received the sacrament of Baptism, as we mentioned in (v. 2), is the one able, by the new nature, to ascend the hill and stand in the holy place, that is, to stand in the Church and partake of the Holy Sacraments. And standing also means steadfastness, that is, to be a firm pillar in the house of the Lord.

4- Ascending is from earthly things to heavenly things, and the hill represents steadfastness, that is, he grows in steadfastness in Christ. And the process of ascending is continuous, because Christ the hill has no end. And it is not possible to ascend to the fullness of the stature of Christ, that is, upon the hill, except with the help of grace.

entries.section: (2) The conditions for entering the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart; who hath not lifted up his soul unto vanity, nor sworn deceitfully.
1- The first condition for entering the house of the Lord is cleanness of hands, that is, having pure, clean works, which have no purpose except pleasing God and the salvation of the souls of others.
2- The second condition is purity of heart; for works to be clean, the intention of the heart must be pure, otherwise the works become superficial, for show, to please people and not God.

3- The third condition is keeping away from everything that is vain, such as the gatherings of the world and its works, however prevalent they may be. As long as they do not please God and do not lead to the salvation of the soul, they are vain.

4- The fourth condition is that a person's will be good, so that he lifts up his soul to good things and not to vanity. And according to how strong his spiritual will is, he will grow in the knowledge of God and his relationship with Him.

5- The fifth condition is truthfulness and faithfulness in dealing with others. In the Old Testament he swears truthfully, or in the New Testament he is truthful in his promises. But whoever swears or promises with deceit and lying is a son of the devil, the liar and the father of lies, even if he has an appearance of piety and a position in the Church, or even in her service. And whoever seeks the truth and rejects vanity from his heart will of course be faithful in his dealings with others, and will not deceive anyone or lie to him.

entries.section: (2) The conditions for entering the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: He shall receive the blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God of his salvation.

1- The one who has the preceding qualities receives a blessing from the Lord. What is meant by the blessing is all the divine gifts, spiritual, psychological and material, so he is in spiritual fullness and in need of nothing material, because God arranges his needs.

2- The one who has these conditions also receives righteousness, that is, a pure life and mercy through the forgiveness of his sins, the finding of excuses for him, and support in his spiritual and material striving, so he is successful in all that his hands undertake, as the first Psalm says, "whatsoever he doeth shall prosper" (Ps 1:3); and besides the blessing and righteousness he receives divine salvation, so he lives the life of salvation, far from sin and enjoying fellowship with Christ, in preparation for his departure to the Kingdom of Heaven.

3- The One who receives all the blessings and all the righteousness is Christ, God incarnate. And at the same time He is the source of the blessings and mercy that He poured out on those who believe in Him by His Incarnation; He alone is without sin, as He said to the Jews, "Which of you convinceth me of sin?" (Jn 8:46).

4- Whoever ascends to the hill of the Lord receives blessings; he is poor and has nothing to give, but his striving toward the house of the Lord and his seeking God give him countless blessings, and he receives Christ Himself through His most holy Body and Blood, and He dwells in his heart for ever.

entries.section: (2) The conditions for entering the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: This is the generation of them that seek him, that seek thy face, O Jacob. Selah.

1- Whoever holds fast to the preceding conditions seeks the face of Jacob, or the face of the God of Jacob as in the Septuagint translation; for what is meant is that just as Jacob saw God, so whoever seeks the Lord wants to enjoy seeing the face of God. Although this is impossible for man because of the loftiness of God, God in His humility showed Himself to Moses, and to everyone who strives toward Him and loves Him, like all the saints in the New Testament.
2- Those who seek the face of Jacob are those who walk as Jacob walked in the way of perfection (Gen 25:27).

3- As Jacob received the blessing of the birthright, so everyone who ascends to the hill of the Lord and seeks Him receives the blessings that Christ, the firstborn among many brethren, grants him, so he receives the blessings of salvation in the New Testament in the Church.
4- The one who seeks the face of God means that he longs and strives, that is, struggles; he is not content with the inner desire but supports it with spiritual striving.

5- At the end of this verse we find the word Selah, which is a musical pause; that is, the preceding verses speak about those prepared to enter the house of the Lord, while the following verses tell us about Christ the victorious, glorified King.

God loves you and sought you by His Incarnation, and still seeks you every day; therefore He rejoices greatly in your striving toward Him in response to His love. Your striving in all the spiritual practices, even if with compulsion, is very precious to God.
Lift up your heads, O ye gates; and be ye lift up, ye everlasting doors; and the King of glory shall come in. Gates: the portals and entrances.

1- The angels who witnessed the Incarnation of Christ and ministered to Him on earth (Mt 4:11) knew that He is God; therefore they ascended with the spirit of Christ so that He might enter heaven, and called to the angels who guard the gates of Paradise, or the Kingdom, to lift up and open these gates so that Christ, the King of glory, may enter.

2- Christ does not need the gates to be opened for Him, because He is God, who fills every place, and no one hinders Him, but He speaks as a man, because He is the firstborn among many brethren. He represents the new humanity ascending to enter Paradise and the Kingdom; therefore it was necessary to announce to the angels standing at the gates of Paradise and the Kingdom that a human being would enter, namely Christ, God incarnate.
3- He says "lift up" and not "open", because Christ by His Incarnation bowed the heavens and came down, so when He ascends the gates are lifted up.

4- These everlasting doors are, of course, not the doors of the Temple of Jerusalem nor the temple of the Church of the New Testament, but they are everlasting doors that were closed from of old, from the days of Adam when he was driven out of Paradise, and now they are opened that Christ may enter. The everlasting doors mean that they are not material doors, and also that they are from a long time ago, that is, from everlasting.

5- These gates signify the gates of the heart of man and the gates of his senses, which should be lifted up to heavenly things, so that Christ may enter into them and dwell, and man may enjoy His work in him. And He says "lift up your heads", meaning that human beings should lift their heads toward heaven to behold God, that is, love prayer, praise and contemplation.

6- He says gates and doors, and not a single door, to declare that there are many heavens, or degrees in heaven, which human beings enter according to their striving and the work of grace in them. Christ, God incarnate, enters all these and opens them, so that all who believe in Him may enter after Him, each according to his degree.
Who is this King of glory? The LORD strong and mighty, the LORD mighty in battle.

1- The angels who guard the gates of heaven asked, saying: Who is the King of glory? For they are sure that it is forbidden for any human being to enter Paradise since it was closed in the days of Adam; so who, then, is this King of glory?!

2- The angels ascending with the spirit of Christ answered them and declared to them that the King of glory is not merely a man, but is the mighty Lord, God become man, and they of course know God, so they opened the gates at once.

3- The mighty Lord is Christ our God, who by His might bound Satan on the Cross, so that he no longer has authority over God's children to take them to Hades; rather, by Christ's opening of Paradise as a victorious bearer of good news He gives a chance to all human beings who believe in Him to enter heaven, which had been closed before them.

4- What the angels ascending with the spirit of Christ said, that is, "the Lord mighty in battle", is the same expression with which Moses began his song after crossing the Red Sea (Ex 15:3), which was a type of what Christ would do in the fullness of time, by His victory over Satan and his binding on the Cross, which the angels ascending with the spirit of Christ announced to heaven.
Lift up your heads, O ye gates; even lift them up, ye everlasting doors; and the King of glory shall come in.

1- He repeats here what he said in (v. 7); so what is the reason? Did the angels who guard the gates of heaven not understand? Of course not. They certainly understood that this is Christ, the mighty Lord. But he repeats the same words here because the angels ascending with the spirit of Christ rose to another, higher heaven and asked the angels who guard these second gates to lift them up. Perhaps the first heaven is meant to be the Paradise of Joy, and the second heaven the Kingdom of Heaven.

2- We should not be surprised if some angels know that this is the spirit of Christ and others do not. There is understanding among the angels, and different abilities, as we see in (Dan 10:12-14), where we find that Gabriel was speaking with Daniel, and likewise the angel appointed over Persia, but Satan, referred to as the prince of Persia, stood before Daniel to hinder him from his service, and there the archangel Michael intervened and drove Satan away from Daniel's way.

3- The angels mentioned as guards of the gates do not include archangels, such as Michael and Gabriel, because these had knowledge of the Incarnation of Christ; for Gabriel is the one who gave the good news to the Virgin, and Michael is the one who announced the Resurrection and sat on the stone after it was rolled away. The meaning of this is that there was a group of angels, such as the archangels, who knew about the matter of redemption, but they were not proud of their knowledge, and the angels who did not know this matter were not grieved. Rather, all were in joy at receiving the ascending Christ.
Who is this King of glory? The LORD of hosts, he is the King of glory. Selah.

1- For the first time in the Old Testament the expression "Lord of hosts", that is, Lord of the armies, or Lord Sabaoth, is used; it is an expression particular to the Father, but the Son is described by it here because of His victory over Satan and his binding.

2- The expression "Lord of hosts" or "Lord of the armies" is mentioned because Christ by His authority, after His victory over Satan, reigns over the hearts of His children and gives them a place with Him in Paradise, and then afterward in the Kingdom.

God wants to reign over your heart; He completed redemption and died on the Cross for one purpose, which is to free you from your sins and give you a place with Him in heaven. So do not be troubled because of your weakness and your falls, but rise quickly, repent, and ask for His help, and He will free you from sin, even if you fall dozens of times every day.
The school of prayer. Of David. "Unto thee, O LORD, do I lift up my soul" (v. 1). Introduction:
1- Its writer is David the prophet.
2- Why was it written?
Because of David's suffering from the pursuit of Saul and Absalom and everyone who wronged him.
3- When did he write it?
In his old age, because he mentions the sins of his youth (v. 7).
4- Its idea:
A prayer lifted up before God, containing a clear example of acceptable and complete prayer before God; it is considered a school of prayer from which a person learns how to pray.
5- It contains wise sayings, truths of the faith, and guidance for walking in the way of God; it is one of the wisdom Psalms and shows God as the Teacher of man in all aspects of his life.
6- This Psalm is considered a personal lament, as it expresses the feelings of a person who feels loneliness and the multitude of enemies against him, and his clinging to God his Savior.
7- This Psalm is among nine Psalms written according to the Hebrew alphabet, and these nine Psalms are 9, 10, 25, 34, 37, 111, 112, 119, 145.
8- This Psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayer of the Prime.
Unto thee, O LORD, do I lift up my soul.

1- Lifting up the soul means drawing near to God, who is exalted above all creatures, and this is done by lifting up the mind and the heart through thinking about lofty things, that is, heavenly things and every spiritual matter, so that the mind and the heart are occupied with the knowledge of God and the spiritual virtues. The body can also be lifted up, as in the lifting up of the hands; that is, the soul is lifted up by prayer and contemplation. Therefore the priest says in the Divine Liturgy, calling to the people, "Lift up your hearts."
2- Lifting up the soul is rising above earthly things and being occupied with them, so that a person is content with using material things in the measure of the necessary needs.

3- Lifting up the soul is by rising above the sins that humble man and put him in a place of lowliness, and not only rising above sins but above their causes, that is, keeping away from the sinners who make the soul stumble and from evil gatherings.
4- If a person humbles himself before God, He lifts him up, because He exalts the humble (Lk 1:52); so whoever strives for humility lifts up his soul.
2- O my God, I trust in thee: let me not be ashamed, let not mine enemies triumph over me.
3- Yea, let none that wait on thee be ashamed: let them be ashamed which transgress without cause.

1- David's enemies, such as Saul and Absalom, tried to attack him and kill him without cause. But in faith he lifted up his soul to God in prayer and trusted in Him, and his heart was assured that God would keep him.

2- The enemies of David, and the enemies of all believers, are the demons, and the sins into which they try to make people fall. So David, as a believer trusting in God, asks that He deliver him from them, so that they do not triumph but, on the contrary, are put to shame.

3- David does not mean by the shame of the treacherous revenge on them, but he means the manifestation of divine truth and justice, so that those who believe in God and all who pray to Him and wait for His deliverance are assured. And on the contrary, the wicked take notice and return to God by repentance.
4- Shew me thy ways, O LORD; teach me thy paths.
5- Lead me in thy truth, and teach me: for thou art the God of my salvation; on thee do I wait all the day.
1- The ways and paths are God's commandments, the Holy Bible, the life of Christ on earth, and the lives of the prophets, the Apostles, the martyrs and the saints, which we ought to imitate.

2- Being shown and taught the ways and paths of God requires the spirit of spiritual discipleship at the hands of the father of confession, the Fathers, and spiritual brethren. And by persevering in discipleship a person finally acquires the learning of the spiritual ways.

3- The truth is God, and training in it is spiritual striving and all the spiritual exercises in which we must persevere, so that our knowledge of the ways of God is not theoretical knowledge but we live it practically.

4- We have no savior in all our tribulations and needs except God, so we do not trust in anyone else, even if we have all human means. And we continue to pray and seek God throughout our lives, because "the day" means the whole lifetime. We wait for God all the day and every day. And we wait for Him by persevering in prayer, reading and every spiritual striving, confident that He is able to rescue us from our tribulation and guide us to His Kingdom.
6- Remember, O LORD, thy tender mercies and thy lovingkindnesses; for they have been ever of old.
7- Remember not the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions: according to thy mercy remember thou me for thy goodness' sake, O LORD.
1- David reminds God of His readiness to have mercy on His sinful, weak children; that is, he entreats Him to pour out His mercies upon him. And this humility brings an overflow of God's mercy.

2- David also reminds God of His promises to redeem humanity, the promises that He declared in Paradise to Eve, that her seed would bruise the serpent's head (Gen 3:15). And these promises show the divine love that has been toward man from eternity, before God created him, and then was manifested in his redemption.

3- David asks God to forget the sins of his youth, that is, those he committed when he was a beginner in his life with God, with his knowledge of sin limited, so that He finds an excuse for him and forgives him these sins.

4- Likewise he begs God not to remember his transgressions, which are his sins when he was grown and knew that his sin was disobedience to God, and he asks God to forgive him them by His mercy. And David's remembering of God's mercies encourages him to confess his sin, because before God's judgment every person fears and trembles and cannot speak.

5- David reminds God of His richness in love and His generosity, that is, His goodness, that He may pour out upon him not only forgiveness but also kindness and blessings, that God may support him in the pure life with Him; for he says to Him "remember me", that is, look at my sonship and that I am a man created by Your hands and in need of You, and have compassion on me and do not look at my sins.

How beautiful it is for a person to humble himself before God and ask for His mercies, for God is very tender toward all the weak and the poor who ask Him, and pours out upon them love with a fatherhood that surpasses the mind.
8- Good and upright is the LORD: therefore will he teach sinners in the way.

1- God is good, indeed wholly good, and He is upright, with no sin or deviation in Him, and He wants all His children to become good. And He does not desire the death of the sinner; therefore He teaches His children goodness and uprightness.

2- He calls four classes of His children and guides them, and the first of these classes is sinners, so He guides them to the straight way so that they leave their sins and return to the way of God. And this is by His commandments and teachings, or by removing sin from them, or by showing its hideousness so that they reject it.

3- The word "teach" here in the Hebrew original means teaching the commandments, and what is meant is that He teaches sinners His commandments, explains them to them, and convinces them of them, so that they reject their evil thoughts, which led them to sin.

4- The Lord is tender; so in spite of His knowledge of the sins of His children, He gives them a chance to repent, as He did with the woman caught in adultery: He did not condemn her or stone her, but after forgiving her He guided her not to return to sin.
9- The meek will he guide in the truth: and the meek will he teach his ways.

1- He makes the meek know the truth, that is, He makes them know Himself; for the meek are those who enjoy inner calm, and therefore they have a greater readiness than others to know God and to understand His purposes, because they are quiet like God, not attached to the world, and are not troubled by any gain or loss.

2- The meek are humble, because meekness and humility are two virtues connected together; therefore the meek, by his humility, is ready to learn faster than others, and God pours out His knowledge upon him.

3- In His guidance of this second class, the meek, God is not content only to guide them, but also trains them practically in walking in the truth, so that they live the commandment practically in their lives.
4- God teaches the meek His ways, and His ways are the virtues, so He teaches them how to acquire every virtue and makes them grow in it.
10- All the paths of the LORD are mercy and truth unto such as keep his covenant and his testimonies.
1- God's way of dealing with His children is mercy toward all the repentant, and at the same time it is truth and justice toward all the stubborn and careless.

2- God's mercy appears first in His coming, when He offered His salvation on the Cross, and we enjoy this mercy in our present life. But truth and justice appear in the Second Coming of Christ, that is, the Day of Judgment, on everyone who did not make use of the period of life for repentance.

3- The third class that God teaches is those who keep His covenant and His testimonies; everyone who cares about and keeps and holds fast to God's covenants and promises and believes in them enjoys mercy, and these are what God repeated in the Holy Bible, and he demands them from Him in prayer with persistence, so he receives them and rejoices in them.

4- God's testimonies are His commandments, and they are also the lives of the fathers in the Holy Bible, and the lives of the prophets and Apostles, and they are also the prophecies of the prophets and the teachings of the Apostles in the New Testament. And everyone who keeps them and holds fast to them, God's mercies are poured out upon him.

5- God's mercy also includes His kindnesses, as in the Septuagint translation, that is, His gifts, His support of His children, and His various blessings that He grants to His children so that they remain holding fast to His commandments. And they are, even more, His spiritual gifts, that is, His revealing of Himself to those who keep His covenant and His testimonies, because experiencing God and feeling Him in this present life is the greatest encouragement to bear the pains of spiritual striving.
11- For thy name's sake, O LORD, pardon mine iniquity; for it is great.

1- God's name means His mercy, His goodness and His fatherhood, to which He referred in the preceding verse. And because of David's faith in the name of the merciful God he dared to confess his sins and ask for forgiveness.
2- When David kept God's covenants and testimonies his mind was enlightened and he felt the greatness of his sin, so he asked for repentance and the forgiveness of his sins.

3- David the prophet feels the greatness of his sin and that he does not deserve forgiveness, and all his good works do not give him a sufficient excuse. But his hope is only in the name of God, so his reliance is on God's grace. And this shows the extent of David's humility, and therefore God pours out upon him forgiveness and many mercies.
12- What man is he that feareth the LORD? him shall he teach in the way that he shall choose.

1- The fourth class that God teaches is those who fear Him. When David says "What man is he that feareth the LORD?", he shows that those who fear the Lord are very few, but they exist, and they alone are saved; because the fear of God makes them keep away from sin, and know God, and enjoy His love and the sense of Him.

2- If God finds a person who fears Him He hastens to him and teaches him the right way that He chooses for him, which is the way of life, the way of the Kingdom; that is, He guides him to keep His commandments and live with Him.

3- If a person fears God but has strayed from the right knowledge because of any strange teachings, yet is sincere in the fear of God, God will not leave him, as He appeared to Saul of Tarsus and guided him to the faith (Acts 9:1-19); and if he is far from the knowledge of the truth, He sends someone to guide him, as He did with Cornelius the Gentile, and sent to him the Apostle Peter, who taught him and those with him, and they believed and were baptized (Acts 10:19-33).
13- His soul shall abide in goodness; and his seed shall inherit the earth.

1- Whoever fears God, God pours out upon him material blessings and many good things in the world, so that he lacks nothing; he lives his day, and sleeps with good things abundant around him, as He did with Abraham, who believed in God and feared Him and left the world for His sake, so He blessed him in the wilderness and gave him material goods sufficient for all his life.

2- Among the most important of God's blessings to those who fear Him is that He blesses their seed, so that they inherit the earth; that is, God's blessings extend to the seed of those who fear Him, because the seed learned the fear of God from the fathers, so they receive a blessing and many good things also, as happened with Isaac and Jacob and the people of Israel, who inherited the land of Canaan as a free gift from God.

3- The person who believes in God and fears Him not only abides in material good things but, rather, in spiritual good things, that is, he settles in the bosom of God, and feels His presence, and enjoys fellowship with Him and all the virtues.

4- Spiritually also, the seed of those who fear God inherit the earth, since by their fragrant conduct they draw others to life with God, so they inherit many souls for God. This is what happened with God's people anciently, when some of the Gentiles believed and joined it, and it appeared clearly in the New Testament, when many from the various countries of the world believed in Christ at the hands of the Apostles and the believers.
14- The secret of the LORD is for those who fear him, and his covenant is to teach them.

1- After explaining two gifts that God gives to those who fear Him, namely that he abides in good and that his seed inherits the earth, he declares here a third gift, which is that He grants them His secret. By His secret is meant many blessings that they do not expect, so He solves their problems in a way that surpasses the mind, and gives them spiritual and material blessings, and grants them His peace in their hearts, so they are distinguished from all people by this inner peace.

2- The secret of the Lord is the knowledge of Him, for there is nothing greater than knowing God and enjoying being with Him closely. And in the New Testament He revealed wonderful secrets about Himself when He made clear His Holy Trinity. And in every generation He makes those who fear Him know Himself, as He appeared to Moses in the bush and spoke with him throughout his life, and as He spoke to David and Solomon, and then His work grew greater in His Incarnation, and the declaring of His secrets to His disciples and all who believe in Him in the Holy Bible.

3- The fourth gift that God gives to those who fear Him is that He declares His covenant to them, and the declaring of His covenant means the fulfillment of His promises; for all His covenants are enjoyed only by those who fear Him, whether they are material or spiritual promises, as He declared that through Moses at Mount Gerizim (Deut 11:29), and declared it again through Solomon at the dedication of the Temple (1 Kgs 8:22-53). And He declared it in the New Testament in His Sermon on the Mount (Mt 5-7) and His talks with His disciples and His intercessory prayer (Jn 14-17).

4- Those who fear God are His close children, indeed His friends, so He rejoices to share with them as friends, as He did with Abraham and shared with him in the decision to burn Sodom and Gomorrah (Gen 18:17).

5- God's covenant to teach those who fear Him is His teaching them the way of the Kingdom, that is, He teaches them His commandments, and how to walk uprightly, keep away from sin and hold fast to their faith, so that they receive the eternal inheritance.
15- Mine eyes are ever toward the LORD; for he shall pluck my feet out of the net.

1- The fifth gift that God gives to those who fear Him is that He delivers them from the snares of the devil, that is, his net. Though the devil is deceitful and strong, God is stronger than he and able to rescue those who fear Him, so they do not fear the wars of the devil, and live always at ease.

2- In order for a person to enjoy this gift he must always lift up his eyes toward God, and this is by prayer, so that he lives in what is called constant prayer, that is, he seeks God throughout the day. It does not mean that he does no work, but that he accustoms himself to lift up his heart as much as he can to God in prayer, so he lives at ease, in addition to his enjoyment of seeing God and fellowship with Him, so he lives the Kingdom while on earth.

3- God in His fatherhood takes care of those who fear Him, so He rescues their feet from the devil's nets, even if they do not ask Him, because they sometimes do not understand and do not know the devil's tricks, but God knows and rescues them, and keeps the nets away from them; and even if they fall as a result of negligence, God in His tenderness visits them for the salvation of their souls.

God guarantees you a life of ease, indeed full of joy, if you live in His fear. For the fear of God is a fortress that protects you from every evil and gives you happiness. Remember God at all times by prayer, and you will live in His fear.
16- Turn thee unto me, and have mercy upon me; for I am alone and poor.
Alone: solitary.
1- Before the multitude of the devil's wars David feels that he needs the five preceding gifts of God, and asks Him to have mercy on him and rescue him from these wars, and to save him if he falls.

2- David feels that his only hope is in God's looking upon him and His care for him, so he says to Him, "Turn thee unto me." And as long as God is looking at him, he is at ease, however much evil surrounds him.

3- David declares that he is alone and poor and in need of God's mercy, and by this humility David receives from God all that he needs; he did not rely on being a king or a military commander, nor did he rely on any resources he had, but he relied on God alone; therefore he lived at ease.
4- By this prayer David is freed from the feeling of loneliness or isolation, and this grace is considered the sixth gift that God grants to those who fear Him.
17- Relieve the troubles of my heart; bring thou me out of my distresses.

1- David is exposed to feelings of distress that assail his heart as a result of many events that pass over him and close in on him, almost choking him; therefore he asks God to relieve him, and remove from him these feelings of distress, and give his heart rest.

2- He also asks God to bring him out of the problems he meets in his life, and all the distresses that pass over him through his dealings with others, since he trusts in God's power, which is able to bring him out in peace from all troubles.

3- David is an example of the spiritual person who fears God; he does not live an easy life but one full of problems, and the devil fights him more than others because he walks uprightly, but he is distinguished from others by God's care for him and his inner peace, because God is with him.
18- Look upon my lowliness and my weariness; and forgive all my sins.

1- The seventh gift that God gives to those who fear Him is the forgiveness of their sins, which is the greatest grace, because by it a person's life is renewed so that he becomes pure after being rid of his sins, however hard they were. And by this a person triumphs over his first enemy, which is sin, that is, the inner enemy.

2- The condition for obtaining forgiveness from God is lowliness, that is, humility, and the sense of weariness, that is, the feeling of need for God; whoever feels his need and humbles himself holds fast to God and is persistent with Him, so God has mercy on him and forgives his sins.
19- Consider mine enemies; for they are many; and they hate me with unjust hatred.

1- David also takes refuge in God to rescue him from his outward enemies, who are the demons, and everyone who submits to Satan and walks in the way of evil and wrongs God's children, and this is the eighth gift. But God's power is greater than any power in the world; therefore when David takes refuge in God he is assured that God will save him from all his enemies.

2- The difficulty of the situation is in the multitude of enemies, but their multitude is worthless, because God's power surpasses all their power. But the multitude of enemies made David hasten to God and ask for His help.

3- The strange thing is that the enemies hated David although he was innocent. He was wronged, but he did not doubt and did not leave his upright way. And on the other hand his heart was not troubled so as to try to take revenge on his enemies, but he trusted in God, surrendered his life to Him, and kept his peace.
20- O keep my soul, and deliver me: let me not be ashamed; for I put my trust in thee.

1- David asks God to keep him in all his ways, whether he sees the enemies or does not see them. For God knows everything, and is able to keep His children from every evil and from all the devil's hidden tricks, so that God's children walk at ease in their present life and do not fear the future.

2- When David discovered the plots of the wicked he also asked God to rescue him from them, and this confirms his faith in God's power, love and care for him. And his confidence appears in that he is assured he will not be put to shame, that is, the enemies will not prevail against him, because he trusts in God.
21- Let integrity and uprightness preserve me; for I wait on thee.
1- The ninth gift that God gives to those who fear Him is perfection, so He adorns them with every virtue, and they strive in the way of perfection, imitating their perfect God.
2- David is confident that however much he is exposed to problems, or even in his weakness falls into sin, he still waits for God and hopes in Him, confident of His care for him.
22- Redeem Israel, O God, out of all his troubles.
