1- David's love for all his people Israel appears when he asks God to redeem them and rescue them from every tribulation; he feels his membership in the community, that is, his oneness with all his brethren, and feels their feelings. The verse also shows David's fatherhood, for he asks on behalf of all his people, for whom he feels responsible.

2- David sees that his salvation is accomplished together with the salvation of the rest of his brethren from the people of God, and he is not isolated from the rest of the believers, and God's complete salvation includes him and the rest of his brethren.
3- By the spirit of prophecy David sees the redemption of Christ that will be accomplished in the fullness of time, when Christ redeems the new Israel, that is, all who believe in Him.
If only you would feel for all your brethren in the Church and pray for them, for God rejoices in your love and gives you and them abundant blessings.
The life of uprightness. Of David. "Judge me, O LORD; for I have walked in mine integrity" (v. 1). Introduction:
1- Its writer: David the prophet
2- When was it written?

a - When David was fleeing from the face of Saul, and Saul was accusing him at that time of betraying his people, rejecting the house of the Lord, and taking refuge in dwelling among the wicked, that is, the pagans, although he was compelled to flee because Saul wanted to kill him. And he wrote this Psalm to defend himself.

b - When Ishbosheth the son of Saul was killed by two of his servants (2 Sam 4:5-12) and the Jews accused David of killing him, he wrote this Psalm in defense of his uprightness and to prove his innocence.
c - When David fled from the face of Absalom he wrote this Psalm, because of his sense of being wronged, and he wanted to prove his uprightness.
3- When is it said?

The priests used to recite it when washing in the house of the Lord, before offering the sacrifices, to remember the purifying of their hearts before serving the Lord, and to declare before those entering the house of the Lord the conditions for entering this place, that is, purity and uprightness.
4- This Psalm is one of the messianic Psalms, because it speaks about Christ, who is without sin, and yet was accused unjustly and bore it for us.
5- This Psalm shares with the seventh Psalm and the seventeenth Psalm that in all these Psalms David defends his innocence.
6- This Psalm speaks about the persecuted Church, or about any person who walks uprightly with God and is exposed to injustice and false accusations.
7- This Psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayer of the Third Hour, in which false accusations were brought against Christ.
1- Judge me, O LORD; for I have walked in mine integrity: I have trusted also in the LORD without wavering.
Without wavering: with steadfastness and without being shaken.

1- David says to God, "Judge", that is, judge, O God, with justice; for You are different from unjust men, You are just and know the secrets of hearts, that is, You know my innocence. It is a taking refuge in God by prayer, that He may rescue him from the words of the wicked.

2- David declares his innocence of the accusations brought against him, and shows his walking in integrity, that is, in God's commandments, and by integrity he means the relative perfection that God allows him. This is not pride on David's part but a defense of his innocence.

3- Before the false accusations David had nothing to do but take refuge in God, trust in Him and abide in Him, because He is the only true refuge of all who are wronged. And this proves his humility and that he is weak and took refuge in God to defend him, and therefore by his saying "in mine integrity" he does not mean that he trusts in his own righteousness.
4- David's taking refuge in God answers the accusations brought against him that he left the house of the Lord and joined the pagans.
5- David's walking in integrity declares the purity of his heart and his forgiveness of those who wronged and abused him, such as Saul and Absalom.
2- Prove me, O LORD, and try me; purify my kidneys and my heart.
1- David accepted the trials that came upon him and did not murmur or ask why these trials, unlike Job, who protested against God, and this shows David's submission to God.

2- David asked God to try him with these trials, not meaning that God should know his purity, for God knows everything. But he means that God should try him so that David may know himself and discover his faults in order to treat them by God's power, just as gold is tested by fire to rid it of dross, or impurities; therefore David said "purify" my heart and my kidneys, that is, the depths of my soul, so that it may be perfectly pure.
3- The word of God examines man and tries him and reveals the secrets of his heart, that he may be purified from all evil.
4- David's saying "prove me, try me, purify" declares his confidence in the purity of his heart toward those who wronged him, and his readiness, if any evil is found, that God purify him from it.

5- The kidneys and the heart are inner organs, so they represent the depths of David that he seeks to have purified, especially since the kidneys purify the blood of toxins, and the heart distributes the pure blood to nourish all the organs of the body. So if the kidneys and the heart are examined and purified, the whole person is pure.
3- For thy lovingkindness is before mine eyes: and I have walked in thy truth.
1- David always looks to God's mercy, so he is then able to accept trial and bear it, because God's mercy supports him and strengthens him.
2- When David looks to God's mercy he remembers God's care for him throughout his life, that is, that God's mercy was always with him, so his heart is assured, and he even praises God.
3- David's walking in the truth gives him courage to come forward asking for God's mercy, because God has mercy on His children who keep His rights.

4- David's declaring his walking in the truth is a defense of himself against the accusations that he separated from the people of God and refused worship in the house of God. He was compelled to flee from the face of Saul, but he holds fast to the rights of God and His commandments.

5- David's thinking is directed toward God; he walks in His truth and asks for His mercy, and has no feelings against his enemies. He does not ask God to vindicate him at their expense, or to punish them, but is concerned with his inner purity and the salvation of his soul. And this is the conduct of God's children.
4- I have not sat with vain persons, neither will I go in with dissemblers.
5- I have hated the congregation of evildoers; and will not sit with the wicked.

1- They accused David of living among the pagans and separating from the people of God, and David affirms here his goodness and righteousness in that he did not mingle, and also kept away from the wicked and hated their evils; that is, even among the pagans he took care to sit with God's righteous children, who accompanied him in his flight.
2- David declares his keeping away from sinners in every form; he kept away from
a - vain persons
b - dissemblers
c - evildoers
d - the wicked

3- David not only kept away from the wicked, but also from his heart hated and rejected evil in all its forms, and his heart was not attached to it; that is, he kept a heart pure toward God, as in the preceding verse he asked for God to examine his heart that it might be pure.

4- David refused to mingle with the dissemblers, who pretended to piety but whose hearts were full of evil. And this shows David's carefulness about those with whom he mingles, and God's guidance of him.

Be careful about those with whom you mingle; for if they are God's children they will be an encouragement to you on the way of life with God. And if they are among the wicked, keep away from them, even if you have an old relationship with them. Do not gamble with the salvation of your soul and your eternity out of shyness before these wicked friends or relatives.

entries.section: (2) Proof of his love for the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: 6- I will wash mine hands in innocency: so will I compass thine altar, O LORD:

1- David said "I will wash mine hands in innocency" because he looked with his heart at what happens in the Tabernacle of Meeting, where the priests wash their hands in the laver before offering the sacrifices for the people; he longs in his heart to share with the priests in washing his hands, to be purified from every sin. And although he is far from the Temple because of his flight from the face of Saul, his heart is attached to the worship offered in the Temple.

2- The hands signify works, so David's washing his hands in innocency means the purity of his works from all evil, since he did not mingle with the pagans around him and did not share with them in their sins.

3- The priests used to go around the bronze altar before offering the burnt offerings and sacrifices upon it. And the one who offered the sacrifice shared with the priest in going around the altar. And David longs to be in the Temple, to go around the altar on which sacrifices are offered for the forgiveness of sin. He longs for God to forgive him his sins.

4- Washing the hands is a well-known ancient custom, by which a person demonstrates his innocence of any charge that may be attributed to him. So David's washing his hands in innocency is a declaration of his innocence of the charges brought against him, which are his mingling with the pagans and his rejection of worship in the Temple.

5- Washing the hands for us in the New Testament takes place in the sacraments of Baptism and confession. As for going around the altar, the priest and the deacon do it in the Liturgy on behalf of the people in circuits accompanied by prayers, and it declares the bond with the altar and the readiness to receive the sacrament of Communion. And the priest recites this verse when he washes his hands during the Liturgy, to declare the purity of his heart, so that he may be able to touch the Body and Blood of the Lord.

entries.section: (2) Proof of his love for the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: 7- That I may publish with the voice of thanksgiving, and tell of all thy wondrous works.

1- David continues in his longings toward the Temple, and while far from it he hears the sounds of praise offered to God (thanksgiving), which the Levites chant. And if the Levites are silent, he hears in the spirit the praises of the angels around God who dwells in His Temple. And he longs to share with them in praising and thanking God.

2- When David hears the praises his heart is moved, so he shares with them by mentioning the wonders of God, that is, he thanks God for His kindnesses, praises Him, and declares his attachment to the worship of God and his separation from the worship of the pagans.
3- David's hearing the voice of praise (thanksgiving), in spite of his distance from the Temple, is evidence of his purity, his strong relationship with God and his distance from sin.

entries.section: (2) Proof of his love for the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: 8- LORD, I have loved the habitation of thy house, and the place where thine honour dwelleth.
1- David always thinks of the house of the Lord, which is the Tabernacle of Meeting, and therefore his heart was attached to it and loved it, so it became the most important thing in his life.

2- David sees God dwelling in His house with great glory, so he was occupied with Him instead of all material things and the glories of the world, and his longings for Him increased, and he lived in it in the spirit, even if he was far from it in the body.

How beautiful is your attachment to the house of the Lord, as you behold in it His glory and enjoy His presence, not only when you partake of the Holy Sacraments but also at times when there are no liturgical prayers; for the Church is always full of the glory of God and His saints.
9- Gather not my soul with sinners, nor my life with bloody men:
10- In whose hands is mischief, and their right hand is full of bribes.

1- David asks God to separate him from the wicked, who commit sin and are hard of heart, so they shed the blood of the innocent and pervert justice by bribery. He means that his heart and feelings be separated from them, that he may live for God in his thought, feelings and works.

2- David means above all that his place on the Day of Judgment be far from the wicked, that is, that he enjoy eternal life with God far from eternal torment; because he separated from the wicked on earth, he asks for separation from them in eternity.

3- David was not concerned with the accusations brought against him that he mingled with the wicked and kept away from God, but his whole concern was God's look at him and what God sees in him; as long as God is pleased with him and knows the purity of his heart, he has his place in the Kingdom.

4- David did not ask for revenge on the wicked, or on those who falsely accuse him, or for any position on earth, or earthly lusts. His only concern was his relationship with God and his place in the Kingdom.
11- But as for me, I will walk in mine integrity: redeem me, and be merciful unto me.

1- His request in the two preceding verses was negative, that is, his asking to keep away from the wicked. But here he makes a positive request, which is to obtain divine redemption and mercy, because he is a sinner and in need of God's mercy and forgiveness.

2- In spite of David's being among the wicked, he walked in his integrity, that is, in God's commandments. And he does not mean his walking in integrity as a boast, because immediately afterward he asks for God's redemption and mercy, out of his sense that he is a sinner; but he only means his holding fast to God's commandments, so that no one may stumble because of him.

3- David affirms here that salvation is accomplished by God's redemption and mercy, and not only by human striving and walking in integrity; rather it becomes clear that God's mercy and redemption are granted to those who strive spiritually, and are not granted to the slothful.
12- My foot standeth in an even place: in the congregations will I bless the LORD.

1- When David asked for God's redemption and mercy, God granted him peace, although he was excluded and a fugitive and did not enjoy seeing the house of the Lord, but he felt rest, as if he were standing on a plain and not among the mountains and heights.
2- The even place signifies the way of the Kingdom, in which God set David. And this confirms David's assurance, which drives him to spiritual striving until he reaches heaven.

3- David longs to stand in the midst of the congregations coming to worship God in the Tabernacle of Meeting, and this means David's attachment to the house of the Lord. And this verse shows the importance of communal prayer in the Church.

4- This verse shows David's love for the whole world; he longs that they believe in God and gather together to praise Him (the congregations), and this includes the Jews who believe in God, and signifies the believers in Christ in every place, who pray and praise God, who redeemed them on the Cross.

5- This verse shows the faith of David, who felt that his request was answered, and that he stands on an even place and in the midst of the congregation and blesses God, although he is still scattered and a fugitive in the wildernesses.

Be careful to love all people, but keep away from the wicked in their gatherings, their works and their words, so that you keep the purity of your heart, gain God's good pleasure, and then obtain your place in heaven.
Faith in the Lord the Savior. Of David. "The LORD is my light and my salvation" (v. 1). Introduction:
1- Its writer is David the prophet
2- When was it written? There are two opinions:

a - When David was fleeing from Saul. This is evidenced by what is written in the title of this Psalm in the Septuagint translation, where it is said, "A Psalm of David before he was anointed." It is known that David was anointed king three times: the first when he was sixteen years old, secretly in his father's house, the second when he reigned over the tribe of Judah in Hebron at the age of thirty, and the third when he reigned over all the tribes of Israel at the age of thirty-seven (1 Sam 16:13; 2 Sam 2:5: 3). And what is meant by "before he was anointed" is before his anointing at the age of thirty, that is, the second time. Thus David wrote this Psalm during his flight from the face of Saul.
b - When he was fleeing from the face of Absalom his son.
3- This Psalm suits the righteous person who faces tribulations, or the Church suffering persecutions; it is a Psalm that comforts and strengthens God's children during their tribulation.
4- This Psalm shows God as a strong fortress for His children, and that He is able to save them from all tribulations.

5- This Psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayer of the Prime; it is a Psalm that strengthens God's children at the beginning of their day, when they remember the Resurrection of Christ, so they rise with Him in power and go out to their lives with vigor and confidence.
1- The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?

1- David, who believes in God, feels that He is the light of his life, and therefore purifies him from all the darkness of sin, so he leaves all evils. Therefore when a person prays this Psalm at the beginning of the dawn of the new day he feels that God is the true light that illumines his life.

2- David also feels that God is his Savior from all his tribulations, so he fears no enemy however strong; for who can stand before God, who is able to do all things? It is a wonderful confidence and faith inside David's heart, which gives him complete assurance. And no one can utter these words except one who has trusted in God and emptied himself and humbled himself, so that he can feel the strong hand of God, which overcomes all enemies.

3- David believes that his taking refuge in God by prayer is like his entering a fortress that cannot be stormed, so he laughs at his enemies, and they are terrified of him, while he does not fear them or tremble before them.

4- David has experienced God's work in his life; therefore he says my light, my salvation, and the stronghold of my life; and so we find him speaking with surpassing confidence. And because he enjoys God's presence continually, fear cannot come near him.
2- When the wicked, even mine enemies and my foes, came upon me to eat up my flesh, they stumbled and fell.

1- David declares that he was exposed to attack by the wicked; he passed through many tribulations that brought him to the point of death. But he says with confidence that the wicked wanted to eat his flesh, but they cannot reach his spirit; their authority is limited, that is, only over the body. Therefore he does not fear them, as Christ said, "Fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell" (Mt 10:28).

2- In spite of the cruelty of the wicked and their attempt to destroy David, they were not able to, but stumbled and fell, that is, they failed in their attempt to destroy him, and their weakness also appeared before him, as Saul fell into David's hand twice while pursuing him, but David spared him and did not kill him (1 Sam 24:6, 1 Sam 26:11, 12).
3- David, when his enemies stumbled and fell before him, signifies Christ, before whom His enemies fell when they came to arrest Him in the garden of Gethsemane (Jn 18:4-6).
3- Though an host should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear: though war should rise against me, in this will I be confident.

1- David's faith appears in his assurance if an army attacks him or war rises against him. He did not specify the kind of enemy, or his weapons, or his strength, because he relies on God, who is able to defeat any enemy or any army.

2- These words also apply to spiritual warfare; if the armies of the demons, or various kinds of wars, rise against the spiritual person, his heart is not troubled, because of his confidence that God is stronger than Satan, and God is able to expose his tricks, and has authority over him, so He always gives His children the victory.

Persevere in your spiritual striving, and do not be troubled by the devil's wars or the multitude of your falls, for in the end you are guaranteed by God's power the victory over Satan. Hold fast to your spiritual rule, and humble yourself before God and people, and the devil will be shattered before you.
(2) The house of the Lord is my fortress (vv. 4-6).

4- One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to gaze intently in his temple.
Gaze intently: look carefully, or examine.

1- Although David suffers many pains and needs while he is pursued from the face of Saul, or Absalom, he did not ask anything of God except to dwell and settle in the house of the Lord. And this clearly shows that he is a spiritual person whose heart is attached to the love of God before everything.

2- David's longings are not only to offer worship to God in His house, or to pray before Him, but his heart longs to dwell and abide in the house of the Lord, to enjoy being constantly in His hands; he declares his constant need of God.

3- The beauty of the Lord that David wishes to behold is the sense of His presence, His fear, and the feeling of the holiness and purity that are in His house; he does not mean fine, beautiful sights in the house of the Lord, but the sense of His presence. The gazing is not at the beauty of the Temple, because David knows well everything in the Temple, but he examines the attributes of God who dwells in the Temple, such as holiness and purity, in order to live and thank God for His support of him throughout his life, so his attachment to Him increases.

4- The concern of David the prophet for the house of the Lord appeared not only in these words but also in his concern to bring the ark of the covenant of the Lord back to Jerusalem (2 Sam 6:1-6). And when God refused that David build a house for the Lord, and said to him that his son Solomon is the one who would build the house, he then hastened to prepare the building materials of gold, silver, timber and all the needs (1 Chr 22).

5- It was not the custom of the priests or the kings to dwell permanently in the house of the Lord, but David's heart's attachment to the house of the Lord made him wish to dwell in the house of the Lord, in order to live with God, and suffer every day in His holiness; he is not content with offering worship and performing the religious rites, but wants always, every day, to contemplate the beauty of God. And if he cannot dwell in the house of the Lord as a building in which he stays, then at least he dwells there spiritually, that is, he always feels his presence in God's hands, while dwelling in any place.
6- David's longings to dwell in the house of the Lord are not limited to the Tabernacle of Meeting, but he longs to be in the presence of God in heaven, to enjoy the beauty that cannot be expressed.

7- David wants to dwell in the house of the Lord to worship Him at all times, because those devoted to worship, such as Simeon the elder and Anna the prophetess, are the ones who stayed in the house of the Lord (Lk 2:25-40), and this shows his love for the worship of the Lord.

8- David's love of dwelling in the house of the Lord and beholding and gazing intently in His temple implicitly declares his love for communal worship; although he loves individual prayer and prays seven times a day, he also loves praying with his believing brethren in the house of the Lord.
9- David wished to dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of his life. This shows two things:
a - His great love for prayer and for being in the house of the Lord.

b - His sense of the luminosity of being in the house of the Lord; therefore he said the days of my life and not the nights of my life, and this agrees with the beginning of the Psalm, when he said "The LORD is my light"; he feels God as the light of the world when he stands before Him in His temple.
5- For in the day of evil he shall hide me in his canopy: he shall cover me with the covering of his tent; he shall lift me up upon a rock.

1- The canopy is what they set up during war for the king to sit under in the midst of his army, with a group of mighty soldiers around him to protect him. So David declares here that God is the one who hid him and protected him in the canopy, using the soldiers, and this shows the extent of David's vision of God and his faith that He is his fortress.

2- During the day the heat in summer is intense; therefore a person takes refuge in the tent to be sheltered inside it, and in the rainy winter he also hides in it from the rain and the cold. And David feels that God shelters him in the tent; indeed David also shelters in God's tent, in which is the ark of the covenant, when he takes refuge in Him by prayer, fortifying himself by prayer in His tent.
3- The rock signifies Christ, that is, the strong God, who cannot be penetrated, so when David fortifies himself upon it his enemy cannot reach him.

4- David represents the spiritual person who progresses in his spiritual life: he hides in the canopy, which covers his head, then shelters inside the tent where people do not see him, because he is within the embrace of God. And in the end he reaches the rock upon which he is lifted up, which is the complete, firm fortress that the devil cannot penetrate, because the rock has no doors or windows.

5- The canopy and the tent signify the Incarnation of Christ, who hid His divinity in our body that is subject to change by death, like the canopy and the tent that are moved from place to place. And our hiding and our enlightenment in Christ is accomplished through our partaking of His Body and Blood; He hides Himself under the appearances of bread and wine to give us the greatest power in the world that gives us victory over all our enemies.

6- When Moses desired to see God, He hid him in a cleft in the rock (Ex 33:22), and then he enjoyed seeing God and his face shone. So everyone who takes refuge in Christ the Rock receives the sight and vision of God, that is, he experiences the Kingdom while on earth.

7- When God's people thirsted in the wilderness of Sinai and were exposed to death, Moses struck the rock, and it brought forth water and the people drank. And the Rock was Christ, as the Apostle Paul said (1 Cor 10:4); so whoever takes refuge in Christ is watered by the work of the Holy Spirit in him.

8- The canopy, the tent and the rock signify the Church; the Church is a canopy in which the believer hides from the arrows of the enemy, and he shelters in the tent from the heat of the day, that is, trials, and is lifted up upon the rock, that is, enjoys God's work in him.
9- The rock signifies the strong, firm faith that we enjoy if we always live in Christ.
6- And now shall mine head be lifted up above mine enemies round about me: therefore will I offer in his tabernacle sacrifices of shouting; I will sing, yea, I will sing praises unto the LORD.

1- Since David experienced hiding in the Lord's canopy, sheltering in His tent, and then being lifted up upon His rock, he cried out in faith, declaring that God has lifted him above his enemies, that is, given him victory over them, and honored him with great honor. So he moved from a weak person needing protection to a person strong in God, receiving honor before people and triumphing over those who try to wrong him; that is, he became confident in himself, and thankful to God, who made him great.

2- When he felt God's grace upon him in the victory and the honor, he hastened to offer thanks to God in the form of peace offerings, which are sacrifices of shouting, and they are sacrifices that express man's love for God, accompanied by the blowing of trumpets, and offered at certain feasts. Likewise shouting and trumpets go before the soldiers returning victorious from war; therefore shouting accompanies the sacrifices (Num 10:10).
3- The sacrifices of shouting that we offer in the New Testament to God, who gives us victory in our spiritual wars with the demons, are in the form of:
a - Prostrations (metanoias) of thanksgiving.
b - Humility before God and people.
c - Offering services to those around us.
d - Offering help to the poor and needy.

4- In the end David declares his joy in the Lord by singing and chanting, that is, praising God in His house and in every place as an expression of his thanks to God. And this is what we do in the New Testament in the sacrifices of praise, and by this we pass from the bloody sacrifice to the sacrifice of the Eucharist, which is a sacrifice of thanksgiving and praise to God, accompanied by many praises.
Be steadfast in Christ your Rock, and fortify yourself in Him, and abide in His Church; then you will triumph over the demons, and live in constant joy and praise to God.
(3) Pleading for deliverance from the enemies (vv. 7-14).
7- Hear, O LORD, when I cry with my voice: have mercy also upon me, and answer me.

1- David asks God to hear his prayers, which he offered previously in the preceding verses, joined with the prayers of the believers who lift up their pleadings before God in His house. For he feels his membership in the house of the Lord, even if he is far from it because of his circumstances.
2- In humility David says "have mercy upon me", that is, I do not deserve, O Lord, that You hear my prayer, but I am needy, so by Your mercy condescend and accept my prayers for my need of You.
8- When thou saidst, Seek ye my face; my heart said unto thee, "Thou saidst, Seek ye my face." Thy face, LORD, will I seek.

1- David presents his request to God from his heart, that is, from the depths of his feelings and not only with his lips. And this is an expression of David's bond with the Person of God and his attachment to Him.

2- God wishes that we love Him for His Person, and not merely as a means of fulfilling our requests, and David understood this; therefore he sought the face of God, that is, His Person, out of love for Him. He moved from asking for God's help against the enemies to being occupied with the face of God, because enjoying the presence of God is sweeter than anything in the world. And of course whoever feels the presence of God, God will not leave him but supplies all his needs; for Christ Himself said, "Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness" (Mt 6:33), and after this He will not neglect man but arranges for him the rest of the matters of his life, among them victory over the enemies.

3- David sinned and repented of his sin, and kept making his bed swim with his tears every night, but his comfort - in the midst of these painful feelings, and in the midst of all his tribulations - is his enjoyment of seeing the face of God, who comforts him, satisfies him and gladdens him.
9- Hide not thy face from me. Disappoint not thy servant in wrath: thou hast been my help; reject me not, neither forsake me, O God of my salvation.
Wrath: severe anger.
1- While David is pursued by Saul and exposed to death at any moment, he was not distracted by this from seeking to see God; it is his life, which he cannot do without.

2- David fears God, and this is shown by his caution and his fear of the wrath of God's justice; he is not careless if he has fallen into any sin, but lives always in the fear of God and guards against it, so he keeps away from sin.

3- David's asking God not to hide His face from him shows his understanding that God hides His face from sinners; it is an implicit declaration of his repentance and his confession of his sin, but he hopes that God's mercy will forgive him and the recompense of his sins, that is, the wrath of God's justice, will not come upon him. He lives a life of repentance.

4- David's saying "Disappoint not thy servant in wrath" shows his hope in God. In spite of David's confession of his sin, his hope is firm, so he asks with confidence for God's forgiveness and the enjoyment of seeing His face.

5- David is accustomed to God's being his help; he lives in fellowship with God, therefore he asks God that this fellowship continue and not be cut off because of his sins, because he asks for God's forgiveness and mercy. And he asks God specifically not to reject him or forsake him, that is, he stresses the necessity that He establish him in Himself.
6- David believes that his only salvation is from God, and he has no relation to any strange gods or human power; he trusts in God in everything, therefore he always receives his salvation.
10- For my father and my mother have forsaken me, and the LORD embraces me.

1- While David was fleeing from the face of Saul, his father and mother were of course not with him, but he had placed them with the king of Moab lest Saul harm them, so he means his deprivation of the care and support of his father and mother, especially as he suffers the pains of Saul's pursuit and evil. This suffering made him feel his need of the support of others, the most important of whom are the parents.

2- The father and the mother represent the most important care a person receives, so David here means his deprivation, not only of father and mother, but also of the support of brothers, friends and loved ones; it is an expression of the extent of his suffering and endurance.

3- If David was deprived of the care of the bodily father and mother, he powerfully enjoys the care of his spiritual Father, who is the Lord, who embraces him to His breast in tenderness and satisfies him with His love.
4- If a person turns tribulation and material deprivation into a relationship with God, he experiences depths he never tasted before, and feels that the Lord embraces him, and this means:
a - That he is in God's embrace, that is, he feels His deep love.
b - That he has become one of God's own and has joined Him.
c - That he has been united with God by joining His embrace.
11- Teach me thy way, O LORD, and lead me in a plain path, because of mine enemies.

1- David's asking God to teach him His way and lead him in the straight path shows David's humility and his feeling as if he were a child who needs to learn how to walk. And of course he receives abundant divine guidance and grace.

2- Saul, David's enemy, and all who were with him adopted evil methods to try to seize David, so David asks God for help, so that he is not influenced by or imitates the ways of evil, but that He teach him the straight way, built on the commandments of God.

3- David did not ask for a way to triumph over his enemies, but asked for the straight way, that is, the divine way. And as long as he walks in the way of God, he is guaranteed His care and protection from all enemies. And above all this he keeps his peace and enjoys fellowship with God.
12- Deliver me not over unto the will of them that trouble me: for false witnesses are risen up against me, and one that breathes out injustice.
One that breathes out: that is, who blows and sends out venom from his mouth like a serpent.

1- David trusts in God's power; in spite of his weakness before Saul's armies, he believes in God's protection and His power, which is able to rescue him from the desire of his enemies who want to kill him.

2- David's faith appears in his steadfastness and his confidence in God who is with him, in spite of the rising up against him of false witnesses, who are Saul's followers, who made many false claims against him, such as his rebellion against the king, or his refusal of worship of God in His house, or his union with the enemies of Israel such as the Philistines, and all this is false; because of the violence of Saul's pursuit, David was compelled at times to flee to the Philistines, but he still held fast to the worship of God, as appeared from the preceding verses in this Psalm.

3- If the enemies relied on breathing out their venom like serpents, in the lies they let loose and in their attempts to kill David, David on the other hand relied on God, who is able to deliver him from their hands.
13- Had I not believed that I would see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living.
The goodness of the Lord: His grace and kindnesses.
1- In the midst of the many tribulations that David suffers, he believed in God's grace and goodness, and that He is able to solve his problems.

2- The land of the living does not mean only our earth on which we live, but also the heavenly Jerusalem. For in the midst of tribulations David believed that God would compensate him for his suffering with rest and glories in heaven.

3- David was preoccupied with the heavenly glories that he sees while on earth more than with all his problems, and this gave him comfort, peace and strength to bear the sufferings. In the midst of the tribulation he is occupied with God and the enjoyment of fellowship with Him more than with solving his problems.
14- Wait for the LORD; let your heart be strengthened and take courage, and wait for the LORD.

1- At the end of the Psalm David addresses everyone who loves God, and even addresses himself also, to wait for the Lord during his suffering in tribulation, because the Lord is without doubt coming. Faith in God's love and concern gives rest to the heart, so it does not find the tribulation heavy.

2- Waiting for the Lord means the necessity of patience and accepting tribulation for a time. This is by God's permission for the benefit and good of man, for we do not obtain good except by patience.

3- Tribulation may be prolonged and may continue throughout life, so a person must wait, and his comfort is God's grace, to which he referred in the preceding verse. Perhaps for this reason he repeated the words "wait for the LORD" at the beginning of the verse and at its end.

4- The devil sends fears during the tribulation to weaken a person, so that he gives way to despair and depression and abandons his spiritual striving, so David calls to him to be strengthened and take courage, to triumph in the spiritual war and come out of the tribulation victorious.

5- David experienced this waiting practically in his life; he was anointed king at about the age of sixteen, but did not reign until the age of thirty over one tribe, the tribe of Judah, then at the age of thirty-seven he reigned over the rest of the tribes; and he wished and waited to build a house for the Lord, but God prevented him and told him that his son is the one who would build it, so he accepted this with thanks from God's hand, and prepared all he could for building the house.

Do not fear tribulation, for its appearance at the beginning seems hard. But be sure that inside its bitterness is a wonderful sweetness, and an experience of God that you have not tasted before, so persevere in your striving, confident of God's help and His comforts. A cry to God the Almighty. Of David. "Unto thee will I cry, O LORD" (v. 1). Introduction:
1- Its writer is David the prophet, as appears from its title.
2- When was it written?

He wrote it when he was fleeing either from the face of Saul or from the face of his son Absalom, as shown by his aversion to the deceitful wicked, declaring his rejection of the treachery that Absalom committed (v. 3).
3- It is considered one of the messianic Psalms, because it speaks about Christ the Savior, who intercedes for His children by His pure blood for ever (vv. 8, 9).
4- This Psalm suits every believer who suffers tribulations, and also suits the suffering Church in her cry to God.
5- This Psalm is not found among the Psalms of the Agpeya.

entries.section: (1) A cry for deliverance from the wicked

paragraphs.text: 1- "Unto thee will I cry, O Lord my rock; be not silent to me: lest, if thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit."
Be deaf (tatasamam): to make yourself deaf toward me, that is, to refuse to hear my prayer.

1- David's crying out shows how much he needs God, for he does not merely speak but cries out, declaring his severe distress. At the same time it shows his boldness before God, for he stood before Him and cried out, showing all his feelings and needs.

2- David trusts that God is his rock, that is, his strong refuge to whom he flees, and he trusts that no one can harm him while he is in God's protection; rather, whoever tries to strike against the rock will be broken, and if the rock falls upon him it will crush him. Therefore David is at peace as long as he takes shelter in his God, his rock. This also confirms his boldness before God, for God is not merely a rock, but his rock.

3- When David fell into sin through his adultery with the wife of Uriah the Hittite, he humbled himself before God in repentance and asked Him not to reject his prayer and stop His ears to it, but to forgive him; and at the same time he continued to pray, and to weep, and to make his bed swim every day.

4- David believes that God is his life, so that if God refuses to hear his prayer he will be like those who go down into the pit, that is, he is exposed to death if God abandons him. Therefore he begs God to hear him, that he may live before Him.

entries.section: (1) A cry for deliverance from the wicked

paragraphs.text: 2- "Hear the voice of my supplications, when I cry unto thee, when I lift up my hands toward thy holy oracle."

The oracle (sanctuary): this is the Holy of Holies, where the ark of the covenant of God is found in Solomon's temple, and into which the high priest enters once every year. The oracle declares the presence of God.
1- David's prayer is a supplication to God. Supplication means humility and contrition before God, and at the same time faith in the God to whom he makes supplication, that he may ask for His help.
2- David's crying out to God shows the extent of his need and suffering; indeed, he finds no deliverer except God. Therefore his prayer is strong and reaches the bosom of God.

3- The oracle had not yet been built by the hand of Solomon, but God had promised David that his son would build the temple. David prepared what was needed for building the temple, including the oracle. The oracle corresponds to the Holy of Holies in the tabernacle of the congregation, and in it is the most important thing in the tabernacle, or temple, namely the ark of the covenant of God, which declares His presence in the midst of His people. David saw this oracle by faith and lifted up his hands toward it, that is, he lifted up his hands toward God, asking for His help.
4- Lifting up the hands is a declaration of asking for help from heaven, where God dwells; so lifting up the hands toward the oracle is asking for succor and strength from God the Savior.

5- Moses lifted up his hands in the form of a cross before God in prayer, and Joshua was able to defeat the mighty army of Amalek. By the cross and prayer the spiritual person can overcome all the warfare of the demons.

6- David, driven out from the face of Absalom, had his heart attached to the ark of the covenant of God. He believes in, and feels, the presence of God even when he is far from the ark of the covenant, confirming the importance of mental prayer, even if a person is not able to be in the temple of God, or the Church, because of circumstances that prevent him.

entries.section: (1) A cry for deliverance from the wicked

paragraphs.text: 3- "Draw me not away with the wicked, and with the workers of iniquity, which speak peace to their neighbours, but mischief is in their hearts."

1- David pleads with God not to remove him from Himself and draw him away from His bosom, lest he join the wicked and the workers of iniquity; for he cannot imagine himself except in the hands of God, whom he loved with all his heart.

2- Although David was pursued by Saul and was sometimes compelled to be among the pagans in flight from Saul, he lived holding fast to God's commandments and attached to His house. So he asks God not to count him and number him with the wicked, because he is still His son and holds fast to his faith.

3- These wicked men are deceivers; they speak peace with people while evil is in their hearts. David holds fast to the purity of his heart, and declares to God that he needs His help to remain in this purity, far from the hypocritical wicked.

4- This verse is a prophecy about Christ the righteous and holy One, who was numbered with the transgressors when He bore the sufferings and the crucifixion for our sake. So He asks the Father not to leave Him, because He bears the sins of the whole world upon His head, and He is crucified for our redemption, when He said, "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?" (Ps 22:1).

5- Perhaps David saw by the spirit of prophecy Judas Iscariot the traitor, who spoke peace with his Master, kissed Him, and delivered Him to the Jews, and they arrested Him. So David asks that God not count him with Judas and with all the traitors and the deceitful wicked.

entries.section: (1) A cry for deliverance from the wicked

paragraphs.text: 4- "Give them according to their deeds, and according to the wickedness of their endeavours: give them after the work of their hands; render to them their desert."

1- David asks that the wicked be repaid according to their deeds and their wicked hearts, and not according to their smooth words that utter deceitful peace, for God is the searcher of hearts and reins; so that the wicked may fear God, and repent, and return to Him when He disciplines them, because discipline makes them feel the hardness of their hearts and the evil of their works, and so they repent.

2- Divine justice appears in repaying the wicked and punishing them, so that the believers may be firm in their faith and upright conduct, and may not be troubled by the temporary, material success of the wicked in the world.
3- When the Lord returns a man's works upon his head, people fear in their conduct and do not wrong others, lest all the evil they have done come upon them.
4- David shows God's hatred of evil by speaking of the wicked's deeds, their work, and their dealings, so that people may turn away from evil in all its forms in all their conduct.

entries.section: (1) A cry for deliverance from the wicked

paragraphs.text: 5- "Because they regard not the works of the Lord, nor the operation of his hands, he shall destroy them, and not build them up."

1- The sin of the wicked is that they did not pay attention to the works of God, and consequently did not believe in Him or walk by His commandments, so they deserved destruction, as the Scripture says, "My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge" (Hos 4:6).

2- The works of the Lord and the operation of His hands are His care for mankind, His support of the righteous, His displeasure with the wicked, and His governance of all His creatures. When a person contemplates all of this, he believes in God and submits to His commandments.

3- God is grieved by these wicked men and hates their evils, so He destroys these evils, that perhaps the wicked may repent. And if they do not repent, He destroys them and brings them to an end in eternal torment.
4- God destroys the wicked and does not rebuild them if they persist in sin. Consequently, because they refused to know God, they deserve this perpetual destruction, that is, eternal perdition.

5- These wicked men are deceivers; they deceived people with false words of peace while concealing evil toward them. This deceit came upon their own heads, for they themselves were deceived and departed from upright conduct, and so they perished.

If you face any distress, hasten to God who loves you and cry out to Him, confident that He hears you, even if you are in the depth of distress; indeed, He will deliver you from the hands of the wicked and give you peace and joy.
6- "Blessed be the Lord, because he hath heard the voice of my supplications."
1- David asked in faith and cried out to God at the beginning of the psalm, and now also in faith he lifts up his heart in thanksgiving to God who answered him.
2- David felt this thanksgiving before God answered, because he believed that He would answer; then he continued to thank Him until He actually answered.
3- How beautiful that David remembered to thank God for His answer and to bless Him, for this strengthens David's faith and makes him feel God's presence with him, so that his joy increases.
7- "The Lord is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in him, and I am helped: therefore my heart greatly rejoiceth; and with my song will I praise him."

My shield: my protection and my fortress; for the shield is an instrument of war that the soldier used in ancient times to defend himself. It is a piece of wood with a handle at the back, in which the soldier places his hand, and he moves it before his head and body, so that it protects him from arrows.

1- David's faith in the power of God made him trust in Him and not in anything else, so he felt strength and protection in Him while he was a fugitive and pursued. And since God saw his faith, He gave him victory. Victory is sure for everyone who believes in God with all his heart.

2- Since David trusted in God, he felt victory in Him before it happened, and he rejoiced in God's being with him, and this gladness spread through all his inner feelings, that is, his heart and consequently his mind, and it also showed on his face.
3- To express his joy, David thanked God and praised Him with a song, that is, he continued in thanksgiving and praise for a long time.

4- Since David felt joy in his heart, and the cause of this joy was the presence of God, in whom he trusted and who gave him victory, gladness became constant in his heart, and he expressed it in constant praise, so that God became his song, that is, his heart was attached to God, and he no longer had any joy except in Him.
8- "The Lord is their strength, and he is the saving strength of his anointed."

1- This expresses the power of the Father's work with those who believe in Him, for he says the Lord is their strength, for He is their glory and their greatness. And it expresses the work of the Son with the believers by saying, "the saving strength of his anointed," that is, that Christ is their Savior, who will accomplish their redemption in the fullness of time on the cross.

2- Christ the Savior gives those who believe in Him a strong and sure salvation, which he likens to a fortress, that is, the devil cannot penetrate it with all his power, his wiles, and his varied warfare; rather, the believers within the fortress enjoy fellowship with their Christ and rejoice with Him.

3- So David cannot separate himself from the company of the believers, that is, the Church; he says that the Lord is "my strength" in (v. 7), but David wants to feel his union with the rest of the believers, so he says that "the Lord is their strength" in (v. 8).

4- The mighty God saved David His anointed, that is, the one anointed king over his people, and became a fortress for him, protecting him all his days from his enemies; this represents the saving power of God, constant in its protection of David.
9- "Save thy people, and bless thine inheritance: feed them also, and lift them up for ever."

1- David changes from a man who cries to God and asks His help to save him from his enemies, into a responsible king and an intercessor for his people, asking salvation for them. By relying on God he was reassured and felt sure victory. And his bond with the company of the believers made him unable to bear receiving salvation alone; rather, he wants all the believers to receive salvation. This confirms his oneness with his people, and as a king he hands over the full responsibility to God with complete confidence in God's faithfulness to His people.

2- He is not content to ask salvation for his people, but with the boldness of love he asks God to bless them also, giving them material and spiritual blessings, that they may enjoy fellowship with Him.
3- The salvation that David asks of God for his people includes two things:
a - Deliverance from enemies, that is, the nations around them.
b - Deliverance from spiritual enemies, that is, the demons and all the sins connected with them.

4- With boldness David says to God that those who believe in Him are His people and He is their God who is responsible for them, who cannot possibly abandon them. Rather, they are His inheritance, that is, the best of what He possesses; for God said, "and my delights were with the sons of men" (Prov 8:31).
5- The third request that David asks of God for his people is that He feed them. This includes many things, the most important of which are:
a - Satisfying them materially.
b - Their spiritual sufficiency by knowing Him and cleaving to Him, and nourishing them with His Body and Blood in the Church of the New Testament.
c - Protecting them.
d - Guiding them in all their steps, until they reach the Kingdom.

6- The fourth and last request in David's intercession for his people is that God lift them up. This represents love at the highest level, so that the people of God are in His hands, and He brings them across the wilderness of this world until they reach eternal life. And when He carries them He gives them the enjoyment of fellowship with Him, and this is something that extends from earth to heaven, that is, it lasts forever with those who believe in God.

7- God's carrying His people means lifting them above material attachments and above every sin, so that they become heavenly, spiritual, lovers of virtues. And He lifts them up even more during tribulations, so that they feel peace however great the sufferings.

How beautiful it is that you see God's work in your life and feel it, so that your heart is moved to praise Him, and you enjoy His fellowship as a result; indeed, God becomes the song of your life, in whom you find your constant joy and your hope in all the circumstances of life, however hard they may be.
The voice of the Lord: "Give unto the Lord, O ye sons of God" (v. 1). Introduction:
1- Its author: he is David the prophet, as appears from the title of the psalm in the Beirut edition.
2- When was it said?

a - Before the tent of the ark: the first opinion is that David said this psalm after he brought the ark of the covenant of God back to Jerusalem and placed it in a tent made for it, which is different from the tabernacle of the congregation that was at Gibeon, which contained the other parts of the tabernacle apart from the ark. So after placing the ark in its own tent, David went out and recited this psalm. In the Septuagint, we find in the title of this psalm "for the going out of the tabernacle," and what is meant by the tabernacle is the tent in which David placed the ark of the covenant.
b - At the Feast of Tabernacles: specifically on its eighth day, because the Septuagint mentions that it is said at the Feast of Tabernacles, when the last harvests are gathered in the autumn.
c - At the Feast of Pentecost: that is, the Feast of Weeks, when the harvests are gathered. This feast comes fifty days after the Passover, and this opinion is mentioned in the Jewish Talmud.

d - Some think that a violent storm blew from the mountains of Lebanon in the north and passed through the land of the Jews, accompanied by lightning, thunder and fire that burned some places, so that fear and terror came upon the Jews. So David wrote this psalm declaring the power of God.
3- Outside the tabernacle: this title found in the Septuagint carries many symbolic meanings, among them:
a - The Jews' going out from the tabernacle of Jewish faith, from following God and accepting Christ, and the Gentiles' entering into faith in Christ.

b - The soul's going out from the body, and this means preparing for eternal life by living with God and offering Him sacrifices of love, so that we are not troubled when standing before the just Judge.
c - Keeping the Church holy in the world, so that she may go out from it and be glorified in the Kingdom of Heaven.
4- It was prayed with this psalm to ask God for rain to break a period of drought, as the prophet Zechariah said (Zech 14:16-18).

5- There is a relation between this psalm and the one before it, which is a cry to God, and He answers with this psalm. It presents the voice of the Lord with power, so that He reassures His children and blesses them.
6- This psalm proclaims the voice of God and repeats it seven times, confirming God's presence through nature; it is a psalm that makes us feel the presence and greatness of God.

7- This psalm is found in the prayer of the Third Hour in the Agpeya, where we see the descent of the Holy Spirit, who descended at this hour accompanied by the blowing of a wind. And this psalm speaks to us of the mighty voice of God, which subdues nature and changes souls by the work of the Holy Spirit, so that they believe in God. And as we mentioned, this psalm was said at the Feast of Pentecost, on which the Holy Spirit descended in the New Testament.

entries.section: (1) A call to worship the Lord

paragraphs.text: 1- "Give unto the Lord, O ye sons of God, give unto the Lord glory and strength."
1- God rejoices in the offerings of His children, and by His children is meant those who believe in Him, who love Him and present Him their gifts, and before their gifts they present their hearts.
2- The children of God believe in Him, so they glorify Him, because there is no other God but He. As for the gods of the nations, they are demons and have no value.
3- What is meant by giving glory and strength to God is praising His holy name, thanking Him for His power that protects His children, and glorifying Him for all His works with them.

entries.section: (1) A call to worship the Lord

paragraphs.text: 2- "Give unto the Lord the glory due unto his name; worship the Lord in the beauty of holiness."
1- God's name means His person, so glorifying His name means glorifying Him. This glorifying lifts the heart and attaches it to God, so that it rises above every sin.
2- Glorifying God is accomplished not only by the praise of the lips, but also by good works and every act of mercy and help toward others.
3- The believer is called to give to God three times, after the pattern of the Holy Trinity; that is, whoever gives to God receives the blessing of the Holy Trinity.

4- In the Septuagint there is also mention of bringing the young of rams, that is, the sacrifices offered in the tabernacle of the congregation and in the tent of Solomon, as proof of the believers' love for God. Thus the believers are called to bring to God four times: the three mentioned here, with the offering of the young of rams added to them. The believers' bringing offerings to God four times is a type of presenting these gifts in the four corners of the world, that is, the whole world. This is completed when the Gentiles believe in Christ and offer the sacrifices of the New Testament, that is, the Body and Blood of the Lord, in every place in the world.

5- After presenting their love to God in offerings, the believers are called to submit to Him with reverence, so he says to them, worship the Lord in the beauty of holiness, that is, in modest clothing, without preoccupation with material things, and with readiness to obey His commandments.

6- In the Septuagint, that is, in the Agpeya, it says, worship the Lord in His holy court; and what is meant by the holy court is the tabernacle of the congregation and the temple of Solomon, then after this the Church in the New Testament, and finally the perfect holy court is the Kingdom of Heaven.

God rejoices in all your offerings, so do not be stingy toward God with the offerings of your mouth's praises, and likewise with works of mercy, and thus you gladden His heart with your love and your response to Him.
3- "The voice of the Lord is upon the waters: the God of glory thundereth: the Lord is upon many waters."

1- David felt that the sound coming from the tumult of the waters is the voice of God, the Creator of these waters, whether in the seas or the rivers, declaring His mastery over them; for it is He who controls the seas by the phenomenon of the tides and does not let them cover the dry land.

2- Before the beginning of creation the world was waters and darkness, and the Spirit of God was hovering over the face of the waters, and it was He who created the heaven and the air, gathered the waters into collections, and caused the dry land to appear. So the Spirit of God is the secret of the life of all creation, and He thunders with His power, declaring that He is the Creator, just as He also thundered on the day of Pentecost, declaring that He created the Church, and He dwells in all who believe in Him, giving them a life that lasts forever.
3- The many waters signify mankind, whether Jews or Gentiles. And the voice of God above them means that He is the Creator of all mankind.

4- The voice of the Lord means the incarnate Hypostasis of the Son, who is the Word of God who appears as a voice that we hear; for "No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him" (Jn 1:18).

5- The phrase "the voice of the Lord" is repeated seven times in this psalm, declaring the perfection of Christ, because the number 7 signifies perfection. And He has given us salvation by His Holy Spirit in the seven sacraments of the Church. And we hear the voice of the Lord in His saving work in these sacraments.

6- When the voice of the Lord thunders, it frightens the wicked, because it judges them, but it reassures the children of God, as it declares that He is their support in all tribulations; for the many waters also signify tribulations, but the Lord above them reassures His children that He is the Controller of all, and no harm touches them as long as He is with them.
4- "The voice of the Lord is powerful; the voice of the Lord is full of majesty."

1- The voice of the Lord is full of power, so it troubled the wicked, like Pharaoh and the Egyptians, who pursued the children of Israel and entered the Red Sea, and God troubled them through the pillar of fire, until the wheels of their chariots came off (Ex 14:25); and likewise He troubled the Philistines in the days of Samuel (1 Sam 7:10).

2- The voice of the Lord was powerful when it declared of Christ, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased," when He was transfigured on Mount Tabor with Moses and Elijah. And His majesty and greatness appeared clearly before His disciples.

3- Christ spoke as one having authority and not as the scribes, so His speech was with power and also with majesty, even when He appeared in weakness, when the soldiers came to arrest Him and He asked them, "Whom seek ye?" and they said, "Jesus of Nazareth," and then He said to them, "I am he," and they fell to the ground on their faces, for fear of His power and greatness (Jn 18:6).
5- "The voice of the Lord breaketh the cedars; yea, the Lord breaketh the cedars of Lebanon."
6- "He maketh them also to skip like a calf; Lebanon and Sirion like a young wild ox."
The cedars of Lebanon: a tall, gigantic, evergreen tree, whose wood is strong and is not broken by violent winds; rather, the tree is uprooted, yet the wind cannot break it.
Makes them skip: crushes them.
Sirion: a name given to Mount Hermon, a mountain lying southeast of Lebanon, very high, reaching a height of about 3000 meters.
The young of the wild ox: quick to flee and run away; what is meant is the young of the wild ox, which are swift to run away.
1- If the cedar trees of Lebanon represent strength and greatness, and signify the pride of man, then God by His mighty voice breaks this cedar and subjects man's pride to Himself.

2- The wicked who humbled the people of God by their pride, when the children of God prayed, He intervened and shattered the wicked, as He drowned Pharaoh and all his army in the Red Sea, and killed 185,000 of the army of Sennacherib the Assyrian in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah (Isa 37:36).
3- The lofty cedar of Lebanon signifies the high places of the idol temples; God breaks them and brings His children back to faith in Him.

4- God's power that breaks the cedars of Lebanon and casts them to the ground is like the calf of Lebanon that treads and crushes the grasses in the green, fertile regions spread across Lebanon. That is, the strongest thing on earth has no strength before God, and is like weak grass before the calf of Lebanon.

5- The mountains too, however towering, cannot stand before the mighty voice of the Lord, but flee from His voice, as the young of the wild ox flee and run away. That is, everything great in creation cannot withstand the power of God, and this reassures the children of God that as long as God is with them, no one can harm them.
7- "The voice of the Lord kindles flames of fire."
Kindles: sets alight.
1- God kindles the flame of fire by means of the lightning that appears in the sky and casts fire upon the earth.

2- God punishes the wicked by kindling fire in their places, as He did in the seventh plague upon Pharaoh and the Egyptians, so that His people might go out of Egypt, when He sent fire along with the hail (Ex 9:24). And as He burned Sodom and Gomorrah with fire from heaven (Gen 19:24). And likewise He burned those who murmured against the priesthood of Aaron, with Korah, Dathan and Abiram (Num 16:35).

3- God kindles by His Holy Spirit the fire of His love in the hearts of His children, so that they cling to Him, and He becomes their only aim, which rises above all aims, as we see in the lives of the martyrs, who sacrificed their lives for His name, and likewise the Apostles and servants who labored in His service, and in the hearts of those who left the world and lived solitary in monasticism to enjoy fellowship with Him, and the heart of every person who lives with God in His Church.

4- In eternity God increases the kindling of love within the hearts of His children, so that they enjoy fellowship with Him forever, but for the wicked He kindles the flame of fire, which burns them and torments them forever.

5- In the Septuagint, "God divides the flame of fire," and this actually happened with the three young men, when God divided the flame of fire and surrounded them with a covering of dewy air (Dan 3:50).
6- God cuts off the flame of the fire of lusts and sin from the hearts of His children, and saves them from it, when they repent and return to Him.
8- "The voice of the Lord shaketh the wilderness; the Lord shaketh the wilderness of Kadesh."
The wilderness of Kadesh: Kadesh means holy. The wilderness of Kadesh is the one the children of Israel crossed before entering the land of Canaan. It lies northeast of Sinai.

1- In the wilderness of Kadesh, Moses spoke to the children of Israel in three long sermons, which are the Book of Deuteronomy. And after he sanctified them with the word of God, and shook their souls so that they would reject evil and enter the land of Canaan with pure hearts, he went up the mountain and died (Deut 34:5).

2- The voice of the Lord is powerful in its speech, that is, it shakes the slack and lazy souls, so that they become alert in the wilderness of this world, and then they deserve to enter the land of Canaan, which signifies the Kingdom of Heaven.
3- This quake also shakes the distant souls, like the Gentiles, so that they believe and have a place in the Kingdom of Heaven.
9- "The voice of the Lord maketh the hinds to calve, and discovereth the forests: and in his temple every one saith, Glory."
The hind: the deer, or one of its kinds.
The forests: the woods.

1- Hinds give birth with difficulty and over a long time, but when they hear loud sounds they give birth quickly out of fear; so the voice of the Lord helps the believers to bring forth virtues, and to offer service and good works to those around them.

2- The voice of the Lord is thunder and lightning, which, when it comes upon the forests, reveals what is inside them by the light of the lightning, shakes the trees and disturbs the animals, so that they come out of their dens and run far away.
So the voice of the Lord reveals man's sins, and every evil lust flees from it, and all anger, violence and savagery, and he is purified from all evil.

3- After David reviewed the voice of the Lord that works in nature, whether the waters, or the cedars, or the flame of fire, or the wilderness, or the hinds, or the forests, he summarizes in conclusion and says that all nature, with the creatures of God in it, is worked upon by Him and is subject to Him; indeed, he declares that all of them are temples of God which He sanctified for Himself, and each of them glorifies God, as it says, "The heavens declare the glory of God" (Ps 19:1).

4- Hinds search for serpents, and when they find them they trample them with their hooves and kill them, then eat them. So they purify the place of poisonous serpents, swallowing them and finishing them off. In this the power of God is shown, which overcomes evil and glorifies Him in His temple, which is the body of the hinds. For the hinds signify the spiritual person, who tramples Satan and his evil lusts, and triumphs over them, and so glorifies God in His temple, which is his body.

5- If all nature is temples of God, then all the more the spiritual person is a temple of the Holy Spirit. And the Church is the greatest and holiest place in the world, because she is the temple of God in which all the believers raise their voices and glorify God with their praises and their works.

Your aim in life is to glorify God, by rejecting evil, walking uprightly and praising God, and this is an introduction to your eternal life. So remember your aim at the start of every day, so that you may live as a temple of the Holy Spirit.

entries.section: (3) The sovereignty and blessing of the Lord

paragraphs.text: 10- "The Lord sitteth upon the flood; yea, the Lord sitteth King for ever."
1- The voice of the Lord, repeated seven times, has done the following:

a - It thundered upon the waters and subjected them to Himself, and however great the power of the waves of the sea, He is the Controller of all, and so He reassures His children, however much wicked men rise up around them.
b - The voice of the Lord is with power, and it subdues the demons under the feet of His children.
c - The voice of the Lord appears with majesty, and gives His children awe in the eyes of those around them.
d - The voice of the Lord shatters the cedar, which is man's pride, and when he is crushed before God he receives His blessings.
e - The voice of the Lord kindles the fire of the Holy Spirit in the hearts of His children who believe in Him, so that they live with Him and keep His commandments.
f - It shakes the wilderness of our life, so that it is purified of all evil, that we may enter the Kingdom of Heaven.
g - The voice of the Lord makes the hind to calve and discovers the forests, so it purifies man of all evil, that he may live in purity before Him, filled with every virtue.
And in the end man becomes a true dwelling place for God and a temple for Him, and he glorifies Him.

2- If the voice of God has prepared the souls of the believers and they have become a temple for Him, then He dwells in them, and sits, and rests in them through the sacrament of Baptism, which the flood signifies.

3- The Lord sits upon the flood and puts an end to all evil, and delivers His children, who are Noah and his family, and also delivers His children in every generation, and sits in their hearts and never leaves them, and protects them from the works of Satan that surround them.
4- God reigns over the hearts of His children and gives them the enjoyment of fellowship with Him, and He remains reigning over them forever in the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.section: (3) The sovereignty and blessing of the Lord

paragraphs.text: 11- "The Lord will give strength unto his people; the Lord will bless his people with peace."

1- The Lord supports, lifts up and glorifies His children and His people, for He saves them from their sins and dwells in their hearts, so they lift up their heads rejoicing and praising God, who gives them victory every day over Satan.
2- As God purifies His children every day by repentance, He grants them by His Holy Spirit good fruits, the most important of which is inner peace, which none but the children of God enjoy.

3- If the voice of the Lord at the beginning of the psalm contains thunder, shattering, burning and quaking, all this is to purify His children from sin and remove from them all disturbance. Although it is a mighty voice, it is not frightening to the children of God; on the contrary, we find at the end of the psalm that He grants them His perfect peace.
The greatest grace that God gives you is inner peace, so cut off everything that hinders your peace and give it up, that you may enjoy the most precious jewel, which is peace, and then joy.
Thanksgiving to God the Savior. A Psalm and Song at the dedication of the house of David: "I will extol thee, O Lord; for thou hast lifted me up" (v. 1). Introduction:

1- Its author: David the prophet, as appears from the title, and not Jeremiah, as some have claimed that he was its author, relying on what is written in the psalm, "Thou hast kept me alive, from among those that go down to the pit" (v. 3), because the intended meaning is symbolic, for God drew David up from death.
2- When was it said?
a - At the dedication of David's own house for his dwelling.
b - He said it in the field of Araunah the Jebusite, where he built an altar and gave thanks to God who stopped the plague. And there the temple of Solomon was built.

c - David said it when God forgave him his great sin with the wife of Uriah the Hittite, and that was by the hand of Nathan the prophet; so this sin is the severe sickness of which the psalm speaks to us, by which he drew near to death, and God healed him from it.

3- This psalm was said at the dedication of the temple, whether in the days of Solomon, or Zerubbabel, or Judas Maccabeus, and it continued to be said at the Feast of Dedication until the days of Christ.

4- Perhaps David wrote this psalm by the spirit of prophecy about King Hezekiah, who would be exposed to a sickness unto death, and after the prayer of Isaiah God healed him. And likewise about God's deliverance of Hezekiah from the army of Sennacherib, when the angel of God killed 185,000 soldiers of this army in one night.
5- This psalm points to the birth of Christ and His resurrection by saying, "Thou hast brought up my soul from the grave, from among those that go down to the pit" (v. 3).

6- In the title of this psalm we find "a Psalm and Song," and this means that it was said with two musical elements, or with one musical instrument, which is the pipe, that is, the "psalm," and the human voice, which is the "song."
7- This psalm, with the four psalms that follow, that is, up to Psalm 34, are psalms of thanksgiving to God.
8- The priest recites this psalm when he puts on the priestly vestments to begin the prayer of the Divine Liturgy.

9- The Church recites this psalm in the prayer of the Third Hour, which is the hour of the descent of the Holy Spirit, because in this psalm appear the blessings of the work of the Holy Spirit in the life of the believer, so that he glorifies God.
1- "I will extol thee, O Lord: for thou hast lifted me up, and hast not made my foes to rejoice over me."

1- This psalm begins with thanksgiving to God, indeed with glorifying and magnifying Him, because there is no god like Him in His care and providence for His children; therefore David thanks Him for His works with him.

2- David was sunk in his sin and did not feel its guilt, so God intervened by means of Nathan the prophet and warned him, and he awoke and rose to thank God, who drew him out of the mire of sin in which he had been immersed, and lifted him to the glory of purity and cleanness that he obtained by God's forgiveness.
3- The nations around David, and likewise the demons, wanted to destroy David, but they were not able, because God delivered him and drew him out of their hands, so they could not rejoice over him.

4- David feels God's special care for him, so he says, "thou hast lifted me up, and hast not made my foes to rejoice over me"; he feels that he is the object of God's care, love and protection from his enemies.

5- The same words apply to King Hezekiah, who was exposed to destruction at the hand of Sennacherib the Assyrian, and likewise to sickness, and God rescued him and killed the army of Sennacherib, and healed him of his sickness.

6- This verse applies to every spiritual person who strives with God against the demons and sin, and feels the hand of God that supports him and rescues him in the sacraments of confession and Holy Communion, and so he glorifies Him.
2- "O Lord my God, I cried unto thee, and thou hast healed me."

1- God is able to do all things and loves His children, but He waits for their faith in Him, which appears in their taking refuge in Him and crying out to Him, and then He intervenes with power and delivers them from all evil.
2- David has the boldness of sonship before God, so he says to Him "my God," and cries out to Him, and God rejoices in David's clinging to Him and answers his request.

3- God heals His children, not only of the diseases of the body, but also of spiritual diseases, which are sins. And His healing is complete, as David rose up with all his strength and continued his life with God in prayers and good works.
3- "O Lord, thou hast brought up my soul from the grave: thou hast kept me alive, from among those that go down to the pit."

1- David was exposed to death from his Jewish enemies close to him, such as Saul and Absalom, and he was also exposed to death from the nations around him, such as the Philistines, and likewise he was exposed to spiritual death through his falling into sin. But God brought him up from death and the grave and gave him life before Him; therefore he thanks Him.

2- What is meant by the pit here is death and the grave, and the hardest thing about the pit is that it is a deep hole that separates one from life and from people. It signifies man's separation from God by his fall and his going down to hell. So he thanks God who saved him from this death.

3- King Hezekiah was exposed to death twice: at the hand of Sennacherib, then by sickness, but God gave him a new life. So David, by the spirit of prophecy, speaks of Hezekiah, who received the grace of life from death (Isa 36-39).

4- David was a type of Christ who died and was buried in the tomb, then rose from it by the resurrection, to be the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep, and to give those who believe in Him a rising from sin and every weakness.

The power of God is able to rescue you from any tribulation or sin, so do not be troubled by the difficulty of the tribulation, nor by your weakness, but rise quickly in repentance and prayer, and be confident that God will support you, and you will glorify Him.
4- "Sing unto the Lord, O ye saints of his, and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness."

1- The pious are those who fear God and feel their unworthiness of His mercies and blessings, so when God blesses them they sing in thanksgiving and joy, and they sing with all their hearts. Only the pious are those to whom God gives joy and praise, but those who do not fear God easily fall into murmuring and cannot praise Him.
