3- Some see this psalm as a prophecy of the praise and blessing of the people of God returning from the captivity.

4- This psalm shows the feelings of David and his people toward God, while the next psalm (Ps 104) is similar to this psalm in praising God, and both end with the phrase “Bless the LORD, O my soul,” but the latter psalm expresses the praise of God by the whole creation.
5- This psalm is a prophecy of the blessings of the awaited Messiah, so it is considered one of the messianic psalms.
6- This psalm is liturgical; the Jews used to repeat it in the Temple, and they still worship with it to this day.
7- This psalm suits everyone who loves God and wishes to thank Him, for it expresses strong feelings of love for God.
8- This psalm is not found in the prayer of the Agpeya.
Bless the Lord, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name.

1- David calls his spirit to praise God. He encourages his soul to rise with zeal, to stand before God, to bless Him and glorify Him for His great works, even though David had passed through sufferings, but he forgets them in the flood of his joy in praising God.

2- David affirms for the second time the praise of God, so he calls his inward parts, meaning his mind and his feelings, to glorify and bless God; that is, he praises God with his whole being, and so enjoys fellowship with Him.
3- The meaning of this verse appears in the words of Christ when He summed up the commandments: "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart" (Mt 22:37).
Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:
1- David calls his soul to thank God for His blessings, His care and all His works with him. This confirms the importance of thanksgiving, which rejoices the heart of God.

2- The believer in God thanks Him for His kindnesses, which are in His gifts, and also for the afflictions that come upon a person, for they are for his discipline and correction, so that they bring him near to God and pluck him out of evil; therefore he thanks God for them as well. These are the feelings of David, and of everyone who has believed and trusted in God.
Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases;

1- The first thing that deserves a person's thanks is God's forgiveness of his sins, and thereby He grants him new life. This is fulfilled in Christ the Savior in the sacrament of confession, and perhaps David saw it with the eye of prophecy.

2- The second gift for which he thanks God is his healing from his diseases, meaning the spiritual diseases that resulted from sin, in addition to psychological and bodily diseases. For God is able to heal all diseases, and He deserves thanks and glory, for He restores a person to his first health, so that he may begin anew an active life with God.
Who redeemeth thy life from destruction; who crowneth thee with lovingkindness and tender mercies;

1- David thanks God who rescued him from the hand of Saul and Absalom and redeemed his life, that is, saved him from death, and clothed him with a great crown by His mercy and compassion when He crowned him king over His people, and even gave him victory over his enemies. And more than this, He gave him spiritual fellowship, and he enjoyed the presence of God.

2- This verse is a prophecy about Christ the Redeemer, who by His death on the cross redeemed us from "the pit", that is, Hades and hell, into which we fall because of our sins. And He crowned us with His mercies and compassions with the crown of victory over sin and Satan. This is a pledge of the crown of eternal glory in the Kingdom.

3- Christ redeems His children from the plots of the wicked in every generation, and keeps them in the faith, and even grants them the crowns of martyrdom, virginity, monasticism, service and the priesthood; all this by His mercies and compassions, as a free gift of love to them.
Who satisfieth thy mouth with good things; so that thy youth is renewed like the eagle's.

1- David also thanks God, in conclusion, for the many good things He gave him. By good things he means all material gifts, and rather the spiritual ones, so he thanks Him for keeping him, for satisfying him with material things, and for the kingdom, and he thanks Him even more for knowing Him, for choosing him in his life, and for enjoying fellowship with Him; and this is what every spiritual person ought to do.

2- When the eagle reaches the age of thirty, its talons and its beak grow weak and the feathers of its wings stick to its body, and it is exposed to death, since it cannot seize its prey and is unable to fly. Then it must renew its strength in order to continue living, so it flies to the top of the mountain and stays there for a hundred and fifty days, that is, five months, in which it breaks its talons, once and then a second time, by striking them against the rock, and likewise its beak, and they grow again, but with strength; and it plucks out its old feathers, and others grow in their place, strong feathers not sticking to its body. It endures all these pains in order to continue its life for another thirty years, or more, for its age can reach seventy years.

3- David wishes for his soul, when it meets spiritual coldness and weakness, that its vitality and spiritual strength be renewed through spiritual striving and suffering. Then it sets out anew in a strong life with God, as the eagle does. Then his soul is able to soar in the heaven of the virtues and to rise above earthly desires. This is what every spiritual person wishes for and strives after.

4- Just as the eagle endures many pains to renew its youth, so the spiritual person must endure trials, and likewise the pains of spiritual striving. Also the servant endures the pains of service, so that spiritual youth may be renewed and the person may rise in his relationship with God.
5- Thus we see that David wishes for himself, and for every one who strives spiritually, six things, which are:
a- The forgiveness of his sins.
b- The healing of his spiritual and bodily diseases.
c- Obtaining redemption from sin and eternal torment.
d- Receiving the crown of life with God and the Kingdom of Heaven.
e- Being satisfied with spiritual goods, in addition to bodily ones.
f- A continual renewal of the spiritual life.

Thanking God establishes His gifts for you, and even more and deeper blessings overflow upon you, so you live full of the grace of God, enjoying fellowship with Him, and you experience the Kingdom on earth, until you reach it in heaven.
The Lord executeth righteousness and judgment for all that are oppressed.
"Executeth": that is, carries out; its meaning is that He puts into effect righteousness and judgment and makes them prevail.

1- God watches over all the oppressed and feels with them, and He will surely give them their right, but sometimes He postpones lifting the oppression from them, to give the oppressor an opportunity to repent, and the oppressed an opportunity to be firm in his faith and not cling to the world. But if the oppressed does not receive his right on earth, he will certainly receive it in heaven. And this is far better, that he should enjoy great delight in the Kingdom, in contrast to what awaits the oppressor, which is eternal torment.
2- If the oppressed has lost material things, then if he takes refuge in God, He compensates him with spiritual and psychological blessings, whereas the oppressor, on the contrary, loses them.
3- Christ our God fulfilled the divine justice on our behalf on the cross, so He removed our sins from us and gave us freedom and eternal life.
He made known his ways unto Moses, his acts unto the children of Israel.

1- The ways of the Lord that He made known to Moses are His commandments, and His acts toward the children of Israel are His power that appeared in bringing them out of the land of Egypt by the ten plagues and in the crossing of the Red Sea.

And likewise He sustained them and kept them in the wilderness, and brought them into the land of Canaan, and they possessed it. Here His righteousness and judgment appear, and even His mercy too. For if they had endured oppression in Egypt, God rescued them from slavery, punished the oppressors, and gave them the enjoyment of His fellowship by dwelling in their midst, and even gave them the land flowing with milk and honey. And He had clearly declared to them that they should live by His ways and observe His acts when He spoke to Moses on the mountain (Ex 34:6, 7).

2- Moses and the children of Israel knew, through His works with them, His ways, that is, His plan for salvation through His incarnation and His redemption of mankind. Just as He freed them by the ten plagues, so He endured the cross for them and redeemed them. And just as Moses and the people crossed the Red Sea, so by Baptism the believers in the New Covenant receive salvation. And likewise the rock that gives water is a type of Christ, and the victory over Amalek is a type of the victory over Satan.

8- The Lord is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy. 9- He will not always chide: neither will he keep his anger for ever. He hath not dealt with us after our sins; nor rewarded us according to our iniquities.

1- If God is just, so that He does justice to the oppressed, then if they err, He is just also so as to repay them, but He is very long-suffering, to give them an opportunity for repentance. And He is also plenteous in mercy if they repent, so He receives them and forgives them, and even compensates them for all that they lost; as He did with Job, for after he repented of self-righteousness He compensated him with double what he had had (Job 42:10). And as He forgave Abraham for his lie and his weakness before Pharaoh, and was long-suffering toward him, and kept Sarah from the hand of Pharaoh (Gen 20:3-7). And as He was long-suffering toward His people in the age of the Judges, and when the enemies humbled them He sent them judges, such as Gideon and Samson, and saved them from slavery.

2- God does not continue His punishment of those who err, so that He would appear to be holding a grudge against them; the meaning of "keep his anger" is His anger against them. But He disciplines His children so that they may repent, and then He has mercy on them and forgives them.
11- For as the heaven is high above the earth, so great is his mercy toward them that fear him.
12- As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us. 13- Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him.
1- The children of God are those who fear Him, so they keep away from sin, and if they sin they hasten to repentance.

And those who always strive toward Him to live by His commandments and adorn themselves with the virtues, God singles out and gives them great mercy, very strong, and even beyond comprehension in its size, for it is unlimited. So he likens it to its height being like the height of heaven above the earth, and also like the distance of the east from the west.
He removes our sins from us, and for this reason we renounce Satan and his sins in Baptism facing the west, while the confession of Christ is made facing the east, that we may live for Him.

2- God's mercy appears in the heavens, for they cover the earth on every side, and His mercies overflow in them; that is, the light from the sun, the moon and the stars, the air we breathe, and the rains that water us and water the crops.

3- The writer of the Psalm explains God's great mercy by saying that it comes upon us from God because He is our Father, so He has compassion on us, and even if we sin He is long-suffering so that we may repent. And we cannot understand the wisdom of our loving, compassionate Father, who seems harsh in His discipline, although He is merciful and wants to remove our sins from us and bring us back to Him. And sometimes He delays His blessings, and then pours out mercies that surpass our understanding. His wisdom is far higher than we are, like the heaven, of which we can understand only a little, and about the movement of the planets and the stars in it, the winds and the mist; these are very difficult for our understanding, so truly "how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out!" (Rom 11:33).

4- The son who loves and fears his father trusts in his fatherhood, so he surrenders himself into his hands, submitting to his will because of his faith that his father arranges good for him; even if he does not understand the things that pass through his life, or the afflictions that come upon him, yet he is at all times at rest in his father's arms.
14- For he knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we are dust.
As a flower of the field, so he flourisheth. 16- For the wind passeth over it, and it is gone; and the place thereof shall know it no more.

1- The writer of the Psalm appeals for God's mercies, so he declares to Him that man is weak, indeed nothing before the greatness of God, and very liable to error, and he likens him to dust, and likewise to the grass that grows and flowers, then the strong wind comes upon it, uproots it and scatters it everywhere. By the wind he means trials and death. And since man is weak to this degree, he needs the great mercy of God to support him, forgive him and receive him.

2- If man is weak to this degree, he ought to humble himself before God and trust in Him, and even hold fast to Him by faith in all his steps, for he always needs God's support. And on the other hand, he should have compassion on the people around him when they err, and not judge them, so that he deserves God's mercies.
17- But the mercy of the Lord is from everlasting to everlasting upon them that fear him, and his righteousness unto children's children;
18- To such as keep his covenant, and to those that remember his commandments to do them.
1- God's mercy is constant throughout life, and for ever, and generous and strong, but it is given only to those who have the following:
a- The fear of God, which keeps them from evil.
b- Those who hold fast to God's covenant, that they may live for Him.
c- Those who always remember God's commandments in order to put them into practice in their lives.

2- Likewise God's righteousness does justice to His oppressed children and rewards them for all their toil with peace and inner joy, and many blessings in life, then the glories of eternity. All this is given not only to the children but also to their children who live as they do as children of God. Likewise "children's children" means the works of the person and his spiritual striving, and for the sake of these works God blesses the children and keeps them by His righteousness, and God's righteousness is completed in the happiness that He gives His children in eternity as a reward to them for their good works.

If God's mercy and long-suffering, my brother, are great to this degree, this urges you to repentance and to strive toward every good work. And do not be troubled by the warfare of the demons and the fluctuations of the world and its fears, for God's mercy and righteousness support you, so you walk with firm steps toward the Kingdom, enjoying the care of your tender Father.
19- The Lord hath prepared his throne in the heavens; and his kingdom ruleth over all.
1- The throne of God and His place in heaven are firm for the following reasons:
a- Heaven rises above the earth with all its desires and material things, for it is a symbol of spirituality.
b- Heaven is firm, not like the changeable earth, for human beings are changeable in their characters and their behavior.
c- Heaven is mysterious, a symbol of the existence of God; for He is unlimited, and the mind cannot grasp all that is in Him.

2- God is the King of kings, and His kingdom rules over all people, for He is the Upholder of all, the Creator of all creatures and their Ruler. Therefore, of course, people ought to submit to Him and obey His commandments.

20- Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word. 21- Bless ye the Lord, all ye his hosts; ye ministers of his, that do his pleasure.
1- The great God who dwells in the heavens is glorified by the angels, and these are distinguished by the following:
a- They belong to God and are set apart for Him ("his angels").
b- They have great strength that gives them the ability to do many services for God, far above the strength of human beings.
c- They are obedient to God's commands and submissive to Him.

2- God also blesses His hosts, and they are the believers in God on earth, who share with the angels in praising God and serving Him, and strive to please Him by keeping His commandments and keeping away from all evil.
22- Bless the Lord, all his works in all places of his dominion: bless the Lord, O my soul.

1- In conclusion he calls on all the works of the Lord to bless Him and praise Him because of His greatness. And God's works include not only the angels and human beings, but also all creatures, living and inanimate. For all of them praise Him by following the order that God created for them. And the leader of creation, who is man, leads it in praise by his obedience to God and his prayers.

2- He ends the Psalm by calling his soul to bless God and praise Him, as he began the Psalm; that is, the life of man from its beginning to its end ought to be filled with praise and thanksgiving to God, just as all eternity is praise.
The most important of your works on earth is prayer and the praise of God; when you become skilled in it, you deserve to join the heavenly worshippers and to enjoy the vision of God.
God the glorified Creator: "Bless the Lord, O my soul. O Lord my God, thou art very great" (v. 1). Introduction:
1- Its writer: This Psalm has no title, that is, it is one of the "orphan" Psalms, but the Septuagint attributes it to David.

2- There is a similarity between this Psalm and the one before it, for both praise God, but the preceding Psalm praises Him for His mercy with His people, whereas this Psalm shows God's care for the whole of nature.

3- This Psalm is also similar to the first and second chapters of the Book of Genesis, but it is to be noted that the Book of Genesis concentrates on the creation that God created, whereas this Psalm concentrates on the greatness of the Creator who cares for all creation.

4- This Psalm is liturgical; the Jews used to chant it on the morning of the great Day of Atonement, when God permits the high priest to enter the Holy of Holies, because this day is a symbol of the renewal of creation, as the Psalm mentions (v. 30), and it is a symbol of the great Friday on which our High Priest, Christ our God, offered Himself and redeemed us on the cross; therefore we declare that He is the Creator and Shepherd of all creation, and we glorify Him.
5- There is a similarity between this Psalm and Psalm 19 (Ps 19), because both show God the great Creator who cares for His creation and is glorified in it.
6- This Psalm does not occur in the prayers of the Agpeya.

entries.section: (1) God the Creator of heaven and earth

paragraphs.text: Bless the Lord, O my soul. O Lord my God, thou art very great; thou art clothed with honour and majesty.

1- The Psalm begins with the praise of God when the writer of the Psalm calls his soul to bless God. The writer speaks proudly about God, so he says "my God", that is, there is a special relationship between him and God, and he says to Him "thou art very great", not in the sense that He has increased in greatness, for He is perfect in Himself from eternity, but He has become great in the eyes of the writer of the Psalm when he perceived His care and His power which created the world and cares for it to order it. And everyone who believes in God and is purified by repentance can perceive the greatness of God.

2- The writer of the Psalm likens God to a great man who has put on majesty and honour, meaning the greatness of God that appears before people in His creation and His care for the world. Glory and majesty cling to Him as clothes cling to a person.

entries.section: (1) God the Creator of heaven and earth

paragraphs.text: Who coverest thyself with light as with a garment: who stretchest out the heavens like a curtain:
Curtain: a piece of cloth or skin that is easily stretched out, like a tent or a veil.

1- God is light and the source of all light, so the writer of the Psalm expresses this by saying "who coverest thyself with light", that is, light clings to Him, and He is the Creator of light. Also He created the heavens by His word with ease, as a person stretches out the curtain of a tent, that is, the cloth of the tent, with ease. And whoever believes in the great God, as in (v. 1), enjoys His light, and then His word, which works in him with ease.

2- God's covering Himself with light points to the Incarnation of Christ in His pure body, that is, a body of light. As for us believers, we put on the light, that is, Christ, if we walk in His commandments. And light reveals everything, so God, who covers Himself with light, searches the hearts and reins, and nothing is hidden from Him. And He stretched out the heaven after He created light on the first day, to declare that although heaven is His dwelling, we human beings who live on the earth cannot see His light, but we see something of His light as much as we are able to bear. Now we see Him as in a mirror, but there in heaven we shall see Him face to face (1 Cor 13:12), that is, God reveals to us some of His light. And as much as we live with Him, He reveals to us the mysteries of His light, so we enjoy fellowship with Him.

3- And God, who covers Himself with light, lit up the world when He created light, and consequently there could afterward be life for man and all creatures; and God also enlightens our hearts with the knowledge of Him, so we are filled with joy.

entries.section: (1) God the Creator of heaven and earth

paragraphs.text: Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters: who maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the wings of the wind:
His chambers: the plural of "chamber", the upper room in the house; what is meant by it is heaven.

1- The writer of the Psalm shows the greatness of God in His creation of the heaven, which is water in the form of vapor, and He made it a roof for the earth and for everything above it, man, animals and birds. God's power is manifested in His control of this water, which is the cloud, so it cannot condense and come down as rain except by His command, and in the amount that He wills for the benefit of man. Job speaks of the cloud, likening it to a waterskin full of water, which God holds in His hand so that the whole earth is not flooded (Job 26:8).

2- God rides upon the cloud and walks upon the wind, which the writer here likens to wings, like the wings of a bird. For God is the Creator of all these and their Controller, and He rides above them or walks upon them.

And because of the greatness of the cloud and the mist, it represents the presence of God, for its height above the earth and its splendor, as the mist used to cover the tent of meeting, or the temple of Solomon, at the presence of God (Ex 20:
21; 1 Kgs 8:12), and when God came down on the mountain and gave Moses the commandments and the Law (Deut 5:22).

3- The clouds, that is, the mist, represent mystery, so they are a symbol of the sacraments of the Church, and the waters are the waters of Baptism, and the winds point to the Holy Spirit who works in the Church, the sacraments and the believers.

In sum, God, who in His thought is exalted above all, works in His children in the Church to fill them with His power and give them all their needs, so He makes His earthly children angels who live in heaven while they are on earth.

entries.section: (1) God the Creator of heaven and earth

paragraphs.text: Who maketh his angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire:

1- God is the Creator of the angels, and He created them winds, that is, spirits with great abilities in understanding and movement. They are spirits who perceive God's love and greatness, so they praise Him always, obey Him, serve Him and take care of human beings according to His commands. They are spirits whom man does not see, but he feels their work.

2- God also created the angels a flaming fire, and that by His fiery Holy Spirit, and they are aflame with the love of God and reject evil; for fire consumes impurities and thorns, which are a symbol of sin, and they carry out God's commands quickly like the flame of fire.

entries.section: (1) God the Creator of heaven and earth

paragraphs.text: Who laid the foundations of the earth, that it should not be removed for ever.

1- The greatness of God also appears in establishing the earth as though it were on foundations, as the ancients believed. By foundations God here means the stability of the earth, although the earth turns on itself every day, but by God's wisdom we do not feel this, so we live in security.
2- The earth bears human beings, and the believers, if they stand firm in Christ the cornerstone, are not shaken.

entries.section: (1) God the Creator of heaven and earth

paragraphs.text: Thou coveredst it with the deep as with a garment: the waters stood above the mountains.

1- The waters covered everything at the beginning of creation, and God said let the dry land appear and let the waters be gathered together into one place, and He called them seas, and He called the dry land earth (Gen 1:9); that is, the earth with its mountains was covered with water, then it appeared at God's command. And the waters did not flood the earth again except in the Flood in the days of Noah, and they will not flood it again as God promised (Gen 8:21).
2- The mountains are a symbol of the saints, the Apostles and the servants. And the waters above them are the work of the Holy Spirit in them, and His blessing upon their heads.

entries.section: (1) God the Creator of heaven and earth

paragraphs.text: 7- At thy rebuke they fled; at the voice of thy thunder they hasted away. 8- They go up by the mountains; they go down by the valleys unto the place which thou hast founded for them. 9- Thou hast set a bound that they may not pass over; that they turn not again to cover the earth.
Thy thunder: God's thunder, that is, His voice, His word and His command.
A bound: limits.
The valleys: the lands.

1- God commanded the waters, and they moved quickly to flood the earth with the Flood in the days of Noah, so they covered the mountains and the valleys, but after this God commanded them to withdraw, and the earth appeared again, and Noah and those with him came down from the ark. And God also reassured man by setting limits for the sea that it does not pass, so that it does not flood the earth, and even gave him a sign in the heaven, the rainbow, when the rains fall heavily and the seven colors of the spectrum appear in the sky, so that he may know that God will not flood the earth with a flood again. All this confirms the greatness and authority of God, and at the same time shows God's wrath against evil, and His love and care for His believing children.
2- God permits trials to cover the Church in order to discipline her so that she repents, then He lifts them again, and blesses His children when they repent and rejoice in God's gifts.
3- The verses (vv. 5-9) tell us of God's creation of the earth on the third day (Gen 1:9, 10).

God created heaven and earth for your sake, and everything on the earth for your benefit, and nothing happens except by His command, so be reassured, for He is the Upholder of all, and He is your Father who loves you and cares for you; so hold fast to His commandments, and abide in His Church, and you will enjoy fellowship with Him.

entries.section: (2) God who sustains man and beast

paragraphs.text: 10- He sendeth the springs into the valleys, which run among the hills. 11- They give drink to every beast of the field:
the wild asses quench their thirst. 12- By them shall the fowls of the heaven have their habitation, which sing among the branches.
The wild asses: the wild donkey.
Their thirst: their being thirsty.

1- In these following verses the writer of the Psalm tells us about God who cares for His creation, for He is not content with preparing the waters of the seas and the rivers for creation, but also makes springs of water burst forth from the underground waters that are in the earth, so they run everywhere, even among the mountains, to water not only man, but also the animals and the plants and the birds that fly above the trees and on the mountains. And He waters the tame animals and the wild animals. And when the animals drink the water they graze freely, while the birds sing on the branches, praising God who cares for them.

2- God cares not only for man but also for the animals and the birds, so that the hearts of people may be moved to have compassion on the animals, the birds, the plants and the trees. And on the other hand, if God has compassion on the animals and the plants, He of course has compassion on the leader of creation, that is, man.

entries.section: (2) God who sustains man and beast

paragraphs.text: 13- He watereth the hills from his chambers: the earth is satisfied with the fruit of thy works.

1- God waters the whole earth, even the highest thing in it, the mountains. If the rivers and springs water the valleys, God waters the mountains from His chambers, that is, the clouds, with rains. And the mountains are a symbol of the saints, whom God waters from heaven with His Holy Spirit, so they are continually filled with His grace.

2- God's works, that is, the waters that water the plants and the trees, yield fruits with which everyone on the earth, man and animal, is satisfied. And this is a symbol of the work of the Holy Spirit in the Apostles, the priests and the servants, for He gives them His spiritual fruits, which overflow upon everyone who needs to hear the word of God, and satisfy him.

entries.section: (2) God who sustains man and beast

paragraphs.text: 14- He causeth the grass to grow for the cattle, and herb for the service of man: that he may bring forth food out of the earth;

1- God cares for the food of the animals, so He gives them grass to eat, which is the fast-growing plants. As for man, who cares for farming, He gives him herbs, that is, vegetables, and also fruit, and also the crops that give bread, such as wheat, maize and barley. For God cares to satisfy all His creatures. And the meaning of this verse is found in (Ps 147:8).
2- The bread is the word of God that satisfies our spirits, and it is Christ, incarnate in the fullness of time to redeem us and satisfy us.

entries.section: (2) God who sustains man and beast

paragraphs.text: 15- And wine that maketh glad the heart of man, and oil to make his face to shine, and bread which strengtheneth man's heart.

1- God cares for man above all creatures, so He gives him bread to support him bodily, and wine also, that is, the fermented juice of the grape, whose vines were widespread in the land of the Jews, gives him health and vitality that appear in the shining of his face. And if some people drink strong wine that makes them drunk, this is a deviation that has no relation to the verse, and the Holy Bible forbids it.

2- It is clear that the wine and the bread are a symbol of the Body and Blood of Christ, which satisfy man spiritually, so he rejoices and his face shines and his heart is glad, and he leans upon them in all his life.

entries.section: (2) God who sustains man and beast

paragraphs.text: 16- The trees of the Lord are full of sap; the cedars of Lebanon, which he hath planted;

1- The trees, including the cedars of Lebanon, tall and evergreen, which God created and planted, are all satisfied with God's water and the richness of the earth, so they grow and extend to a great height, and thank God who gives them life.

2- The cedars of Lebanon are tall trees, a symbol of the holy believers who are raised up to heaven by their many prayers. And just as the trees are evergreen, so the saints are full of spiritual life, and God has established them to be a light to the world. And they are satisfied by the overflow of the Holy Spirit upon them.

entries.section: (2) God who sustains man and beast

paragraphs.text: 17- Where the birds make their nests: as for the stork, the fir trees are her house.

The stork: a bird with a long beak and long legs, which flies to great heights and fights the eagle and overcomes it. It is a friend of man, and eats insects, frogs and mice from the fields. And it builds its nests at the tops of trees and on electric wires.
The fir (cypress): tall trees that grow in Lebanon, perennial and evergreen, which rival the cedar in height.

1- Small birds, such as sparrows, or large ones, such as the stork, take refuge in the tall trees, and make a dwelling for themselves in them, and settle in them, and praise God who feeds them and provides for them their dwellings and their settling.

2- The tall trees such as the cedar and the cypress are a symbol of the saints, to whom beginners in the spiritual life take refuge, to learn from them and cling to them; but they must rise toward heaven by their prayers, to learn the spiritual life, as the sparrows and the stork fly to the tops of the trees.

3- The cypress is a sweet-smelling tree, evergreen and rising to heaven, and the woodworm does not eat it, so it is a symbol of the incarnate Christ, the source of life, who came down from heaven and is also without sin, so evil (the woodworm) does not come near Him.

entries.section: (2) God who sustains man and beast

paragraphs.text: 18- The high hills are a refuge for the wild goats; and the rocks for the conies.
The wild goats: the plural of "wa'l", the mountain goat, which is distinguished by activity and speed of movement.
The conies: a small animal that resembles the rabbit.

The wild goats can attack snakes and eat them, and therefore they dwell in the mountains and fear nothing, so God gave them strength and activity to dwell in the mountains. As for the cony, it is a weak animal that cannot dig a dwelling for itself, so it takes shelter in the rock. It is an unclean animal in the law of the Jews, like the stork, and yet God gave them to dwell in the rocks and the cypress, as Christ receives repentant sinners.

How great are Your arrangements, O God, for You give life to all Your creatures in the way that suits each kind; how much more, then, do You care for man, Your image and likeness. Therefore my soul praises You at all times, and rejoices when it sees You in Your creation and Your works, so that my heart may cling to You always.

entries.section: (3) God the Creator of the sun and moon

paragraphs.text: 19- He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down.

1- This verse speaks of what God created on the fourth day, that is, the two great lights, the sun and the moon, and how by them God ordered the seasons, that is, time, with the existence of night and day through the earth's turning on itself once every day, and the seasons of the year through the earth's turning around the sun once every year. The sun knows when it will set each day, and the moon knows when it will appear each night. And by this God orders the life of man, so he works in the day and sleeps in the night.

2- The sun is a symbol of the Sun of Righteousness, our Lord Jesus Christ, and the moon of the Church, which reflects the light of Christ the Sun of Righteousness, and so shines upon the whole world. On the other hand, the moon is also a symbol of the Jews and the Law, which prepared the way for Christ, who came in the fullness of time and knows when He will set, that is, die and redeem mankind. Therefore the spiritual person must know the source of his life, who is Christ, and cling to Him, and prepare every day for his end and for eternal life.

entries.section: (3) God the Creator of the sun and moon

paragraphs.text: 20- Thou makest darkness, and it is night: wherein all the beasts of the forest do creep forth. The forest: uninhabited places, such as mountains and deserts and all abandoned places.

1- When the sun and its light go away, night comes upon the earth, for God permits the night so that man may be calm and sleep, and on the other hand leave the works of the world and be occupied with prayer and praise.

2- The wild beasts use the night to come out and creep and seek prey, and they are a symbol of Satan, who takes man unawares to make him fall into sin, which is symbolized by the darkness; but God protects His children who are spiritually watchful, and gives them spiritual alertness, understanding and strength, so the devil cannot overcome them. But those who forget God are in spiritual darkness and it is easy for the devil to devour them.

entries.section: (3) God the Creator of the sun and moon

paragraphs.text: 21- The young lions roar after their prey, and seek their meat from God. 22- The sun ariseth, they gather themselves together, and lay them down in their dens.
Their dens: their lairs, that is, their dwelling or their holes.
Lay them down: lie down and rest.

1- The young lions, which are the cubs of lions, move at night and give their loud voices to frighten the one they attack and devour. In this they seek their food from God, for they cannot devour except by His permission, as we see that when Daniel was cast into the den, God prevented the lions from devouring him (Dan 6:22). But when the sun rises these cubs hide in their holes.

2- The demons work in the darkness, that is, in man's heedlessness, or when he is far from God, but when the Sun of Righteousness rises, that is, when God gives light to His children who take refuge in Him, the demons fear and flee far from them.

entries.section: (3) God the Creator of the sun and moon

paragraphs.text: 23- Man goeth forth unto his work and to his labour until the evening.

1- In the day, that is, in the light of the sun, man goes forth and does all his works until the evening, that is, at the end of the day, as Christ said, "Walk while ye have the light, lest darkness come upon you" (Jn 12:35).

2- The day until the evening is a symbol of the whole lifetime, so man ought to use the opportunity of life to live with God and prepare for eternity, and not fear if he has fallen in the night, meaning the darkness of sin and not only the material night, but rise quickly and repent, and God receives him, and he resumes his striving with firm hope.

3- If obstacles are found in the ministry, the priests and servants should not be troubled, but continue the preaching and the service, trusting in the power of God, which defeats the hindrances of the demons, and they gladden the heart of God by the souls that return to Him.

Remember the Resurrection of Christ at the beginning of every day to renew your activity and your vows to God, and begin with vigor a new life with Him, so pray the prayer of Prime, and set out in your spiritual life and your works and glorify God.

entries.section: (4) God the Creator of the sea creatures

paragraphs.text: 24- O Lord, how manifold are thy works! in wisdom hast thou made them all: the earth is full of thy riches.

1- God's works are great in all His creatures, because God ordered them all with wisdom, so every animal, or being, or inanimate thing is exact in its making and moves in an exact order to be in harmony with the rest of creation; all this God made with wisdom for the service of man, that he may enjoy it and that it may help him to reach God.

2- God filled the earth with His creatures, whether the heavenly bodies, or the plants and animals on the earth, and the birds in the sky, and the animals that live in the water, whether in the seas or the rivers. For God is rich in the variety of His creatures and the multitude of His works, which dazzles man and reassures him, so he leans upon God and enjoys fellowship with Him.

entries.section: (4) God the Creator of the sea creatures

paragraphs.text: 25- So is this great and wide sea, wherein are things creeping innumerable, both small and great beasts. 26- There go the ships: there is that leviathan, whom thou hast made to play therein.
Things creeping: everything that creeps on the earth, or at the bottom of the sea, or on the shore.
Leviathan: a large sea animal, whether among the animals that have become extinct or those that live now, such as the whale and the crocodile.

1- God created the wide sea, and created in it many sea animals, large in size and small, all of which live in the water and die if they leave it. And some of them live in the water and on land, and these are the amphibians. For God is diverse in His creation and inventive in His making, and when man contemplates it he sees the greatness of God.

2- This great, fearful sea, in which man drowns and dies if he dives into it and does not come out, yet at the same time ships can go in it freely and quickly. And the ships are a symbol of the Church, which lives in the midst of the world, but the world does not enter it by its thought. And the ships are also a symbol of the cross, which conquered Satan and bound him; for Leviathan is a symbol of Satan, who plays in the world (the sea) and fights the children of God, but he cannot attack the ships except by God's permission, just as Satan cannot conquer the Church, but on the contrary, by the power of the cross the believers in Christ tread down the power of the enemy and Satan.

entries.section: (4) God the Creator of the sea creatures

paragraphs.text: 27- These wait all upon thee; that thou mayest give them their meat in due season. 28- That thou givest them they gather: thou openest thine hand, they are filled with good. 29- Thou hidest thy face, they are troubled: thou takest away their breath, they die, and return to their dust.

1- All the animals that live in the sea, or the waters, God feeds, and they gather their food from His hand, but when God wills He ends their life, so they die, large or small, and cleave to the earth and its dust.

2- God is the source of life for all His children, so He gives them their spiritual and bodily food, on condition that they seek Him and stretch out their hands, and He gives them, and as much as they pray they enjoy fellowship with Him. But if they go far from Him and walk in sin, He hides His face from them, and they die in their sins, since they have become carnal and earthly. And if they continue so they perish and die far from God.

entries.section: (4) God the Creator of the sea creatures

paragraphs.text: 30- Thou sendest forth thy spirit, they are created: and thou renewest the face of the earth.

1- God, who created the world of old, is He who renews life, and creates new creatures every day; for He is the giver of life, whether He creates a human being, or an animal, or a plant, for all of them are His handiwork, and consequently He must renew them, and at their head man.

2- Man is weak and liable to fall into sins, but if he repents God renews life in him in Baptism and the sacrament of confession, and by partaking of the Body and Blood, and by the work of the Holy Spirit in him he walks in the new life and regains his way to eternal life.

Do not be troubled by the multitude of your sins, or their ugliness, because your God is able to forgive them for you and renew your life, so rise quickly to make up for what you have missed by the power of God, and complete your striving, trusting in God's support for you, until you receive your heavenly crown.
31- The glory of the Lord shall endure for ever: the Lord shall rejoice in his works.

1- The children of God, and all His creatures, glorify Him throughout their life on the earth, then God raises man to the Kingdom to glorify Him for ever; that is, the glorification of God is continual from now and to the age, that is, for ever.

2- The glorification of God gladdens the heart of man, and God also rejoices in His children who praise Him; not because He needs their praise, but because He loves His children and rejoices in their salvation and their joy.

3- God rejoiced when He created the world and said of it that it was good, and very good, and rested on the seventh day. And He also rejoiced at the completion of the redemption of mankind on the cross. And He rejoices at the repentance and salvation of His children: "joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth" (Lk 15:7). And He rejoices in the praise of His children and the submission of all creation to Him in its service to man.
32- He looketh on the earth, and it trembleth: he toucheth the hills, and they smoke.

1- When people on the earth sin, and God looks at them in His wrath, they are very afraid, and this great earth becomes like a leaf trembling before the wind, as the earth quaked when Christ was crucified, and when He rose from the dead (Mt 27:51). But by repentance people obtain God's forgiveness, and by redemption they obtain their new life in Him.

2- The great mountains, which have nothing like them in strength and in height above the earth, smoke if the Lord touches them, as happened when the Lord appeared to Moses and his people on the mountain when Moses received the commandments and the Law (Ex 20:18). And however great a person becomes in position, or power, or even in the spiritual life, if he falls into pride, he smokes and trembles if God touches him in His wrath and permits him a trial. Therefore the children of God ought to live in His fear with humility, and walk in the Spirit, and so enjoy His love and care.
33- I will sing unto the Lord as long as I live: I will sing praise to my God while I have my being.

The opportunity of life is for repentance and returning to God with all the heart, and this is the sweetest song. Then the heart opens with love, and thanks God who forgives and gives; for God satisfies the heart with His love, so it praises Him and glorifies Him all its life, until it goes forth to the Kingdom to continue its praise.
34- My meditation of him shall be sweet: I will be glad in the Lord.

God rejoices in the repentance of His children, their prayers and their thanksgiving, and delights in their voices, as He said, "my delights were with the sons of men" (Prov 8:31). And when God rejoices He gladdens the heart of man also, so his joy in being with God increases, and he increases in praise, and He grants him spiritual gifts that cannot be expressed; he tastes something of them on earth as much as he can bear, and then wonderful things in the heavens.
35- Let the sinners be consumed out of the earth, and let the wicked be no more. Bless thou the Lord, O my soul. Praise ye the Lord.

1- If the children of God set out in a life of repentance and prayer and enjoyment of fellowship with God, the wicked are immersed in their sins and reject God, so nothing awaits them then but eternal torment, and they have no place with God.

2- In view of all the works of God that this Psalm mentions, the writer of the Psalm ends his words by calling his soul to bless God and praise Him continually, and to rejoice with all the believers until it reaches the joys of eternity.

How sweet is the praise of God; for it fills the soul with peace and joy, and frees it and liberates it from the chains of the world, so it keeps away from sins, and sets out to taste the sweetness of being with God, and breathes the fragrance of eternity while it is still in the body.
God's care for His people: "O give thanks unto the Lord; call upon his name" (v. 1). Introduction:

1- Its writer: This Psalm is one of the "orphan" Psalms that have no title, and the name of the writer is not mentioned in them, but most of the Fathers incline to the view that its writer is David. For it has the same style of writing as David, and there is not one verse that shows otherwise.
2- When was it written? David wrote it after he brought the ark of the covenant of God back to Jerusalem (1 Chr 16:1, 7).
3- This Psalm is counted among four Psalms that show God's promises and His faithfulness to His people throughout their history, and they are Psalms 78, 106, 136 in addition to this Psalm.

4- This Psalm is liturgical, for it was sung at the beginnings of the months, the feast of the Dedication, and the three great feasts, the Passover, Pentecost and Tabernacles, as appears from (1 Chr 16:8-22); indeed, this chapter contains a number of the verses mentioned in this Psalm. So this Psalm was used in worship.
5- This Psalm calls every person who believes in God to meditate on His wonderful works, so that he thanks Him and praises Him.
6- This Psalm does not occur in the prayers of the Agpeya.

entries.section: (1) The call of the believers to praise

paragraphs.text: 1- O give thanks unto the Lord; call upon his name: make known his deeds among the Gentiles.
Talk ye of all his wondrous works. 3- Glory ye in his holy name: let the heart of them rejoice that seek the Lord.

1- The writer of the Psalm calls the believers in God to give thanks to Him and repeat His great name; that is, to remember His gracious person, so that their faith increases, and then he charges them with the responsibility of making the pagan nations know the greatness of God so that they may believe in Him.
2- This verse is a prophecy about the work of the Apostles, the priests and the servants in the New Covenant. And it defines for them a basic task: a- Prayer and praise.
b- Preaching to unbelievers so that they may know God and His works with His people.

3- The writer of the Psalm calls the believers to glory in God, and not in material things, or positions, or power, as Peter did with the lame man at the Beautiful Gate, so he healed him in the name of Christ (Acts 3:6). And the glorying is in God, because He is able to do all things, and loves His children and answers them.
4- The inevitable result of praise, preaching and glorying in the Lord is that a person rejoices and enjoys fellowship with God.

entries.section: (1) The call of the believers to praise

paragraphs.text: 4- Seek the Lord, and his strength: seek his face evermore. 5- Remember his marvellous works that he hath done; his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth; 6- O ye seed of Abraham his servant, ye children of Jacob his chosen. 7- He is the Lord our God: his judgments are in all the earth.

1- The people of God in the Old Testament, who are the descendants of Abraham and Jacob, seek the Lord and seek His face, and remember His miraculous works with them. By this praise their faith is confirmed and they rejoice.
And seeking the Lord is not only by words, but also by obeying His commandments, and especially when a person feels his sin and weakness, he seeks God and asks for Him with humility, need and faith.

2- The face of the Lord points to the Incarnation of the Lord of glory Jesus Christ, and consequently the seed of Abraham, and the people of God in the New Testament, are the Christians; because the Lord's judgments are in all the earth (v. 7) and not only for the Jews, for the Gentiles believed in Christ in addition to the Jews.

I wish, my brother, that in all your needs and afflictions you would seek God first, and lean on Him before you think of people or money, while taking care to do your duty with all your energy; and trust that God hears you and moves the whole universe for your sake, and be at ease because He is your God who loves you.

entries.section: (2) God's promise to Abraham and his seed

paragraphs.text: 8- He hath remembered his covenant for ever, the word which he commanded to a thousand generations. 9- Which covenant he made with Abraham, and his oath unto Isaac; 10- And confirmed the same unto Jacob for a law, and to Israel for an everlasting covenant: 11- Saying, Unto thee will I give the land of Canaan, the lot of your inheritance.

The lot of your inheritance: in ancient times land was measured by the cord, so what is meant is the land of Canaan, whose measure by the cord was known, which God gave to His people, and He drove out its wicked inhabitants from it and destroyed them.

1- God promised Abraham to give him the land of Canaan, for him and for his seed (Gen 13:14, 15). And He swore to Isaac that He would give him Canaan as an inheritance (Gen 26:3, 4). And likewise to Jacob the son of Isaac He confirmed this promise (Gen 28:13-15), and especially after He changed the name of Jacob to Israel He affirmed the promise (Gen 35:9-15). And although they did not receive these promises in their lifetime, God is true in His promises, and He gave it to their seed.

2- God's promise to the fathers was to a thousand generations (v. 8), and by this He means eternity (v. 10), for these promises of blessing are not meant only for the seed of Abraham in the Old Testament, but rather the seed of Abraham in the New Testament, that is, the Christians, those who do the works of Abraham (Jn 8:39), to whom He will give the Kingdom of Heaven as an eternal inheritance, and not merely the land of Canaan that flows with milk and honey.

entries.section: (2) God's promise to Abraham and his seed

paragraphs.text: 12- When they were but a few men in number; yea, very few, and strangers in it. 13- When they went from one nation to another, from one kingdom to another people; 14- He suffered no man to do them wrong: yea, he reproved kings for their sakes; 15- Saying, Touch not mine anointed, and do my prophets no harm.

1- The descendants of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob were a small number, seventy persons (Ex 1:5); they moved from the land of Canaan and went to Egypt, then returned from it to the land of Canaan, after they had multiplied and become two million, but they were strangers. For the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob lived in tents, and their seed who dwelt in the land of Canaan - after four hundred years - continued to keep the Feast of Tabernacles, which reminds them of the sojourning of the world.

2- God preserved the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and reproved kings for their sake when He reproved Pharaoh for the sake of Abraham, and kept his wife so that Pharaoh did not wrong her (Gen 12:17), and Abimelech king of Gerar for the sake of Isaac (Gen 20:3). And Laban for the sake of Jacob his sister's son, so He did not allow him to harm him (Gen 32, 33). And when He says "Touch not mine anointed" He means the fathers, and although they were not anointed with oil like the priests and the prophets who came from their seed, they were anointed by the Holy Spirit, and received many blessings, like those who were anointed with oil. And God called them prophets although they did not prophesy, but they were like the prophets, that is, anointed by the Holy Spirit (Gen 20:6, 7).
If you are weak and have only a little, trust that by the blessing of God you will become many; for God blesses you and keeps you, and reproves the demons who try to harm you.

entries.section: (3) Joseph from prison to the throne

paragraphs.text: 16- Moreover he called for a famine upon the land: he brake the whole staff of bread.
The staff of bread: a wooden staff on which bread is kept.

God permitted a great famine in Egypt and all the neighboring countries, and God broke everything in which bread is kept, or from which bread could be made, that is, there was no longer any food in the land. And this famine was an opportunity for Joseph the righteous to shine as manager not only of Egypt but of the whole earth, so he fed them, and the descendants of Jacob came to Egypt to sojourn there, and Joseph provided for them.

entries.section: (3) Joseph from prison to the throne

paragraphs.text: 17- He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant: 18- Whose feet they hurt with fetters: he was laid in iron: 19- Until the time that his word came: the word of the Lord tried him. 20- The king sent and loosed him; even the ruler of the people, and let him go free. 21- He made him lord of his house, and ruler of all his substance:

1- Joseph's brothers rose against him and sold him as a slave, and he came to Egypt to work in the house of Potiphar, and Potiphar's wife rose against him with her lust, but he refused evil, so he was thrown into prison and bound with iron.

All this was by God's permission, to prepare a place for the people of the sons of Jacob, and to prepare Joseph spiritually and psychologically, so that he would be strengthened and trust in God through the sufferings and his holding fast to purity. So God tested Joseph and he succeeded greatly, and he always enjoyed fellowship with God.

2- God promised Joseph long before, through his dreams, that he would be a ruler over his brothers, and years passed in which God tested him with many afflictions in the land of Egypt, until the time came in which the word of God was fulfilled, when Pharaoh dreamed his dream and no one interpreted it for him. And although Joseph had interpreted a dream for the king's cupbearer in prison, and asked him to remember him to the king, he forgot him for two years, until the king's cupbearer remembered Joseph when an interpreter was needed for Pharaoh's dream. So the word of God was fulfilled, and Pharaoh summoned him and he interpreted the dream and gave him the solution, so he made him ruler over all Egypt. God cares for His children through afflictions, and fulfills His promises at the right time, and raises them above all they imagine, as He raised Joseph to the throne of Egypt.

entries.section: (3) Joseph from prison to the throne

paragraphs.text: 22- To bind his princes at his pleasure; and teach his senators wisdom. 23- Israel also came into Egypt; and Jacob sojourned in the land of Ham.
To bind his princes: the rulers of Egypt submit to Joseph.
His senators: the elders of Egypt learned from Joseph's wisdom and management.
The land of Ham: the land of Egypt.

Joseph ruled over all Egypt, and gathered the wheat into storehouses, and all the rulers of Egypt, indeed the whole world, submitted to him. And when the famine came, and all the Egyptians came to buy from him, they even sold themselves as slaves, after Joseph had bought everything that was in Egypt and made it subject to Pharaoh. And Joseph's brothers and his father came to Egypt to live in it, and Joseph hosted them, and they lived. All this arrangement was from God so that His people would not perish from hunger, and He used Joseph to provide for them.

God arranges your whole life, so do not be troubled however many afflictions come upon you, for He is able to keep you during them, and to turn every evil into your good, as He did with Joseph, and even to make you grow spiritually, and you feel God with you in everything.
24- And he increased his people greatly; and made them stronger than their enemies.

God blessed His people who entered the land of Egypt, who are the descendants of Jacob, and their number was seventy persons (Ex 1:5), and over the years they multiplied abundantly by the grace of God, so that in about four hundred years they became two million persons. This was at first useful to the Egyptians, since they enslaved them and forced them to work in the cities, in addition to shepherding the flocks, but their great increase aroused fear in the hearts of the Egyptians (Ex 1:10), and God permitted the evil that was in the hearts of the Egyptians toward His people to appear, so they tried to humiliate them and force them to work for nothing, hoping that from the toil a great number of them would die, but by the blessing of God their number increased. So they made plans to weaken them, such as killing the male children through the women who deliver the Hebrew women. Then they also schemed against them, as Pharaoh commanded that the male children be thrown into the river Nile, but by the grace of God all these attempts failed, and on the contrary, the more they humiliated them, the more they grew and multiplied (Ex 1:12). For whom God protects and keeps, no one can harm.
26- He sent Moses his servant; and Aaron whom he had chosen.

God chose Moses, who according to Pharaoh's orders was supposed to be drowned in the river, but was brought up by God's arrangement in Pharaoh's palace by the princess, Pharaoh's daughter, who drew him out of the river. And when Moses grew up he went to the wilderness, and there God appeared to him in the bush and called him - he and Aaron his brother - to bring His people out of the land of Egypt. And so God delivered Moses from death, and made him a leader to deliver the people and bring them out of the land of Egypt. How wonderful are Your works, O Lord!
27- They shewed his signs among them, and wonders in the land of Ham.

God commanded Moses to meet - he and Aaron - the elders of Israel, and to announce to them that God would bring them out of Egypt, and would do signs before them; these were the turning of his rod into a serpent, and the turning of his hand to be leprous, then returning whole, and the turning of water into blood (Ex 4:1-9). So the elders believed and rejoiced. Then Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh and asked him to let the children of Israel go out of Egypt, but he did not agree. So God struck Egypt with wonderful signs, which are the ten plagues, and God intended to confirm the faith of His people and to call the Egyptians to faith through these plagues.
28- He sent darkness, and made it dark; and they rebelled not against his word.

1- God struck the Egyptians with ten plagues, and Pharaoh was hard of heart, so he refused to obey God. But in this verse he refers to the ninth plague, and it was severe and shows God's intense wrath; for it was complete darkness over all the land of Egypt, such as Egypt had not seen before. And at the same time there was light in the land of Goshen, where the children of Israel lived (Ex 10:21-23). And light is a symbol of the presence of God, while darkness is a symbol of sin and affliction. By this God struck their god Ra, that is, the sun, so that they would feel the weakness of their gods and believe in God.

2- "They rebelled not against his word": this applies to Moses and Aaron in their obedience to God and their confronting Pharaoh. And nature also did not rebel against God. As for the Egyptians, they obeyed God because of the severity of this trial, and they sent out the children of Israel after the next plague. For the ninth plague, in its severity, was a preparation for the most severe of the plagues, the tenth, concerning the killing of the firstborn.
29- He turned their waters into blood, and slew their fish.

1- The writer of the Psalm returns to the first plague, which was the turning of the river Nile, and all the waters that were in Egypt, into blood. By this He struck one of their great gods, the Nile, so that they would not worship it because of its weakness. And at the same time He caused them a huge problem, for they found no water to drink, so they were forced to dig wells of water to drink (Ex 7:19-25).

2- It was not the turning of the river to a red color but real blood, and the proof of this is that the fish that lived in the Nile died and stank, that is, the Nile and all that was in it lost life, and became a source of distress and disgust.
30- Their land brought forth frogs in abundance, in the chambers of their kings. 31- He spake, and there came divers sorts of flies, and lice in all their coasts.
Chambers: bedrooms.

1- The second plague on Egypt was the frogs, which spread in abundance in all the land, and entered the houses, the palaces and the temples, and defiled everything in Egypt, so they showed the weakness of the priests and the gods.

2- The frogs also entered Pharaoh's palace and the princes of Egypt, and troubled them, and defiled their houses, until they were very distressed. And they gathered the frogs that died and stank, and they corrupted the air of Egypt (Ps 78:45). All this in the hope that they would repent and return to God.

3- The third plague was the gnats, which spread in the land of Egypt, and with their stings troubled the Egyptians severely. And the fourth plague was the flies (resembling the beetle), which spread among the Egyptians with their gloomy appearance and troubled them. All this was in Egypt except the land of Goshen in which the children of Israel lived, which was not exposed to the ten plagues (Ex 8:22, 23).
32- He gave them hail for rain, and flaming fire in their land. 33- He smote their vines also and their fig trees; and brake the trees of their coasts.

1- The seventh plague was the falling of hail, which is sheets of ice that kill whomever they strike. And strangely, it was accompanied by fire from heaven to destroy the Egyptians. So it was a violent plague that killed many of the Egyptians who were outside their houses (Ex 9:18).

2- This plague broke the trees and the plants and burned them, so it ruined and devastated the land of Egypt, in the hope that this affliction would bring the Egyptians back to the mighty God, who surpasses all their gods.
34- He spake, and the locusts came, and caterpillars, and that without number, 35- And did eat up all the herbs in their land, and devoured the fruit of their ground.
Caterpillars: small locusts not yet fully grown.

The eighth plague was the swarms of locusts that attacked Egypt in huge numbers, in its different stages, whether the young locusts or the large locusts, which ate every green plant in Egypt, so they completed the ruin of the land after the plague of hail and fire. And by this the land of Egypt was utterly destroyed (Ex 10:12-15).
36- He smote also all the firstborn in their land, the chief of all their strength.

The tenth and last plague was the most severe of the plagues; for it killed all the firstborn of Egypt, man and beast, even the firstborn of Pharaoh, and it was terrifying as it took place at midnight, so there was crying and weeping in all Egypt. So Pharaoh finally submitted, and let the children of Israel go out of the land of Egypt.
37- He brought them forth also with silver and gold: and there was not one feeble person among their tribes. 38- Egypt was glad when they departed: for the fear of them fell upon them.

1- When Pharaoh let the children of Israel go out of Egypt, God gave them strength, so there was no sick or weak person among them. And they asked the Egyptians for silver and gold, and they gave them in abundance, to please them and bring them out of their land, since they were in great terror of them.

2- Despite Egypt's grief over its firstborn, it was glad to be rid of the power of the God of the children of Israel, who had terrified them. And the children of Israel were glad at the power of their God and their liberation from the slavery of Egypt.

I wish you would rely on God and trust in Him more than in every power you depend on, whether your understanding, or your position, or your knowledge, or your various abilities, for they are nothing before the power of God. And however great your weakness, you are stronger than all around you because of God's work in you and through you.

entries.section: (5) The wilderness of Sinai and the entry into Canaan

paragraphs.text: 39- He spread a cloud for a covering; and fire to give light in the night.
A covering: a cover.

1- When God brought His people out of Egypt, and their number was about two million persons (six hundred thousand men besides women and children) (Ex 12:37), He shaded them with the cloud so that the sun would not burn them. And at the same time the cloud went before them and they walked behind it. And at night a pillar of fire appeared to them, going before them to guide them in the way and give them light. And so God appears as the leader of His people, and their Father who cares for them and guides them.
2- God always shades His children and guides them, and works by His Holy Spirit in their hearts like fire to burn up their sins and kindle their hearts with His love.

entries.section: (5) The wilderness of Sinai and the entry into Canaan

paragraphs.text: 40- The people asked, and he brought quails, and satisfied them with the bread of heaven. 41- He opened the rock, and the waters gushed out; they ran in the dry places like a river.
The quail (salwa): a kind of migratory bird resembling the quail (samman).

1- God cared to provide for His people and feed them, so He gave them the bread of heaven every morning, which is the manna, and gave them also the quails, that they might be satisfied with meat and lack nothing. As for water, it came out for them from the rock when Moses struck it with the rod. So the people of God saw that their God is mighty, able to feed them in the barren wilderness with food and drink, however many they were, so that their faith in Him would be confirmed.

2- The coming down of the manna from heaven, and the quails with the wind, lifts the hearts of the people to God who is able to feed them spiritually also. And the wind is a symbol of the Spirit, for the Holy Spirit is the One who gives them life.
And the rock is a symbol of Christ, who by His death on the cross gave them the Holy Spirit, who is symbolized by the water of life and the river that flows in the dry wilderness of our hearts.

entries.section: (5) The wilderness of Sinai and the entry into Canaan

paragraphs.text: 42- For he remembered his holy promise, and Abraham his servant. 43- And he brought forth his people with joy, and his chosen with gladness:

God promised Abraham to bless him and his seed, and although long years passed, about four hundred years, God does not forget His promises or go back on them, so He remembered it, that is, He fulfilled it at the right time, and brought His people out by the might of His arm, and parted the Red Sea for them, so they crossed over, and Pharaoh and all his army perished because of the hardness of his heart. For after he let the people of the children of Israel go, he came back and felt the loss to Egypt in the departure of two million slaves, so he rose to pursue them to bring them back, and was drowned in the Red Sea. And when the people of God saw the power of their God in saving them from Pharaoh and his drowning, they praised Him and sang under the leadership of Miriam, the sister of Moses and Aaron, and this is the spiritual satisfaction after they had been satisfied materially.

entries.section: (5) The wilderness of Sinai and the entry into Canaan

paragraphs.text: 44- And gave them the lands of the heathen: and they inherited the labour of the people; 45- That they might observe his statutes, and keep his laws. Praise ye the Lord.

1- God punished the pagan peoples who lived in the land of Canaan for their many sins, toward which God had been very long-suffering, so He finally drove them out of the land of Canaan, and settled His people who believe in Him in their place.

2- By the children of Israel's possession of the land of Canaan, the promise of God that He gave to the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob was fulfilled. And the fulfillment of this promise helps the people of God to wait for the promise of the heavenly Jerusalem, that is, to live with God until they reach the Kingdom of Heaven.
3- The condition for the children of Israel's remaining firm in the land of Canaan was their keeping God's laws and statutes.
So because of their faith they remain in the land, just as God, because of the unbelief of the pagans, drove them out of their land.

4- God, who keeps His children, and guides them and provides for them in the wilderness of Sinai, completes His work, and brings them in and settles them in a land flowing with milk and honey, that is, abundant good things, and that is the land of Canaan.
As much as you hold fast to God's commandments you receive His power and His blessings, and by your keeping the commandment it keeps you in all your ways until it brings you to eternal bliss.
The people's rebellion and God's kindnesses: "Praise ye the Lord. O give thanks unto the Lord; for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
"Who can utter the mighty acts of the Lord?" (vv. 1, 2) Introduction:
1- Its writer: It is a Psalm without a title, that is, one of the "orphan" Psalms whose writer is not known. But many of the Fathers incline to attribute it to David.
2- When was it written? When the ark was brought back to Jerusalem from the house of Obed-edom the Gittite (1 Chr 16:

34-36), because it glorifies God who abounds in kindness. And there is another opinion that David wrote it when he was a fugitive in Gath, therefore it says "gather us from among the heathen" (v. 47).

3- There is a similarity between this Psalm and the one before it (Ps 105), for the first tells us of God's care for His people, while this Psalm tells us of God's faithfulness to His people despite their disobedience.
4- There is some similarity between this Psalm and (1 Chr 16), in which the bringing back of the ark of the covenant of God is mentioned.

5- There is a similarity between this Psalm and the prayers of Ezra (Ezra 9), Nehemiah (Neh 9), Daniel (Dan 9), and Baruch (Bar 2); in all of these the writer mentions the rebellion and errors of the people of God, and on the other hand God's faithfulness, love and kindness.

6- This Psalm shows the ugliness of our sins before God's kindnesses; therefore we praise Him. The meaning of this is that my falling into sin calls me to repentance, and does not hinder me from prayer and praise.
7- This Psalm does not occur in the prayers of the Agpeya.
8- This Psalm is among the Psalms that begin and end with Alleluia, and they are eight Psalms, which are, besides this Psalm, Pss 111, 113, 135, 146, 148, 149, 150.
Praise ye the Lord. O give thanks unto the Lord; for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.

This Psalm begins with the praise of God because He is good and merciful for ever; for His nature is mercy and goodness. Therefore the heart rejoices at this and begins with rejoicing; because man is a sinner and in need of God's forgiveness and mercy, as will appear from the details of this Psalm. And these sins call man to humility, and to singing of God's mercies.
2- Who can utter the mighty acts of the Lord? who can shew forth all his praise? 3- Blessed are they that keep judgment, and he that doeth righteousness at all times.

1- The writer of the Psalm asks, in the midst of the congregation of the believers, who can speak of God's great power and declare God's praises? And he answers in (v. 3) that the one who can praise God and declare His power is the one who keeps the truth, and always does righteousness. And he is the one who obeys the truth; that is, keeps His commandments.

2- "He that doeth righteousness at all times" is a clear prophecy about Christ, and the believers in Him join Him, those who enjoy fellowship with Him, that is, the saints, so they are able to praise God with all their hearts.

And everyone who strives in the way of righteousness and the keeping of the commandments advances in the way of praise, that is, praise is not words that the mouth repeats, but a life that a person lives, so he speaks of the greatness of God and glorifies Him.

4- Remember me, O Lord, with the favour that thou bearest unto thy people: O visit me with thy salvation; 5- That I may see the good of thy chosen, that I may rejoice in the gladness of thy nation, that I may glory with thine inheritance.

1- The writer of the Psalm feels his weakness, because he does not do righteousness at all times; therefore he asks God to remember him with the favour toward His people; that is, to be pleased with him; because God is merciful and loves His people. And he also asks for God's help, so he asks Him to visit him with His salvation, that is, to care for him and support him, so that he may keep the truth and do righteousness. Then he enters into tasting the fellowship with God which the chosen enjoy; not only on earth, but rather in heaven, and then he rejoices greatly and glories in God's mercy and kindnesses with all the believers who have received the eternal inheritance.

2- The writer of the Psalm sees with the eye of prophecy the Apostles and the believers of the New Testament, who enjoy the sight of Christ and the work of the Holy Spirit in the Church, where there are many spiritual good things that gladden the heart, and in which everyone who receives them glories. So he longs for the Incarnation of Christ, and the sight of the New Testament, and the birth of the Church.

I wish, my brother, that you would care about keeping God's commandments and applying them in your life, so that you may be satisfied and your tongue be set free to praise Him in the Church, and in your closet, and everywhere.

entries.section: (2) Rebellion in Egypt and the wilderness of Sinai

paragraphs.text: 6- We have sinned with our fathers, we have committed iniquity, we have done wickedly. 7- Our fathers understood not thy wonders in Egypt; they remembered not the multitude of thy mercies; but provoked him at the sea, even at the Red sea.
The Sea of Suph: the Red Sea.

1- With feelings of repentance and regret the writer of the Psalm declares on behalf of the people of God that they rebelled against God many times, and offended Him through the rebellion of the fathers. And the first rebellion was after their departure from the land of Egypt and their arrival at the Sea of Suph, when they saw Pharaoh with his army coming toward them.

So they murmured against Moses saying: Are there no graves in Egypt that you brought us out to die in the wilderness before the Sea of Suph? Did we not say to you: Leave us to live in the wilderness of Egypt, it is better than dying in the wilderness (Ex 14:11, 12).

2- This murmuring of the children of Israel took place after they had seen God's wonders in the ten plagues with which He struck the Egyptians, and at the same time His mercy on His people, which kept them from these plagues. They saw the wonders but did not understand them, and this is what happens with us to this day, for we see God's works with us but we do not understand, so we are agitated and anxious and murmur.

entries.section: (2) Rebellion in Egypt and the wilderness of Sinai

paragraphs.text: 8- Nevertheless he saved them for his name's sake, that he might make his mighty power to be known. 9- He rebuked the Red sea also, and it was dried up: so he led them through the depths, as through the wilderness. 10- And he saved them from the hand of him that hated them, and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy. 11- And the waters covered their enemies: there was not one of them left. 12- Then believed they his words; they sang his praise.
The depths: the many waters; what is meant by it is the depths of the sea.

1- In the face of the people's rebellion we did not see God's wrath, but on the contrary His power in saving them from Pharaoh and his army, for He rebuked the sea by means of Moses' striking the sea with his rod, so it was divided and the depths of the sea were uncovered, and became dry land like the wilderness, and the people of God crossed over in it to the other shore.

But Pharaoh and his army, who dared and pursued the children of Israel and did not fear their God who had struck them with the ten plagues, when Moses struck the sea a second time it returned as it was, and Pharaoh and all his army were drowned, and all of them died, and it was the strongest army in the world at that time; because Egypt was the first empire in the world, and it controlled those around it. So the children of Israel rejoiced and sang to God with thanksgiving and believed in Him.
