For God is steadfast, and His creatures like heaven are steadfast, and His word is also steadfast, which all heavenly creatures, that is, the angels, hold to. And in proportion as a person holds fast to God's commandments he keeps his peace and steadfastness, and becomes heavenly, and prepared to dwell in the Kingdom. On the contrary, by rejecting God's word the wicked are agitated, and move away from God and hasten to their fixed end, which is eternal torment.

2- Christ is the Word of God, firm in the heavens from eternity and for ever, and He became incarnate in the fullness of time to redeem us, but He prepared for us a heavenly place, and awaits us that we may be lifted up to Him after our life on earth, and remain in Him for ever.

3- God's word and promises, though they seem as far away as heaven is from earth, are firm and cannot change, as Christ declared (Mk 13:31), and must be fulfilled even if after a while. And waiting for God's promises lifts a person's heart to heaven, so he rises above all earthly lusts and lives a heavenly life, pure before God.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Thy faithfulness is unto all generations: thou hast established the earth, and it abideth. They continue this day according to thine ordinances: for all are thy servants.

1- The steadfast God also made His creatures steadfast, not only the heavens but the earth too, with all its conditions of day and night and the four seasons. All creatures, whether the sun, or the air, or the whole earth, are servants of God, that is, subject to Him. And therefore God's word and promises are firm.

2- If God's faithfulness is firm from generation to generation, what is meant is His steadfastness in His care and commandments for the Jewish people in ancient times, then the second generation, or the second age, which is the Church of the New Testament, so His promises and commandments for the Church are firm, and His judgments and word remain firm for ever in eternity.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Unless thy law had been my delights, I should then have perished in mine affliction. I will never forget thy precepts: for with them thou hast quickened me.

1- The prophet David remembers that he had fallen into sin, which caused him humiliation, but when he returned to God and began to recite His word he delighted in it; because He forgave him his sins and even gave him the joy of fellowship with Him. Therefore he promises God not to forget His word for ever, that is, all his life; because God's word is the secret of his life.

2- If Satan wants to make the believer fall into sin, the protection from his wars is in repeating God's commandments and reciting them and delighting in them; by this he lives with God and is fortified in Him, and therefore does not leave God's commandments all his life; even in eternity he will continue to enjoy the word of God, and there the sweetness of God's word will be revealed more and more.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (I am thine, save me; for I have sought thy precepts. The wicked have waited for me to destroy me: but I will consider thy testimonies.
I will consider thy testimonies.
I will consider: I will understand.

1- Since David delighted in the word of God and was always reciting it, he surrendered his life to God, and said to Him, "I am thine, save me", for I have sought thy precepts, and I will keep seeking them all my life. Therefore the divine grace works in him with power, and keeps him and protects him, however the wicked surround him and try to destroy him, but he held fast to understanding and repeating God's testimonies and commandments.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (I have seen an end of all perfection: but thy commandment is exceeding broad.

1- Everything that seems strong or perfect in the world has an end. David saw Goliath the giant, whom no one could stand before, fall by a stone from a sling, and Absalom the commander of the great army die hanging by his hair in a tree. But God's commandments have no end; they are a treasure in which, whenever one reads it, one finds new meanings and thoughts, and not only in the days of David but even today: empires fall and every power in the world collapses, but the word of God is rich, and no one can comprehend all its depths. And all the perfections of the world, that is, the material things that David sees as complete and perfect, are also limited, whereas the word of God is broad and has no limits, because it is connected to His divine, unlimited person.

2- The word of God, His knowledge and His mind is the Son incarnate in the fullness of time, Christ our God, and He is unlimited, whereas all the words of the world and everything great have limits, and Christ our God is above every power in the world and endures for ever.

When you read the Holy Bible every day, ask God to reveal His secrets to you, so that you understand new meanings that satisfy your soul, that you may live by them, and so you hear the voice of God as a personal message to you every day. May you memorize the verse that pleased you in order to repeat it always.
The thirteenth section (Mem): The sweetness of the word of God (vv. 97-104). The aim:
When David realized the steadfastness of the word of God, its loftiness and its breadth, he loved it very much and learned it and held fast to it, so that he hated all evil and falsehood.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (O how love I thy law! it is my meditation all the day.

1- David tasted the sweetness of the word of God and loved it very much, so that he repeated it all day, indeed all his life, and his love for it increased, and he kept it, that is, applied it in his life, and experienced new depths in it, and enjoyed it with an enjoyment that cannot be expressed.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Thou through thy commandments hast made me wiser than mine enemies: for they are ever with me.

1- Since David held fast to the word of God, he acquired more understanding and knowledge than his enemies the demons, so he was able to discover their devices and keep away from them, and his holding fast to the word of God increased, and he felt that it is his, that is, his life, indeed he also belongs to it, so he lived by it and its influence on him increased.

2- This verse is a prophecy about the Christians, for every believer in the New Testament can understand and know God more than the Jews who crucified Christ and persecuted the Apostles and the Christians, because the believer in the New Testament receives by the Holy Spirit an understanding of the commandment deeper and more perfect than the Jews.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (I have more understanding than all my teachers: for thy testimonies are my meditation. I understand more than the ancients, because I keep thy precepts.
I understand: I comprehend

1- David learned from teachers and benefited from the elders, but at the same time he was attached to the word of God, kept it and tried to live by it, and he used to repeat it and enjoy meditating on it, so God gave him additional understanding and wisdom, until he understood more than those from whom he learned and than the elders; that is, God gave him in his youth the wisdom of the elders, because he clung to the word of God.

2- David met teachers and elders who knew a great deal of information about the world, and who were not teachers of the Law and the word of God, and he benefited from them, but he learned more, and received great wisdom, from keeping, studying and meditating on the word of God.

3- These two verses apply to Christ, who understood more than the teachers and elders of the Jews; because He is the Word of God and the source of wisdom from eternity, and it is His meditation, and He of course keeps it because He Himself is the Word of God, and the wisdom of Christ appeared when He sat in the Temple among the teachers and all who heard Him were astonished at His wisdom (Lk 2:46, 47).

4- The believers in the New Testament, when they knew Christ the Word of God and kept His word, meditated on it and received more wisdom than all the teachers of the Jews and the elders from whom they learned. For the teachings of Christ are of course the perfect teachings, whereas the teachings of the teachers and elders of the Jews were about the Law, which is a type of Christ and leads to Him. The Apostles were younger than the elders of the Jews in the knowledge of God, but the Holy Spirit granted them wisdom and understanding of the word of God more than the elders of the Jews.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (I have refrained my feet from every evil way, that I might keep thy word. I have not departed from thy judgments: for thou hast taught me.

1- David's attachment to the word of God helped him to keep away from evil, and he even loved the word of God to the point that he was concerned to keep it, not only in his mind but to live by it. And however much Satan tried to draw him away from God's commandments, he did not leave them or depart from them; because God taught him through the commandment that it is life, and there is no life without it.

2- In these two verses the importance of spiritual striving appears in David's keeping his feet from walking in evil and not turning aside from the way of God's commandments, and grace granted him this spiritual inclination, and even taught him to live by it.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (How sweet are thy words unto my taste! yea, sweeter than honey to my mouth!

1- After David kept away from the ways of evil and was occupied with the word of God, he discovered its sweetness in his mouth, sweeter than every sweetness in the world, which he expressed by honey; that is, he tasted new depths of the sweetness of God's word, so his holding fast to it increased. Thus David shows that the word of God is spiritual food that satisfies the soul, just as bodily food satisfies the body.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Through thy precepts I get understanding: therefore I hate every false way.

1- By continually tasting the sweetness of God's word David acquired the wisdom of "understanding" which made him keep away from everything; that is, deepening in the understanding of the word of God automatically keeps a person away from the ways of evil, and the reverse is true: whoever is lax in keeping the word of God falls easily into evil. For the wisdom a person receives from keeping the word of God surpasses all knowledge, or experience, or intelligence in the world.

Do not be content with reading the Holy Bible every day, but may you meditate on the word of God and pray, until God reveals to you the sweetness of His word, so that you are satisfied by it, and the word of God turns into a new life whose sweetness you feel, and its loftiness above the works of the world.
The fourteenth section (Nun): Spiritual enlightenment (vv. 105-112). The aim:

After enjoying the sweetness of the word of God, David experienced spiritual enlightenment through the word of God, so he held fast to it and pledged to live by it, and it became the gladness of his heart and rescued him from the snares of the wicked.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.

1- David loved the word of God and tasted its sweetness, so his heart opened to it, and then God by His word lit for him the way of life, which is full of the snares of the demons and the darkness of sin, so he walked in it with wide strides and in peace, discerning good and rejecting evil.

2- Christ the Word of God is the light of the world who lights the way for us, indeed He is the way in which we walk with assurance, holding fast to His commandments and rejoicing in fellowship with Him, so we never go astray.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (I have sworn, and I will perform it, that I will keep thy righteous judgments.
Perform it: fulfill what I pledged

1- Swearing by the name of God was permitted in the Old Testament so that the believers would be established in God and would not swear by strange gods, and therefore David swore here and pledged to keep God's word in order to live by it, and so walk in the way of righteousness; because there is no way to righteousness and goodness except by keeping the word of God. And it is good for David and for every believer in the New Testament to renew his vows to God every day to keep His word and walk in righteousness through the words of the Holy Bible, even if he repeats one verse throughout the day.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (I am afflicted very much: quicken me, O LORD, according unto thy word.

1- David expresses the afflictions he passed through, which drove him to abase himself in humility, asking the help of God, who is able to bring him out of the affliction that almost kills him, by the life He grants him through His word.
2- David's self-abasement expresses his repentance before God for his sins, asking forgiveness and the new life that he receives according to God's promises and His life-giving word.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (My soul is continually in my hand: yet do I not forget thy law.

1- David was exposed to death several times at the hands of Saul and Absalom, so he expected death at any moment, and therefore he surrendered his life to God, and said, "My soul is continually in my hand." Despair did not fight him, but on the contrary he lived for God, and clung to His commandments and never forgot them, so he is a wonderful example of positiveness in the midst of afflictions, that is, the afflictions drove him to cling to God and His commandments and to surrender his whole life to Him, so he experienced God's power and reliance on Him.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (The wicked have laid a snare for me: yet I erred not from thy precepts.

1- The demons and all the wicked who follow them try to make the righteous fall in plots and snares, but as long as the righteous hold fast to God's commandments, these light their way so that they do not fall into these snares, and guide them in everything, so their holding fast to the commandment increases and they do not stray from it.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Thy testimonies have I taken as an heritage for ever: for they are the rejoicing of my heart. I have inclined mine heart to perform thy statutes alway, even unto the end.
Inclined my heart: directed it and made my heart lean

1- If the Jews held fast to the inheritance of the land of Canaan because it is from God, David felt all the more that his true inheritance is the testimonies of God and His commandments, for it is by them that he lives all his life, and he will continue to meditate on them for ever, especially as they give him a joy that remains with him for ever. For this reason he clung to the commandment, and it drew his heart to it, so he inclined to carry it out all his life, and his eyes were on the Kingdom, as the Septuagint translation says, "because of the reward". And he cared for God's statutes, that is, His worship, all his life.

When you fall into sin, or are perplexed about some matter, hasten to read the Holy Bible, that it may light the way for you and lead you to repentance and the doing of righteousness, and even define and guide you in all your steps.
The fifteenth section (Samekh): God's support (vv. 131-201). The aim:
After David experienced spiritual enlightenment through God's commandments, he asked for His support, that he might keep away from the wicked, hold fast to His worship, and live in His fear.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (I hate vain thoughts: but thy law do I love.

1- David was troubled by those who waver between good and evil, and hated their evils, and his love for God's commandments increased. And the more he loved God's commandments, the more he was troubled by, and distanced from, evil and all who do it, so as not to share with them in their deeds, and he distanced himself from the agitation in which they live; because he had tasted the stability and peace that he receives through keeping God's commandments.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: Thou art my hiding place and my shield: I hope in thy word. Depart from me, ye evildoers: for I will keep the commandments of my God.

Shield: the shield is the large buckler. And the buckler is a defensive implement consisting of a piece of wood with a loop at the back into which the soldier puts his hand and moves it in front of his face and body to protect himself from the arrows of the enemies

1- Before the wavering wicked around him David feels that their conduct and thoughts hinder him from God, so he flees from them by prayer, where he hides in God and takes refuge in Him, and in his prayer he waits for the word of God, which satisfies him and protects him and covers him. And when the wicked go away from him he has a quiet opportunity to keep God's commandments, meditate on them, and enjoy repeating them.
2- He asks God to take the wicked away from him, that is, his evil thoughts, and he hides and takes refuge by repeating the word of God and delighting in meditating on it

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Uphold me according unto thy word, that I may live: and let me not be ashamed of my hope. Hold thou me up, and I shall be safe: and I will have respect unto thy statutes continually.
Uphold me: help me and assist me

1- David feels that evil thoughts and the conduct of the wicked almost kill him, but his hope is in God's help according to His promise to him, so that he lives. And by God's support of him he receives salvation, and expresses his love of righteousness in holding fast to holy worship.

2- Here the work of grace supporting striving appears, for David relies on God's grace which drives him in his spiritual striving, and he is also encouraged by his looking to eternity, that is, the new life, where he receives complete salvation.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Thou hast trodden down all them that err from thy statutes: for their deceit is falsehood. Thou puttest away all the wicked of the earth like dross: therefore I love thy testimonies.
Dross: the impurities that the craftsman separates from metals

1- In order to live with God, David despised the thoughts and conduct of those who err from God, who went astray because of their holding to evil, vain thoughts, and supposed that they give happiness, although they are all passing material things.

He does not despise the erring in themselves, but he despises the error and the evil thought, and regards the conduct of the wicked as dross, that is, worthless impurities, so he keeps away from them and clings to the word of God.
And so he keeps away from evil company, lest it corrupt his life (1 Cor 15:33)

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (My flesh trembleth for fear of thee; and I am afraid of thy judgments.
I am afraid: I fear

1- When David saw the wicked and the evils surrounding him, he remembered God's judgment, so his body shuddered and he was terrified, and he remembered that God would judge him by His word if he mixed with the wicked, and therefore he fled from every evil and held fast to God's judgments, which give him peace and tranquility.

Examine yourself at the end of every day, and remember God's works and care throughout your day in order to thank Him. On the other hand, remember your sins that you committed before the awesome and just God, that you may repent of them, ask His mercies, and promise Him to live a pure life with His help.
The sixteenth section (Ayin): Steadfastness and keeping the commandment (vv. 121-128). The aim:

After the righteous man has experienced God's support, he asks Him to protect him from the wicked, have mercy on him and make His word known to him, that he may love it and live by it in the upright way.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (I have done judgment and justice: leave me not to mine oppressors.

1- David the king walked in the way of God, and established justice in his kingdom and in his judgments, out of his fear of God, as the previous section ended. And he entreats God here to protect him, and not to leave the wicked oppressors to harm him and wrong him, but that God treat him with justice, because God is just and merciful.

2- David here is not boasting when he says "I have done justice", but he implores the just God, who understands him, to protect him from the oppressors, especially since he tried to apply God's commandments and justice, so he asks for God's mercies.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Be surety for thy servant for good: let not the proud oppress me.

1- David asks God in humility to include him in His care, so that He guarantees him good by His mercy, lest the demons and their followers, the wicked oppressors, wrong him. He feels his weakness before the power of the wicked and has no guarantee except God's protection.
2- This verse is a prophecy about Christ the Redeemer who offers us salvation and guarantees us good, and delivers us from the hands of the proud demons.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Mine eyes fail for thy salvation, and for the word of thy righteousness.
Fail: grow weary

1- David awaits God's salvation and lifts up constant prayers, and his eyes even pour out many tears, until his eyes fail, but he did not despair, and remained waiting for the word of God that helps him to live in righteousness, for he longs for God and cannot live without His word.

2- David lifted his eyes in the spirit of prophecy, awaiting the salvation that Christ would accomplish in the fullness of time on the Cross, and he sees the righteous, holy Word redeeming mankind, and so He gladdens the hearts of all who awaited Him in the Old Testament, and likewise the believers in Him in the New Testament.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Deal with thy servant according unto thy mercy, and teach me thy statutes. I am thy servant; give me understanding, that I may know thy testimonies.

1- In humility David asks for God's care and tending of him according to God's mercy, and not according to his deserving; for he feels that he deserves nothing because of his many sins. And he longs to receive spiritual understanding, so as to hold fast to the worship of God, which is His statutes, and likewise His testimonies, which are His word.

2- In proportion as a person asks God to give him understanding, God's mercies and wisdom are poured out upon him. For God gives to His children according to their sense of need of Him, their faith in Him, and their love for Him shown in many prayers.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (It is time for thee, LORD, to work: for they have made void thy law.

1- David felt that people had turned away from God's law and His Law, as they plunged into many sins. So he was jealous with the zeal of God, and felt that he must work with all speed and power to proclaim the name of God and bring souls back to Him, that is, the necessity of service and of preaching the name of God, to bring His children back to Him.

2- David says this verse in the spirit of prophecy about Christ, that is, Christ says in the fullness of time that it is a time to work for the Lord, that is, to offer Himself on the Cross after He preached and performed many miracles, to draw the distant souls that had forsaken God's law.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Therefore I love thy commandments above gold; yea, above fine gold. Therefore I esteem all thy precepts concerning all things to be right; and I hate every false way.
Fine gold: pure gold

1- David loved God's commandments, so he acted by them, and they made his life upright and kept him away from the ways of falsehood and evil. So he hated the evil, crooked ways, and each day he grew in holding fast to God's commandments because they are upright, and they raise up and correct his life whenever he lives by them.

2- When David loved God's commandments this helped him to apply them, especially as he loved them more than gold, from which the most precious idols are made. For the worship of God is above all worships and gods. And also God's commandments are better than all the lusts and material things of the world, even the precious among them, such as gold.

Today is an acceptable day and the hour is an hour of salvation, so may you rise to live in God's commandments, to experience them and enjoy them, and then you will be able to teach them to those around you, because they have departed from God and His word and plunged into the lusts of the world, and are in great need to see a living picture of God's children who live by His word.
The seventeenth section (Pe): Wonderful effects (vv. 129-136). The aim:

Steadfastness in the word of God drove the righteous man to enter into the depths of the commandment, so he discovered its various effects in enlightenment, keeping away from sin, keeping the commandment, and grief over sinners

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Thy testimonies are wonderful: therefore doth my soul keep them.

1- David feels that God's words are wonderful, because they revolve around one idea despite the different times of their writing, and this idea is Christ the Savior, wonderful in His works, as Isaiah mentioned (Isa 9:6). And whenever we read them and meditate on them we find new depths; because God is unlimited and the depths of His word have no end.

2- God's testimonies are also His works in all creation, which speak of His glory, and meditating on them shows us the greatness of God and His love. Therefore David kept them, not in his thought only but in his soul, that is, with his thought and feelings, so they lived within him and influenced his works and all his life.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (The entrance of thy words giveth light; it giveth understanding unto the simple.

1- David felt that he was a beginner in his knowledge of the word of God. And that he opened his mind to understand the word of God, and was enlightened by it. And he saw in the spirit of prophecy that Christ, who is the Word of God, would come in the fullness of time and give salvation to mankind, and so would reveal new depths of the word of God, and the divine revelations about the word of God increase in eternity. And whenever a person reads the word of God it gives him a blessing and a new understanding according to his need and his longing to know God.

2- Those who are enlightened are the simple, or the plain, or the children, that is, those who feel their ignorance and weakness, so God grants them His knowledge, whereas the proud know nothing, and live in superficiality and a philosophy that avails nothing, for they do not enter into the depths of the word of God or even understand it, but are prisoners of their minds, and not subject to God, that He may give them understanding.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (I opened my mouth, and panted: for I longed for thy commandments.
Opened: I opened. Panted: I put out my tongue from intense thirst and weariness.

1- In great humility David declares his thirst for the water of life, which is the word of God, saying, I have opened my mouth, and shown my thirst for the word of God and my need for the air I breathe, which is the Spirit of God; that is, the word of God is the water, the air and the life for which David longs. And he declares his inability to obtain it by himself; therefore he opens his mouth for God to give him.

2- This verse is declared by the priest on the day of his ordination, and he repeats it according to the Septuagint translation, "I opened my mouth and drew in the Spirit for myself", and he opens his mouth, and the Father the Patriarch, or the bishop, breathes into his mouth so that he may receive the Holy Spirit, and receive a special grace to practice the sacrament of the priesthood with all its responsibilities. So the priest declares his need of the Holy Spirit and the word of God, for which he longs like David.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Look thou upon me, and be merciful unto me, as thou usest to do unto those that love thy name.

1- David continues to declare his weakness and his need of God, and asks Him to look upon him; because the mere looking of God upon him gives him all blessings. This look is according to God's mercy and not according to David's deserving, and this confirms David's humility.

2- God has mercy on those who love His name, who are those who repent of their sins and walk in righteousness, and David declares his repentance and tries to walk in righteousness; therefore he entreats God to have mercy on him. And when he says "as thou usest to do unto those that love thy name" he does not mean that this is his right, and demand it from God as if he were God's creditor, but he means to express his need, as one who loves God, of His forgiveness and support, that he may live in righteousness and virtue.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Order my steps in thy word: and let not any iniquity have dominion over me.

1- David also asks God to establish him in reading His word, meditating on it, repeating it and turning it into conduct; because by this steadfastness evil does not have dominion over him, and even if a sin fights him, or he falls into it, he hastens to repentance to live by the word of God, that is, the word of God protects him from sin, and the more he is established in it, the higher he rises above evil.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Deliver me from the oppression of man: so will I keep thy precepts.

1- David asks God to redeem him and rescue him from the oppression of man, that is, those who are hostile to him and try to kill him, like Saul and his men, so that he can go to the house of God and draw near to Him, and this helps him to keep His commandments. In this he does not murmur against the affliction, but asks for a wider opportunity to keep God's commandments, and God is able within the affliction to give him peace, and strength to keep His commandments and not be hindered because of the affliction, or fall into various sins, but to be established in God's commandments.

2- David looked in the spirit of prophecy and saw Christ the Savior and Redeemer, who is able to deliver him from the oppression of the wicked behind whom the devil hides, that is, to deliver him from the oppressing demons, and this gives him an opportunity to keep God's commandments.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Make thy face to shine upon thy servant; and teach me thy statutes.
1- David entreats God to make His face shine upon him, that is, to look upon him, and God is the source of light, so David is enlightened, and then he learns His judgments from God.

2- David declares that he is the servant of God, that is, His follower, and this confirms his humility, and his love of God, and that any enlightenment David receives is not from himself but from God. And then he cares for and tends those around him, giving them of what God has given him, that is, he gives this enlightenment and the teaching of the word of God in humility.
3- David longs for the face of God, that is, Christ incarnate in the fullness of time, who shines upon him and upon all the believers in the Old and New Testaments, so that all learn His judgments.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Rivers of waters run down mine eyes, because they keep not thy law.
Rivers of waters: plural of river, which is a small stream

1- When David was enlightened by the face of God, his feeling was stirred for those far from God, who had not kept His commandments and had plunged into their evils, so he prayed for them and wept over them much. And he expresses the abundance of his weeping by the likeness that many waters ran from his eyes as if they were rivers of waters. By this he moves God's mercies upon himself, and upon those far away, that He may have mercy on them and draw them to Himself.

Look to God with many prayers, and then your heart will open to feel the suffering of those far from God, and you will pray for them every day in your prayer; and be confident that your prayer is very precious to Him, so He has compassion on the whole world, for the sake of your prayer, however weak you are.
The eighteenth section (Tsadi): Justice and truth (vv. 137-144). The aim:

After David experienced the depths of the word of God, the truth and justice in it also drew his heart, especially in the midst of people's wronging one another, so his heart was filled with zeal, and he loved the commandments while feeling his weakness and his need to learn His rights, and he endured afflictions, but remained holding fast to God's commandments.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Righteous art thou, O LORD, and upright are thy judgments. Thy testimonies that thou hast commanded are righteous and very faithful.

1- God is the righteous, holy One, and His word is upright, just and true. It is a light in the midst of the darkness of people's thoughts and their evil works, for the measure to which we return is the word of God, the source of justice, truth and judgment.

2- The wicked describe the word of God as hard and impossible to carry out, and even say that God's judgments are unjust because He permits the wrong that is spread in the world, whereas the word of God carries all the justice and truth in which alone man finds rest. Everyone who believes in God and repents of his sins is enlightened, and discovers that God is the source of justice and uprightness.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (My zeal hath consumed me, because mine enemies have forgotten thy words.

1- David loved the word of God and wished that all people would keep it and enjoy it. But he was greatly troubled because the wicked, his enemies, neglected the word of God and walked in evil. So his heart was filled with good zeal for these souls that are being lost and do not enjoy prayer in the house of God, and from the abundance of his ardor the spiritual zeal weighed upon him, until it almost consumed him; that is, he was deeply affected by the wicked turning away from the worship of God in His house.

2- Christ repeated this verse when He was in the Temple and saw the sellers and the people's preoccupation with buying and selling and their neglect of prayer, so He drove out the sellers and rebuked the people (Jn 2:17).

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Thy word is very pure: therefore thy servant loveth it.
Pure: free of impurities, that is, clean

1- The words of the wicked are vain and false, and they accuse God of injustice, but the truth that David declares is that God's word is pure; it is the only pure word in the world, indeed the source of purity.
2- David loved the pure word of God, which he keeps, and so his heart is purified. And when he writes the purity of the heart he is able to behold God and enjoy fellowship with Him.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (I am small and despised: yet do not I forget thy precepts.

1- David was the youngest of his brothers, so in humility he feels that he is small and despised, and therefore he held fast to God's commandments and did not forget them, and by this he became the greatest of the kings of Israel, with a heart like the heart of God. Humility makes a person hold fast to God's commandments.

2- This verse is a prophecy about the Gentiles who would believe in Christ, and feel that they are small and despised and their strength is in holding fast to God's commandments, and so they surpassed the Jews who refused to believe in Christ.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.
1- David testifies that God is just and that His word is the source of justice and is the truth itself. And therefore it is the reference of the believers in all their thoughts, speech and conduct.

2- Christ is the Word of God, that is, the Truth, and the source of justice, and He remains for ever shining with His light on those who believe in Him, so that they grow in the knowledge of the truth.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Trouble and anguish have taken hold on me: yet thy commandments are my delights.

1- In holding fast to God's commandments, David met afflictions and lusts because of the wicked around him and the hard circumstances of life. But his holding fast to God's commandments made him experience the delight of fellowship with God, so he forgot his sufferings and was in joy, and his holding fast to the word of God increased.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (The righteousness of thy testimonies is everlasting: give me understanding, and I shall live.

1- David concludes this section by declaring that God's testimonies and word are just, and firm for ever, that is, to eternity. They are the permanent source of justice, so he entreats God to give him understanding of them, that he may live with Him. For the life of the righteous is in the knowledge and understanding of the word of God, so they live with uprightness and purity in this world, and then in the age to come.

May you review your life in the light of the word of God that you read every day, for it is the source of justice and truth, and by this you discover the uprightness of your works and words, and correct every deviation, so you obtain God's pleasure, and He even grants you His knowledge every day.
The nineteenth section (Qoph): Longing for the word of God (vv. 145-152). The aim:
Because the word of God is justice and truth, the righteous man longed for it and kept it, and since he was nourished by it his prayers rose to God.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (I cried with my whole heart; hear me, O LORD: I will keep thy statutes. I cried unto thee;
save me, and I shall keep thy testimonies.
David loved prayer, so that it became very deep, as is shown by:
1- It turned into a cry, that is, he held fast to God intensely.
2- With the whole heart, and not only from the lips or the mind, but with all his feelings.
3- Prayer led him to hold fast to worship, that is, the statutes, and to keep them, so he enjoyed individual worship and communal worship.
4- Continuing in prayer and calling upon God.
5- Relying on God and asking salvation from Him alone, that He might rescue him from his afflictions.
6- Asking salvation from God that he might rise above every sin and earthly concern, and he did not ask material requests or passing lusts.
7- Keeping God's testimonies and word and holding fast to them.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (I prevented the dawning of the morning, and cried: I hoped in thy word. Mine eyes prevent the night watches, that I might meditate in thy word.
Night watches: plural of watch, which is a division of the night. The Jews divide the night into three watches of 4 hours each, while the Romans divide it into four divisions of three hours each.
1- David's longings for God increased, so that he rose from the morning to pray, waiting for God to make him know His word, that he might live by it.

2- David's longings for prayer continued to increase, so that he could not bear to sleep the whole night without praying, and before the night watchman announced the beginning of the watch David would wake, open his eyes and stand to pray, and repeat the word of God and murmur it. This shows the extent of David's attachment to prayer and the word of God by night and by day.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Hear my voice according unto thy lovingkindness: O LORD, quicken me according to thy judgment.

1- In his prayers David asks God to grant him life with Him, but according to God's will, mercy and judgments; David does not ask his own will or any requests, but surrenders his life to God in tranquility, as his heart is free for prayer and the praise of God.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (They draw nigh that follow after mischief: they are far from thy law.

1- David describes the wicked who persecute him and pursue him as drawing near to the followers of vice and evil; because the wicked who pursue him love evil and all who do it, and therefore by this conduct they go far from God's law; for what fellowship hath light with darkness? And the Septuagint translation clarifies the meaning of this verse, saying, "They draw nigh in iniquity who pursue me, and they are far from thy law."

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Thou art near, O LORD; and all thy commandments are truth.

1- Those who pursue David trouble him, while he is steadfast in God's commandments, and God encourages him by making him feel that He is near to him, so his heart is reassured and comforted, and he is sure that God's commandments are the truth, so his holding fast to them increases, and he is not disturbed by the wicked who pursue him. By this David experienced that the nearer he draws to God, the further he is from evil, whereas those who pursue him on the contrary draw near to evil and go far from God. David is enlightened and knows that God's commandments are truth, whereas those who pursue him have been occupied with evil, and lived in it, and it has become their life.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Concerning thy testimonies, I have known of old that thou hast founded them for ever.

1- David knew and was sure that the word of God was founded by Him of old, that is, from eternity; if God is eternal, His word is also eternal, and therefore firm until today and for ever, so David can rest his life on it, and live by it strong and stable.

2- The eternal word of God is Christ, who has existed from the beginning and who became incarnate in the fullness of time. He is the way, the truth and the life, and faith in Him gives steadfastness, strength and eternal life.

Know that God is very near to you; so do not be anxious if afflictions or sins surround you, but cry out to God and He will surely answer you and rescue you; indeed He will comfort your heart in the midst of the affliction as well.
The twentieth section (Resh): Life by the word of God (vv. 153-160). The aim:

After showing his longings to be with God, and God's drawing near to him to comfort him, David declared his need of God's wisdom and his grief over the wicked for their turning away from His commandments, and asked for life by the word of God, for it is truth and justice.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Consider mine affliction, and deliver me: for I do not forget thy law.

1- David met afflictions and pursuits from enemies so that he came to be in severe humiliation, but his faith in God did not waver, so he asked Him to rescue him. Self-abasement before God, and humility, is the shortest way to the heart of God to obtain His mercies.

2- David saw with the eye of prophecy Christ the Savior, and saw himself as a member of His body, so he resembles Christ the head of the body in His humility, as He endures sufferings to the Cross, and so he came forward in humility toward the Cross to receive the divine mercy.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Plead my cause, and deliver me: quicken me according to thy word.

1- David brings his cause to God the just Judge after human beings had judged evil against him. But he appeals and brings his cause to the supreme divine court, and asks God to free him and release him from the troubling of his enemies, holding to God's promise in His word to exalt and deliver the humble. And here he is, in humility and abasement, asking His mercy according to His promises.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Salvation is far from the wicked: for they seek not thy statutes.

1- Although God desires the salvation of all, and Christ the Savior died for the redemption of all sinners, some sinners refuse repentance and go far from God's commandments, and therefore feel that God is far from them, since they themselves have pushed Him away. And this of course stirs David's grief over them, because they will perish.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Great are thy tender mercies, O LORD: quicken me according to thy judgments.

1- If the sinners have refused repentance and the word of God, and therefore lost His mercies and His salvation, David, on the contrary, drew near to God to enjoy His many mercies and to live by His word. For in proportion as a person draws near to God and asks His mercies, he receives life in God and enjoys His life-giving word.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Many are my persecutors and mine enemies; yet do I not decline from thy testimonies.

1- The sinners were not content to go away from God, but because of their distance from Him they were filled with evil, so they wronged the righteous without cause, persecuted them and troubled them. But the righteous held fast to their deliverer, which is God's testimonies by which they lived, and did not deviate or turn aside from them.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (I beheld the transgressors, and was grieved; because they kept not thy word.
Grieved: I hated intensely

1- Since David held fast to the word of God, he was not disturbed by the persecutions of the wicked, and more than this he had compassion on them; because he hated their evil ways, and wished that they would repent and return to the word of God and keep it, and be saved. For the cause of their falling into evil and treachery is their going away from the word of God.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Consider how I love thy precepts: quicken me, O LORD, according to thy lovingkindness.

1- David comes with boldness to God and asks Him to look upon him, to see how David loved His commandments, as it appeared in his words and works. And with the boldness of sonship he asks God to grant him life by His mercy, and not by his deserving. He is humble and does not try to show his righteousness by holding fast to God's commandments, but out of his need he held fast to the commandments, asking the divine mercy and life with God.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Thy word is true from the beginning: and every one of thy righteous judgments endureth for ever.

1- David concludes this section by declaring that the true word of God has existed from the beginning, and is the head and beginning of everything because it is eternal, and to the age, that is, for ever, God's just judgments prevail and lead the world, and the believers enjoy them in the Kingdom. For the Word of God, that is, Christ, is the beginning and the end, and therefore holding fast to Christ the Savior and His life-giving word gives life and joy and the enjoyment of fellowship with God.

Read the word of God every day, for it is the measure by which you weigh all your thoughts, words and works, and by which you sort the right from the wrong among the thoughts of the world, so you walk in tranquility, peace and joy.
The twenty-first section (Shin): Peace and joy (vv. 161-168). The aim:

Life by the word of God drove David to hold fast to it, so it became the gladness of his heart, and he loved it very much, and so he enjoyed inner peace, hoped for God's salvation, and kept His testimonies and acted by them.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Princes have persecuted me without a cause: but my heart standeth in awe of thy word.
Standeth in awe: fears

1- By the princes David means Saul and his servants, who rose up against him, pursued him and tried to kill him without his having wronged them, or opposed them, or asked to take their place; on the contrary, he was subject to all orders, and helped in killing Goliath and fighting the enemy Philistines. So he is amazed at this persecution, especially since the ruler is expected to care for his people; how then does he turn into an enemy and persecutor?!

2- David did not fear the persecution of the princes; because he feared God and His word, and sought to carry out His law. And whoever fears God has his heart strengthened, so he fears no one whatever his position, since he trusts in God's protection and care, and rises above earthly lusts. And so all God's children in the Old and New Testaments did not fear, whether the prophets and men of God, or the Apostles, martyrs and all the saints.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (I rejoice at thy word, as one that findeth great spoil.

1- The fear of God made David hold fast to the word of God, and so he experienced its sweetness, and rejoiced greatly with a joy that he could express only by the comparison that he had obtained great spoil. The fear of God does not prevent a person's joy; on the contrary, it drives out the fear of people, begets joy, and attaches the heart to the divine love. But whoever neglects the fear of God cannot enjoy His love, nor rejoice in His word, as David himself said in the Psalms, "Let my heart rejoice to fear thy name", according to the Septuagint translation (Ps 86:11).

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (I hate and abhor lying: but thy law do I love.

1- The natural result of the fear of God is that a person loves His commandments, and if a person loves the word of God he hates sin and crookedness, such as lying, and this keeps him from falling into lying. And the farther a person keeps from evil, the more his love for the word of God grows. And likewise, the more he loves the word of God, the farther he keeps from evil.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.
Great: much and abundant

1- As a result of the fear of God and the love of His commandments, and many prayers and praises, a person finally receives the greatest grace, which is inner peace, and it is great on condition that the person keep away from stumbling at the word of God, meaning doubt, so he believes the word of God and is therefore able to live by it, and so he enjoys the peace that remains firm within him, whatever disturbances he meets from outside.

2- The love of the law does not only give a person inner peace, but also keeps him from stumbling blocks, that is, sins, since it occupies him with God and lifts him to heavenly things, so he keeps far from evil and does not stumble at it.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (LORD, I have hoped for thy salvation, and done thy commandments. My soul hath kept thy testimonies; and I love them exceedingly. I have kept thy precepts and thy testimonies: for all my ways are before thee.

1- Acting by God's commandments made David experience his love for God, so he hopes for His salvation, and a person cannot receive God's salvation and grace unless he strives and keeps His commandments, for grace works with the strivers who hold fast to God, supporting them, moving them and satisfying them.

2- If a person keeps God's commandments he loves them by meditating on them. And if he loves them and his heart is attached to them he is moved to carry them out, and so experiences new depths in them.

3- David hopes for God's salvation which rescues him from his enemies and pursuers, but with the eye of prophecy he also hopes for the salvation of Christ in the fullness of time, and then he advances with longings toward heaven, hoping for complete salvation in eternity.

When you read the word of God each day, try to memorize one verse, or meditate on it, for this moves your feelings toward God, and you love His word, and so you become qualified to carry out His commandments, experience the work of His grace in you, and taste the sweetness of His word and of being with Him.
The twenty-second section (Tau): Asking for salvation (vv. 169-176). The aim:

The peace and joy that David tasted drove him to prayer, relying on God's promise, who wants to draw His children near to Him. So he asked to be before God, praising Him and singing to Him, and asking for His salvation and life with Him, and that He not leave him to go astray because of his sins, because he loves His commandments.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Let my cry come near before thee, O LORD: give me understanding according to thy word. Let my supplication come before thee: deliver me according to thy word.

1- In this last section of the psalm David draws near to God, because he loved Him and loved His commandments very much. But when he drew near he felt his unworthiness of this nearness; yet he loved God, so he entreated Him that his cry might reach Him and come near, and that his requests might also come before Him, as he felt his weakness and his sins, which hinder him from appearing in the presence of God.

2- He asked God to make him understand how to stand before Him, and to grant him the new life in Him, and deliver him from his sins and from everything surrounding him; because he is in great joy at being in the presence of God, and never wants to leave Him.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (My lips shall utter praise, when thou hast taught me thy statutes. My tongue shall speak of thy word: for all thy commandments are righteousness.

1- When David found himself near to God and in His presence, his lips overflowed with the praise of God like a spring from which much water flows. And because God taught him His statutes and His worship, in which he experienced fellowship with God, his praises and spiritual songs increased, as he rejoiced in the presence of God.
2- David is in joy because of the justice of God, who granted him to be with Him, and compensated him for the afflictions surrounding him with an enjoyment that cannot be expressed

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Let thine hand help me; for I have chosen thy precepts. I have longed for thy salvation, O LORD; and thy law is my delight.

1- David chose God's law to live by it, and this choice is the opposite of the choice of his enemies, who chose evil, and therefore he asks God's help to carry out His commandments and be established in them however much the enemies resist.

And when he experienced God's commandments and help he longed to be saved from his sins, the wars of the devil and the resistance of enemies, to be free for the word of God and delight in meditating on it. For this is David's true life, in being with God and enjoying His commandments.

2- The hand of God that David asks for his help is a prophecy about Christ the Redeemer, and he longs for His salvation that He would accomplish on the Cross in the fullness of time, so that He grants him and all the believers the delight of being in Paradise with Him. David's heart was drawn to God, so he crossed time and saw Christ, and even rose to Paradise and the Kingdom.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Let my soul live, and it shall praise thee; and let thy judgments help me.

a- David's heart was attached to God and to the praise of His holy name, so he asked Him to grant him the spiritual life, that is, constant existence with Him, that he might continue in His praise by day and by night. He also asked God to help him by His judgments and commandments, so that he would not fall into sin, or concern about this world, or be occupied in any way away from God; because life had become, in David's view, being in constant prayer and praise with Him, indeed he longs for constant praise in the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek thy servant; for I do not forget thy commandments.
Sheep: a beast, but what is meant here is a lamb.

1- After David rose very high and enjoyed, he did not forget his weakness, his unworthiness, his exposure to falling into any sin, and he remembered his previous sins, so he called on God his helper and said to Him, "I have gone astray by my sins like a sheep, and I have no helper but You, O Lord, and I cannot return to You because of my weakness, so seek me Yourself and rescue me, and I have no boldness before You except that I loved Your commandments, and repeat them, and strive to live by them. Despite my weakness and my sins I love You, and I love Your commandments, and I wish to remain in Your presence, praising You all the days of my life and for ever."

How beautiful it is to be with God, so do not deprive yourself of meditation and praise every day. Give enough time to prayer, that you may taste the sweetness of fellowship with God, and rise to heaven while you are on earth, and your heart be attached to eternity so that you live for it.
Songs of Ascents
1- They are the psalms from (Ps 120 to Ps 134), which are fifteen psalms
2- Their writer:
a- Four of them are attributed to David, which are (Ps 122, 124, 131, 133).
b- One of them is attributed to Solomon, which is (Ps 127).
c- The rest of these psalms, ten, have unknown writers.
3- When are they said?

a- When the children of Israel went up to Jerusalem, which is built on five hills, or mountains, and they used to go up to Jerusalem to worship in its Temple, especially at the three great feasts, at which every male of the children of Israel had to appear before the Lord in His Temple, which are the feasts of Passover, Pentecost (the Fifty) and Tabernacles.
b- Those returning from the captivity repeated them, declaring their joy at returning to the Temple and its rebuilding.

c- The Levites repeat them as they go up the ascending steps from the outer court to the inner court, which number seven, then those going up from the inner court to the house of the Lord, which number eight, and they would stand on each step and say a psalm of the fifteen Psalms of Ascents, and perhaps they remembered the angels ascending on Jacob's ladder in his wonderful dream, and also the fifteen years that God gave to Hezekiah, by which He lengthened his life.

d- The priests repeat them as they go up from the Holy Place to the Holy of Holies, that is, from the house to the sanctuary, and the number of these steps is fifteen, so the priests would stand on each step and repeat a psalm of the Psalms of Ascents.
Songs of Ascents
4- Their meanings:

a- They include different meanings and have many spiritual purposes suitable for worshipers who pray and love God. A spiritual meaning and purpose can be set for each psalm suitable for the one ascending from earth to heaven, or from the world to the house of the Lord to enjoy being in His presence. And here is one of these meanings:
(Ps 120:) "In my distress I cried unto the LORD"... It represents the cry of a person who suffers on earth, but has hope in heaven. (Ps 121:) "I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills"...
Meditation on the loftiness of God, His help, and His work in His children.
(Ps 122:) "I was glad when they said unto me"...
Joy in going up to the house of the Lord, which is a pledge of the heavenly Jerusalem.
(Ps 123:) "Unto thee lift I up mine eyes... as the eyes of servants"...
The humility of the one ascending and his feeling that he is a servant before his master.
(Ps 124:) "If it had not been the LORD who was on our side" Trust in God who supports us in our ascent.

(Ps 125:) "They that trust in the LORD shall be as mount Zion" Reliance on the Lord. (Ps 126:) "When the LORD turned again the captivity of Zion, we became like those who are comforted" Divine comforts in the midst of the sufferings of the ascent:
(Ps 127:) "Except the LORD build the house" The Lord builds our new house, that is, our new nature in Baptism:
(Ps 128:) "Blessed is every one that feareth the LORD" The Lord's blessings for those who trust in Him:

(Ps 129:) "Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth" The sufferings of the ascent, in which one experiences the victory of the Lord, for the one who bears the Cross experiences the Resurrection: (Ps 130:) "Out of the depths have I cried unto thee, O LORD" The cry of the sinner with hope in God:
(Ps 131:) "LORD, my heart is not haughty" Humility is the way of ascent:
(Ps 132:) "LORD, remember David, and all his afflictions."
The Lord dwells in the heart, and so a person finds his rest:
(Ps 133:) "Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!"
Fellowship among the believers encourages those who ascend:
(Ps 134:) "Behold, bless ye the LORD" The praise of those ascending, as they are filled with the Holy Spirit and have reached God:
b- The fifteen psalms can be divided into five units in their meanings, each unit containing three psalms, and these units are:
(Ps 120-122:) The need for the Lord the Savior.
(Ps 123-125:) Faith and reliance on the merciful Lord.
(Ps 129-131:) Endurance, repentance and humility are the marks of those who ascend.
Songs of Ascents (Ps 132-134:) The praise of God who dwells among His children.

5- The prayers of the Agpeya: All the Psalms of Ascents are found in the prayers of the Agpeya; they are prayed in the Agpeya in the Vespers and Compline prayers, in addition to their repetition in the Veil prayer and the Midnight prayer. Why do you pray them at these times?

a- The Vespers prayer: It includes the first ten Psalms of Ascents, which are (Ps 120-129), and they tell us of the hope in God of those of the eleventh hour, to whom we ascend in humility, faith and reliance, that He may gladden our hearts and comfort us in the midst of the sufferings of life.

b- The Compline prayer: It includes the remaining five Psalms of Ascents, which are (Ps 130-134), and they tell us of the repentance of the sinner before his day ends and he meets God, so he comes forward in humility asking God to dwell in his heart and in the midst of His Church, to lift hearts to praise.

c- The Veil prayer: It includes (the two psalms (Ps 121, Ps 129) of the Vespers prayer, and the five Psalms of Ascents found in the Compline prayer. So when the veil of night comes upon us the one who prays lifts his heart to God, after enduring the sufferings of the day, and comes forward in repentance and longing to be with God in the quiet of the night.
d- The Midnight prayer: It includes all the Psalms of Ascents, for at midnight a person rises in prayer above earthly things, and turns to heavenly things in humility, repentance and longing for God.
6- Their characteristics:
a- All the Psalms of Ascents are short, to suit the one who prays as he ascends from one step to another, so he can concentrate on them and grasp their meanings.
b- The words of these psalms touch a person's feelings, because he is ascending and his heart is attached to the house of God and to being with Him.
c- There are relations between the meanings of these psalms that can be understood from the fourth item of this introduction.
The Helper in afflictions - a song of ascents. Introduction:
1- Its writer: The title of this psalm does not mention the name of the writer, so it is one of the orphan psalms whose writer is unknown.

2- This psalm shows that the writer suffers from the deceit and hypocrisy of those around him and much false speech, so that he felt his exile in their midst. He represents the cry of a righteous man who wants to live with God in a world full of evil.
3- You sense in this psalm tranquility and faith in the heart of its writer and a wonderful peace, and this confirms his strong relationship with God.
4- This psalm suits every person who passes through affliction or is exposed to problems from those around him.

5- This psalm is considered one of the Messianic psalms; because it expresses the psychological sufferings to which Christ was exposed from the Jews who persecuted Him, deceived Him and tried to catch Him in a word, hiding behind false words of praise (v. 2).

6- This psalm is found in the prayers of the Agpeya in the Vespers and Midnight prayers, for it expresses the sufferings that the spiritual person endured throughout the day, and he casts them before God in reliance on Him, to regain his peace.
Deliverance from the hypocrites (vv. 1-4):

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: 1- The psalmist suffers severe distress, so that he cried out to God, and what he offered was not merely an ordinary prayer or petition, but he enjoys great faith, so that he believed that God had answered him even though the answer had not yet appeared. Yet he trusts in God's answer, which gave him inner peace, because he relies on a previous spiritual experience with God, who rescued him from many sufferings.

2- This verse is a prophecy about Christ in the midst of His sufferings and His endurance of the Cross, for He trusts that His prayer will be answered, whether in the Garden of Gethsemane or on the Cross, and that He will redeem mankind and rise from the dead, proclaiming His victory over sin for our sake.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: 1- The psalmist marvels at the man with the deceitful, lying tongue, for what does he gain from this evil and hypocrisy, and from his persistence in this deceit, which must lead him to eternal destruction? By the one with the deceitful tongue is meant Satan, and every wicked person who follows Satan. The torment that awaits the liar is not only at the end of his life, but also deceit and trickery torment their possessor, for he feels a division and duplicity within himself, so that he is troubled and has no peace; and even if the deceiver thinks that by his lying he obtains some of the material things of the world, these are passing away.

2- At the beginning of the spiritual path, when a person tries to ascend to God, for this is the first of the psalms of ascents, that is, the first step on the way of spiritual striving, when a person decides to live with God, the demons gather around him with their deceptions. They praise him and entice him with lusts, hoping that he will fall into pride or defilement, and so be hindered from ascending to God.
3- These verses are also a prophecy about Christ and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Him with a deceitful kiss, and in hypocrisy showed himself as a friend of Christ.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Juniper: a kind of wormwood tree found in deserts such as the desert of the Arabian Peninsula, called the "ar'ar", from which charcoal is made, distinguished by its intense heat and the long time it stays alight.

1- The psalmist likens the wicked deceivers to sharp arrows of a mighty man, with which they wish to kill those who offend them, and he also likens them to a fire blazing fiercely to burn those around them; but the righteous, the children of God, take refuge in Him, so the offenses of these wicked people do not reach them.
2- The wicked liars will receive severe torment, which he likens to sharp, strong arrows and a fiercely burning fire, so that their torment will be very painful.

3- On the other hand, St. Augustine sees that the sharp arrows are the arrows of the word of God that prick the wicked and lead them to repentance, and the coals of juniper are the fire of the Holy Spirit, which burns their sins away through repentance and kindles their love toward God.

Do not be affected by the deceit and trickery that surround you in the world, but take refuge in God through prayer, that He may establish you in His commandments, so that you are not swept along with the current of evil, and are not disturbed by the deceit of the wicked, but live in peace through the strength of your faith.
The alienation of the worker (vv. 5-7):

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: (Mesech: they are the descendants of Japheth the son of Noah (Gen 10:2), tribes who dwelt to the north-east of the land of the Jews and worked in trade; they represent the people of the world who are far from God and preoccupied with material things. Kedar: the second son of Ishmael, tribes who roamed the Arabian Peninsula and were distinguished by violence and fierceness, and who lived in tents made of black goat skin, so their tents are a symbol of darkness and evil.

1- The psalmist declares his distress at dwelling, not among the tribes of Mesech or the tribes of Kedar, but among wicked people who resemble the tribes of Mesech, far from God, or the tribes of Kedar, full of evil and violence. Therefore he felt his estrangement from those around him, and sought God's help to reassure him and surround him with His love.

2- The spiritual person who walks by God's commandments feels like a stranger in the midst of the world, because of the conduct of those around him in evil, deceit and lying, so he asks God's help to deliver him from this distress of soul, to support him with His love, and to restore his peace to him.

entries.section: (4) Celebrating salvation in the house of the Lord

paragraphs.text: 1- Although the psalmist feels estranged among the wicked people of the world, who are occupied with deceit and lying, he held fast to God and His commandments, and God granted him an unshakable peace.

2- He held fast to peace and love, so they could not bear his words, and insisted on making war with others, and with him too. Yet he was not troubled, because God protects him and establishes him in peace and love toward them and toward all people.

3- This verse is a prophecy about Christ, who is the God of peace, and who endured His opponents and enemies who tried to trap Him in a word, and reviled Him, and tried to kill Him, but He remained loving them and died for their sake.

Be firm in your faith in God, and ask His help to live in peace however much the wicked provoke you. Do not act with violence and harshness in response to their offenses, and be confident that your love extinguishes the flame of evil and remains a light for the world.
The Lord is the Helper and the Keeper. A song of ascents: "I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help" (v. 1). Introduction:
1- Its author: the title of the psalm gives no name for its author, so it is one of the orphan psalms whose author is not known.
2- This psalm was recited on the second step, after the preceding psalm, during the ascent, for it is one of the songs of ascents, as the title states.

3- After the preceding psalm showed the estrangement of the spiritual person who seeks God, this psalm shows God who helps His children and keeps them in all their steps. It is therefore suitable for everyone in distress, or who expects distress to come upon him, so that his faith in God may be established.

4- This is a liturgical psalm; those going up used to chant it antiphonally among the groups ascending: one group chants (vv. 1, 2), then another group chants (vv. 3, 4), and after this they chant vv. 5-8.

5- This psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayer of Vespers, where the worshiper lifts his eyes to God before the sun of his life sets, asking His help and His keeping in the remaining hours before he sleeps, not only on this night, but for the rest of the days of his life.
I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.

1- The one going up to Jerusalem and its temple would lift his eyes to the mountain that rises toward heaven, where dwells God who is able to help a person in all his steps, so that he is strengthened and endures the pains and weariness of the ascent.

2- The mountain is a symbol of the saints who rise with their lives to heaven; they are an example for us through their lives, that we may imitate them, and so find God's help in our lives as they did.
3- The mountain is a symbol of Christ the Mighty and Powerful, who came down from heaven to lift us up on high through faith in Him, and through His help.
My help cometh from the Lord, which made heaven and earth.

1- The psalmist feels that his help comes from the Lord, the Creator of heaven and earth, in whose hand is everything, and it is not right to look to anyone but Him, because He is the Almighty. A person's help is from God, and even if He allows someone to help a person, it is God who works through him.

2- When the children of Israel sinned, and worshiped idols, and drew far from God, and were preoccupied with lusts, they entered the distress of captivity; and when they returned to God, He brought them back from captivity, because God alone is the Helper.

The more you lift up your eyes to heaven and trust in God, the more you gradually rise above earthly lusts and the cares of this world, and then you receive inner peace, in addition to abundant blessings.
He will not suffer your foot to be moved: he that keeps you will not slumber. Behold, he that keeps Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep.

1- God keeps you so that you do not slip, and what is meant by slipping is falling and persisting in the fall, that is, not repenting. This comes from pride, or its opposite, smallness of soul, which leads to despair.

But as for the one who repents, however much he slips and falls, the compassionate God receives him. The one who believes in God and trusts in Him does not remain in slipping or despair, because he looks to the Lord his keeper, who rescues him however much he falls.

2- The Lord differs from all people in that He neither slumbers nor sleeps, whereas all people, however great their strength or their love for you, are weak; they slumber and are heedless of you, and cannot keep you. Therefore it is folly to depend on them, but the Lord is the keeper of Israel, that is, the keeper of His people; He alone is able to keep you.
The Lord is your keeper: the Lord is your shade upon your right hand.

1- The Lord shades a person during afflictions and helps him in them; these are symbolized by the scorching rays of the sun. And He shades the striving person if he falls, to raise him up and let him repent. By this shade He shows tenderness to His children, as a hen has tenderness for her chicks, to encourage them in their spiritual striving.

2- He shades the right hand, which is a symbol of good works, namely the prayers lifted up before God, works of goodness, and every spiritual service; so He encourages His children in them and supports them against the schemes of the devil.
3- If the shadow of Peter healed the sick (Acts 5:15), how much more does the shadow of Christ heal and support in all spiritual and bodily sicknesses.
The sun shall not smite you by day, nor the moon by night.

1- God, who keeps His children, keeps them from the strokes of the sun, which symbolizes trials and the open wars of Satan; God supports His children and repels these attacks from them, so long as they hold fast to Him and seek His help.

2- The Lord also keeps His children from the strokes of the moon, for it is said that the light of the moon harms those who dwell in the deserts if they are not careful. The strokes of the moon are a symbol of the cunning, deceptive strokes of Satan, and of every sin committed in the dark for fear of the eyes of people. In sum, God protects His children night and day, and throughout their lives, because they have trusted in Him.
The Lord shall preserve you from all evil: he shall preserve your soul.

The Lord keeps His children from every evil, great or small, and keeps their souls in faith in Him, firm in His commandments; even if He does not remove the affliction, He gives them grace, and they experience Him deeply during the affliction. Indeed, His work shines forth with power if He allows the affliction to remain, as He kept the three youths inside the furnace: He did not quench it, but appeared to them and walked with them, and they praised Him.
The Lord shall preserve your going out and your coming in from this time forth, and even for evermore.
1- The Lord keeps your entering into the world and your going out from it, that is, He keeps you throughout your life.

And He keeps you also at your entering into the Church through Baptism, and keeps your going out to the Kingdom of Heaven. Likewise He keeps you in your going out from the lusts of the world and your entering into a deep relationship with God, which begins now and continues forever in heaven.
2- This verse is a prophecy about Christ in His entering into the world by the Incarnation and His going out by the Resurrection and the Ascension.

If the Lord keeps you in all the stages of your life, and throughout your lifetime, then be at ease and cast your care upon Him, that you may enjoy His care and be free to meditate on Him and to enjoy His fellowship.
Joy in Jerusalem, the house of the Lord. A song of ascents of David: "I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the Lord" (v. 1). Introduction:
1- Its author: the prophet David, as the title of this psalm states.
2- This psalm shows David's love, and his heart's attachment to the house of the Lord and to worship in it.
